News.title: ‘Flying chairs’ fairground ride crashes to the ground injuring seven kids in Venezuela
News.content:
SEVEN children have been injured at a fairground after a flying chair ride collapsed.

What began as an evening of fun in El Callao, Venezuela, ended in sheer terror for dozens of families.



Around 10.20pm on Saturday, the flying chairs collapsed mid-ride, injuring at least seven children.

Footage from the incident captures a chaotic scene of panic after the malfunction, showing desperate bystanders rushing to lift the wreckage to get to the children.



While the severity of the children’s injuries is not known at this stage, authorities have said they all were injured with “cuts and bruises”.

The stricken children were rushed to hospital.



According to preliminary reports, a failure in the rotating shaft or in the central metal base caused the structure to detach and violently projecting the children towards the ground.

Following the incident the park was immediately closed and an investigation was launched into the fault.



Experts will inspect the equipment to find out if the collapse was caused by poor maintenance, worn-out materials, or faulty assembly.

The investigation will determine if anyone is legally or even criminally responsible for the accident.

It comes following a string of malfunctioning ride incidents across the world.

In May a similar swing ride failed, sending five people into hospital – including two teens.

Spectators watched as the entire ride hit the hard floor and flung passengers onto the solid ground in India.



Emergency responders were dispatched to the scene and rushed the injured victims – one who was in a critical condition – to nearby hospitals.

In a similar incident in April, a fairground ride suddenly collapsed as crucial cables suddenly snapped.

The malfunction in southern Brazil left 11 people injured, including one person who suffered a fractured vertebra.

Dramatic video — taken by a passenger on the ride — captured the exact second the cables snap in the horror malfunction which left 11 people injured.

Spectators screamed as the entire ride hits the hard floor and flings passengers onto the solid ground.

News.title: Urgent ‘do not swim’ warning issued at popular UK beach after mystery substance turns water bright blue
News.content:
BLUE-DUNIT Urgent ‘do not swim’ warning issued at popular UK beach after mystery substance turns water bright blue

AN urgent “do not swim” warning has been issued at a popular beach after a mystery substance turned the water bright blue.

People have been encouraged to stay out of the water at Littleham Brook in Exmouth, Devon with pollution being blamed for the distinct colour.

The brook feeds into Exmouth beach, leading to the warning to bathers at the popular spot.



The Environment Agency (EA) has advised against bathing but added there was no “visible environmental impacts”.



On Saturday night, the source of the blue pollution was traced to an “industrial source”.

It has since stopped leaking into the river.

There was an earlier sewage spill this week near Exmouth’s bathing waters but the EA said the two incidents are not linked.



It’s thought the latest pollution started at just after 8.30pm on September 111.

The EA said it was waiting on a toxicity report on the substance and will lift the warning when it is safe to do so.

A spokesperson for the EA said on X: “A bright blue substance was reported in Littleham Brook, Exmouth.

“We attended and found no visible environmental impacts, but issued an advice against bathing as a precaution.



“Overnight it was traced to an industrial source, but it has stopped.

“It is not linked to the sewage network.

“The pollutant is still moving downstream and is likely to reach the bathing water this afternoon.

“We’re awaiting toxicity information, so the advice against bathing on Swimfo remains. We’ll review again later and lift it when safe.”

The EA explained the necessity to have the swim warning on its bathing quality map, saying: “Exmouth bathing water is affected by the catchment surrounding the Littleham Brook, which is approximately 600 hectares, and also by the enormous Exe Estuary catchment which is approximately 150,000 hectares.



“The Littleham Brook is four and a half kilometres long and flows southwest from Littleham Village through Green Farm and Maer Farm to Maer Bridge where it is piped under the beach to the sea at Maer Rocks.”

News.title: Fury as Home Office pays 9,000 Brazilians up to £3,000 to return home after overstaying their visas
News.content:
ALMOST 9,000 Brazilian migrants have each been paid up to £3,000 to leave Britain — yet most Channel arrivals ignore the “bribe” to go, The Sun can reveal.

Taxpayers have funded golden goodbyes for 8,901 from the South American country out of the 20,365 international total who went under the assisted returns scheme in two years.



Each of them was given travel and living expenses by the Voluntary Returns Service department for visa overstayers, failed asylum seekers or anyone without the right to remain.

The official bill from July 2024 to this March was £35million. But sources reckon the total now tops £40million owing to the cash splashed out in the past six months.



It puts the average payment to leave at £1,964, with the top £3,000 amount generally reserved only for families and vulnerable people.

Alongside the Brazilians, 3,629 Indians took a funded flight home, 746 Colombians and 468 Hondurans.



Yet the five biggest nations for small boat migrants barely featured in the figures.

Just seven Eritreans, 11 Sudanese, 14 Afghans, three Somalis and 77 Iranians agreed to accept a bung to go home.

Farewell payouts have soared under Labour, running at nearly four times the rate of the final two years under the Conservatives.

Chris Philp, the Shadow Home Secretary, said: “Labour are paying illegal immigrants to leave instead of stopping them arriving in the first place. They have found an expensive way to avoid the actual problem.



“Paying off thousands of Brazilians does nothing about the boats crossing the Channel.

“Meanwhile, the people arriving in dinghies are being returned at a rate of just seven per cent. The Conservative Party would end this racket altogether. Our Borders plan would ensure illegal immigrants could all be forcibly deported, meaning there would be no need to pay them off.”

The bill could soon rocket after Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood rolled out a pilot scheme offering failed asylum seekers and their families up to £40,000 to leave.

The one-time offer is valid for one week only. Those accepting will also be given flights home.

The cash is expected to be issued on pre-paid debit cards once they have left the country.



Home Office sources say assisted voluntary returns cost less than the £48,000 for a forced removal, and do not require border agents to accompany a migrant all the way home.

Ministers claim the payouts save taxpayers money as, for example, housing a migrant family of three in asylum accommodation costs about £158,000 a year.

The top £3,000 assisted voluntary return payment would fund three months for one migrant in a typical house of multiple occupation (HMO).



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Home Office said: “Encouraging voluntary returns is vastly better value than paying for hotels or forced returns, saving taxpayers millions. Under this government, returns of those with no right to be in the UK are up by more than 50 per cent, and close to 65 per cent for small boat arrivals.”

The assisted returns scheme is separate from the facilitated returns scheme which deports foreign criminals directly from jail.

News.title: Criminals freed from jail could have restrictions decided with help of AI under new government rules
News.content:
CRIMINALS freed from jail could have decisions over their restrictions supported by AI under new government guidance.

Probation officers will be allowed to use artificial intelligence to support “licence condition-related decision-making” when managing offenders in the community.



The rules state AI must “support, not replace, professional judgement” and any decisions must remain “explainable and defensible”.

The Ministry of Justice says the technology could be used for routine work such as summarising case information, transcription and note-taking, while frontline staff retain the final say.



But it comes as the probation service braces for thousands of lags being freed early as part of the Government’s bid to ease pressure on overcrowded jails.

Shadow Justice Secretary Nick Timothy warned:“Labour have been warned their early release scheme will overwhelm the probation service.



“We know Labour have abdicated responsibility for this chaos, but they must ensure AI will have no role in making decisions that affect the lives of victims.

“Using technology to speed up administration is fine, but the decisions on how dangerous offenders are managed in the community cannot just be automated.”

Licence conditions are used to protect the public and prevent reoffending, with extra restrictions imposed depending on the risks posed by an offender.

They can include curfews, exclusion zones, restriction zones and electronic monitoring.



Probation officers are already required to use a separate computer tool called EPF2 during pre-release planning, which suggests additional licence conditions for them to consider.

But the Ministry of Justice stressed that decisions over licence conditions will remain with trained probation staff.

A spokesman said: “Decisions on licence conditions will always be made by frontline staff.

“We’re looking at how we can use new tech to support Probation Officers on routine tasks – such as summarising information or note taking – so staff can spend more of their time monitoring offenders and keeping communities safe.”

News.title: Fury as BBC wastes over £65,000 of licence-payers’ cash on taxis, trains and hotels NEVER used
News.content:
THE BBC has wasted more than £65,000 of licence-payer’s cash on taxis, trains and hotel rooms that were never used.

Some 344 rail tickets, 870 cab journeys and 190 hotel bookings were paid for but aborted – with no refund able to be claimed – in the last three years.



Cancelled train trips cost £19,124, abandoned hotel reservations added another £31,155, while wasted taxi fares totaled £14,771, according to data released under Freedom of Information laws.

It means the Beeb has wasted £417 per week on transport and accommodation which nobody used.



Last year, each unused cab cost the broadcaster an average of £17.50, cancelled train tickets cost around £57 each, while the hotel bookings stood at £175 each.

The £65,050 total squandered is equivalent to around 361 TV licences.

Anne Strickland, researcher at the Taxpayers’ Alliance, said: “License fee payers will be appalled that the BBC has wasted tens of thousands of pounds on journeys and hotel rooms nobody even used.

“£65,000 may be small change to Broadcasting House, but it is still money taken from households through an outdated and hated TV tax.

“The licence fee should be scrapped, and the BBC forced to stand on its own two feet.”

The real figure is likely to be even higher, as the FOI Act does not cover expenses incurred by the BBC for its creative outputs, such as news, radio, or the arts.



The figures relate solely to policy and strategy, finance and operations, legal, HR and other central support teams.

In April, the BBC was forced to introduce immediate cost-control measures, including tightening up on all non-essential travel, in a bid to save £500 million over the next two years.

In an email to staff, interim director general Rhodri Talfan Davies said the broadcaster is facing “significant financial pressures”.

He added: “Put simply, the gap between our costs and our income is growing.

“This is being driven by a number of factors: production inflation remains very high; our license fee and commercial income is under pressure; and the global economy remains turbulent.”



The Beeb announced it will cut between 1,800 and 2,000 jobs – almost one in 10 – and impose tighter controls on recruitment, management consultancies and attendance at awards and events.

Several TV shows are also set to be axed as the broadcaster slashes content spending by £80 million.

Earlier this week, The Sun revealed that the beloved series RuPaul’s Drag Race is being cancelled after 11 series.

Other popular shows being terminated include Blankety Blank, Celebrity Mastermind, and Live At The Apollo.

News.title: Moment people jump from third-floor window as factory goes up in flames & six including 3 kids rushed to hospital
News.content:
THIS is the moment terrified people leapt from a third-floor window to escape a raging factory fire, as six including three kids are rushed to hospital.

Horrific footage shows a person dropping from the window and hurtling to towards the ground below as enormous clouds of smoke billow into the sky.



The desperate six were left with no choice but to leap for their lives after the fire broke out at a factory in north Delhi, India, on Sunday.

They have been identified as Priyanka, 28 and her daughters Vanshika, 8, and Vaani, 5 as well as Vijay, 30, Santosh, 33, and her daughter Tanvi, 8.



All six jumpers were rushed to hospital with one being treated for a serious leg injury.

Delhi Fire Services (DFS) were informed of the blaze at Swaroop Nagar around 11 am on Sunday.

A total of 15 units were immediately dispatched to the scene.

DFS said: “Six people from the adjacent house inhaled smoke, jumped from the building, and suffered minor injuries.”



Preliminary investigations suggest the fire started on the first floor of the factory where PVC and cotton fabrics are stored.

The factory was a judo dress and boxing gloves manufacturing unit.

It was not yet known whether the factory was running legally.



Police are investigating the incident and are also investigating the cause of the fire.

12 other people were rescued from nearby buildings.

In a separate incident just hours later, a second fire struck another factory in east Delhi.

A huge blaze broke out at a Godown in Dallupura around 3:30 pm.

Plumes of thick, black smoke covered the sky in the area.



The tin building is understood to have contained plywood and, like the previous blaze, PVC – both of which are highly combustible materials.

The blaze is understood to have broken out on the ground-floor and spread to an area of over 95 square ft.

Over 200 firefighters rushed to the scene around 3:30pm.

The fires come as at least nine people – including a toddler – were killed in a horror fire which ripped through a hotel in Kolkata.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Around 60 people were rescued from the building but nine were found unconscious and later confirmed dead in hospital.



Investigators believe the fire first broke out on the third floor of the hotel and may have been sparked by an air conditioning unit exploding.

News.title: Moment half-naked drug dealer is caught hiding in wardrobe & arrested after exposing location on public Wi-Fi
News.content:
THIS is the moment a half-naked drug dealer was caught hiding in a wardrobe and arrested after he exposed his location on public Wi-Fi.

The Met Police had been investigating the ‘Bobby’ drugs line after examining the mobile phones seized by children suspected of being involved in the supply of narcotics.



However, the dealer in charge of the line had taken extensive steps to conceal their location and had been running all devices through a virtual private network (VPN).

They were able to identify Joel Louis, 34, of Wembley, North London, as the line owner after he inadvertently logged into a public Wi-Fi connection at an address he was hiding at.



As soon as officers had this intelligence, they executed a warrant at the address in Wembley on July 7.

Louis had tried to hide in a wardrobe but was immediately discovered by officers.



Bodycam footage shows the moment officers find him.

One officer says: “Come down, mate.”



During the arrest Louis asked officers: “How did you find me?”.

Later analysis of his phone found Louis was receiving more than 100 calls a day from his contact list of nearly 250 drug users.

He had also bragged to some about how he owned a firearm.

A search of the address led to the recovery of Class A drugs, including cocaine and heroin with a street value of £8,800, approximately £8,000 in cash and six mobile phones.

One of which was identified as the phone used to run the ‘Bobby’ line.



Officers also found a loaded firearm concealed inside a box, thirteen rounds of 9mm ammunition, including three rounds loaded into the firearm’s magazine, a machete, and a flip knife.

Louis was charged on July 7 with two counts of possession with intent to supply Class A drugs, possession of offensive weapon in a private place, possession of a firearm, and possession of ammunition.

Detective Constable Lauren Gresty, who led the investigation, said: “Louis recruited numerous young people to move drugs around north Kilburn, exposing them to violence, intimidation and criminality for his own financial gain.

“County lines devastates lives. It is far more than drug dealing. It causes damage to local communities through its connections to acquisitive crimes and anti-social behaviour.

“Louis believed he could hide from police to further his offending, but this result shows our tenacity in going after those who cause the most harm in London.”



At Harrow Crown Court, Louis was sentenced to 12 years’ and nine months’ imprisonment for offences connected to the supply of cocaine and heroin in north Kilburn.

News.title: Army veteran and midwife killed after plane crashes in Brit holiday hotspot – as probe launched into tragedy
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

CRASH HORROR Army veteran and midwife killed after plane crashes in Brit holiday hotspot – as probe launched into tragedy

AN army veteran and a midwife have been killed after their biplane crashed in a Brit holiday hotspot.

The aircraft crashed on Sunday morning in La Londe-les-Maures, a popular spot nestled between Marseille and Saint-Tropez in the south of France.

Retired air force general Patrick Feron was at the controls when the plane went down, according to local officials.

The biplane had taken off from Cuers airfield in the Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur region before crashing in the commune around 20 kilometres further south, according to French newspaper Le Figaro.





Feron died alongside his passenger, who has been named in reports as a senior midwife at the Fréjus Saint-Raphaël hospital.

Feron served as the vice-president of Les Ailes de la Reconnaissance, a local association for aviation enthusiasts.

The charitable association – which means ‘Wings of Recognition’ in English – provides introductory flights to healthcare workers to thank them for their dedicated service.

Authorities confirmed that the cause of the tragic crash remains undetermined as investigations continue.

The association’s president, Daniel Muraro, told French outlet La Depeche: “The plane was in perfect condition, there was fuel, the weather was perfect.

“He (the pilot, editor’s note) had flown it the day before. Everything was going very well.

“Then he took off and didn’t come back.”

Muraro claimed to the newspaper that the accident occurred after approximately 15 minutes of flight.



Only one fire engine from the Var fire department was involved, according to France 3 Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur.

La Londe-les-Maures is a coastal commune nestled on the French Riviera at the foot of the Massif des Maures mountain range.

It sits between the towns of Hyères and Le Lavandou.

The spot is widely favoured as a relaxed, less glitzy alternative to the nearby Côte d’Azur hotspots, drawing visitors with its long sandy beaches, scenic walking routes, and vineyards producing renowned Côtes de Provence AOC wines.

Its large marina also serves as a major departure point for boats heading out to the Golden Islands, an archipelago famous for its dramatic rocky cliffs, dense pine forests, and crystal-clear waters.

News.title: UK weather maps show 34 areas will be battered by heavy rain on Monday - see full list
News.content:
UK weather maps show 34 areas will be battered by heavy rain on Monday - see full list

The Met Office says the unsettled Atlantic weather will return on Monday, delivering typical autumnal downpours and strong winds - especially in the north of England and in most of Scotland

View 3 Images Umbrellas will be out on Monday for millions across the UK (Image: PA)

More than 30 areas are about to be pounded by heavy rain with flood alerts issued as any hope of one last heatwave is washed away.

‌



It appears the UK won't be getting a sixth and final period of scorching temperatures, but although millions will have to seek cover amid a very wet start to the new week, we could still see 25C warmth before next weekend.

‌



But the Met Office's weather maps are about to turn blue and the agency's forecast for Monday shows rain is set to hit almost all of Scotland as well as parts of northern England. It will be hard for anyone in the areas to evade the downpour as maps show every county being bombarded by wet conditions, with the heaviest rain expected in the far north of Scotland near Stornoway.

‌



But things will be challenging in England, too. Flashes of striking orange appear on Met Office weather maps around the Lake District, suggesting the area will see the heaviest downpour.

Forecasters fear 'intense' El Nino effect to last until at least February READ MORE :

Heatwave verdict as UK temperatures forecast to rise once more READ MORE :

View 3 Images Weather maps show an orange flash coming on Monday

Three flood alerts are now in place. There are warnings over the Tidal River Avon, on the Somerset coast at Porlock Weir and the tidal River Waveney, with high tides expected.

‌



However, the battering doesn't spell the end of the warmth. Most areas will see sunshine in the days ahead, before the unsettled Atlantic weather returns.

Five sweltering periods between May and August left the majority of the country in drought, sparking wildfires, hosepipe bans and travel disruption and another heatwave hadn't been ruled out in September. Things will warm up, but the conditions aren't likely to satisfy the official structural requirements for a heatwave.

‌



The Met Office's forecast for Monday states: "Warm and humid in the south with cloudy skies, although some brighter spells are possible. A dry start in the north, before heavy rain moves into Northern Ireland and Scotland."

While rain will hit in the north of the UK, the Met Office has also forecast warm temperatures, especially in the south.

There could be highs of 25C in London and 22C in Manchester and Cardiff, the forecast shows. It will also likely reach 20C in parts of Scotland.

‌



BBC weather forecaster Ben Rich says conditions are about to get warmer but doubts the high temperatures will stick around.

Explaining that it will feel warm and muggy over the next few days, he said: "While things will undoubtedly feel warm, it will remain below the criteria for a heatwave.

"This would require three consecutive days of temperatures above a threshold which varies from 25C in Scotland and Northern Ireland to 28C in the London area."

‌



While the cool conditions have been a welcome reprieve for many, with some much-needed rain falling across the UK this week and more to follow next week, it would appear that there may be one final blast of summery weather to come.

News.title: 'Questions must be answered when a staggering £72million buys political influence'
News.content:
'Questions must be answered when a staggering £72million buys political influence'

Reform’s £72million in donations from two crypto billionaires raises questions over political influence, particularly as Nigel Farage pushes policies that could benefit the cryptocurrency industry

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

Peers on Monday confront a fundamental question about whether Britain’s democracy can be bought, just days after Reform banked an astonishing £72 million from two crypto billionaires. Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne each gave Nigel Farage’s party £36 million as Parliament prepares to debate tougher rules on mega-donations. The timing is extraordinary and demands the closest scrutiny. So does Reform’s record. For months, Farage has chipped away at the authority of Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey, even suggesting he would remove him from office if he gained power and later refusing to guarantee he could serve out his term. Such political interference in the Bank's independence would be highly unusual and deeply troubling. Farage has also waged war on plans for a government-backed “Britcoin”. After lobbying the Bank last September, he told crypto enthusiasts he was “prepared to go to prison” to stop it. He also wants lower taxes on crypto assets and a Bitcoin reserve. The donors insist they want nothing in return. Perhaps so. But when £72 million lands in the coffers of a party promising policies that could benefit the industry that made its donors rich, suspicion is inevitable. Parliament must ensure political power can never simply go to the highest bidder.

‌



Charles must act

King Charles is right to use his influence to demand that artificial intelligence is developed in the public interest, not simply at breakneck speed. His meeting with some of the biggest names in AI comes at a moment when even industry leaders are sounding the alarm. Anthropic boss Dario Amodei has warned that progress is moving so quickly that safety measures risk being left hopelessly behind. His fear that AI could within months be powerful enough to control vast swathes of the internet should concentrate minds. The King’s message must be unmistakable: the people building this technology cannot be allowed to race ahead while the rest of the world is left to deal with the consequences. He should demand safeguards, transparency and proper human control before more power is handed to machines.

Running for a cause

Andy Burnham joined 63,000 hardy souls pounding the Great North Run, raising money for homelessness charity Changing Lives and donating 15 per cent of his first month’s Number 10 salary. The PM may have grabbed the headlines, but thousands more ran for causes close to home. Sore legs, blistered feet and millions raised. Not a bad day’s work.

News.title: Pressure mounts for mega-donations crackdown after Reform's £72m haul from crypto billionaires
News.content:
Pressure mounts for mega-donations crackdown after Reform's £72m haul from crypto billionaires

Crypto billionaires Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne both announced mammoth donations of £36million each to Nigel Farage's Reform Party over the weekend

View 5 Images Reform UK received two mega donations from crypto billionaires over the weekend (Image: Getty Images)

Calls to slam the door on mega-donations will be heard in Parliament on Monday after Reform trousered a record £72million from two crypto billionaires.

‌



Nigel Farage's party was handed £36million each from Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne over the weekend in a move that has fired up growing pressure to curb political donations.

‌



The record-breaking gifts cast a new light over the Reform UK's leaders' attempts to lobby the Bank of England last year against plans for a state-run alternative to crypto.

‌



Mr Farage has since suggested twice that he would sack the Bank of England governor if Reform was in power, and said he would rather go to prison than support plans for a digital pound.

Mr Farage said in October that he'd get rid of Mr Bailey if he was in charge, saying: "He's had a good run. We might find someone new." In January he refused to guarantee the Governor would be allowed to serve out his term to March 2028

The massive cash injection will deepen scrutiny over Reform's finances. The party is already facing several probes including a criminal investigation into an alleged foreign donations scandal exposed in an undercover sting.

‌



TUC General Secretary Paul Nowak said voters would smell a rat. He said: "The public will say what does he want for his £36million?"

View 5 Images Angela Rayner said donors should not be able to buy their way into democracy (Image: Jeff Overs/BBC/PA Wire)

And Unite's Sharon Graham told the Mirror: "We must ensure that Britain’s democracy is not for sale."

‌



The news of Reform's latest donations has electrified the debate over the influence of big money in British politics.

The Representation of the People Bill, which heads to the Lords on Monday, includes plans for a £100,000 cap on donations from Brits living overseas. The proposals would apply for the remainder of the calendar year and the following calendar year after they return.

Communities Secretary Angela Rayner signalled Reform could be forced to hand back the cash if it falls foul of new rules. Both men are British but have spent time abroad - with Mr Delo previously living in Hong Kong and Mr Harborne based in Thailand.

‌



Asked about the donations, Ms Rayner told Sky News: "We need to have secure elections that are for the people, and that you can’t buy your way into our democracy. And that’s why the Rycroft Review was set up, and we’ve already taken action against overseas donations, which will be backdated for when Rycroft published [March 25].”

But Reform’s Treasury spokesman Robert Jenrick said: "These two donations are entirely in line with the law as it is and, as far as we know, the law as it's going to be in the future.”

View 5 Images Businessman Christopher Harborne has donated millions of pounds to Reform (Image: George Cracknell Wright/LNP)

‌



Both men have already donated millions of pounds to Reform. Mr Harborne also gave £5m to Mr Farage ahead of the 2024 election, which is subject to a probe by the parliamentary standards commissioner as Mr Farage failed to declare it. He insists no rules have been broken and claims it was a personal gift.

Mr Farage has given shifting explanations, originally saying it was for his personal security and then later claiming it was a reward for campaigning for Brexit. In a bad-tempered media round earlier this year, he said it was no one's business what he spent the money on, and said he could splash it on Ferraris or betting on horse racing if he wanted to.

Reform is facing a separate police investigation in the wake of an undercover report by Channel 4 and Verbatim Investigations, which appeared to show senior figures discussing ways to evade the law to secure foreign donations worth £500,000.

‌



The inquiry is also looking into donations given to the party by Fiona Cottrell, mother of George Cottrell - a Farage ally known as Posh George. Reform denies wrongdoing.

View 5 Images Nigel Farage with ally George Cottrell, known as Posh George (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Ms Rayner also opened the door to a wider cap on political donations from UK individuals and companies. “It’s not as simple as saying we won’t put a cap,” she told the BBC, saying officials have been instructed to look at how one could work.

‌



Labour MP Stella Creasy tabled an amendment to the bill to prevent donors from giving more than £100,000 in a single year, but it was not debated. Instead, the Government said it would set up a taskforce to look at mega-donors. Labour peer Lord Wills is expected to raise the issue today(MON) and to table an amendment in the House of Lords.

Reform insists the two men want nothing in exchange for the donations, and will not receive a knighthood, peerage or government contracts. But the record sums have sparked alarm over whether mega-donations could have a distorting impact on British politics.

Elections expert Robert Hayward said electoral law was struggling to keep up with donations of this scale and warned it could trigger an “arms race” among political parties. “If we don't do anything about our law then there is no question, we will be into American politics where money buys attention, and attention buys votes,” he told the BBC.

‌



TUC General Secretary Paul Nowak told reporters on Sunday: "I think they are going to cause a crisis in our democracy." He said there was no comparison between a care worker or someone working in a car plant giving a few pounds a year to a union, which lobbies openly for its members.

View 5 Images TUC General Secretary Paul Nowak sounded the alarm over the mega donations (Image: Tim Merry)

Mr Nowak said: "I don't know what's driving Christopher Harborne or [Ben] Delo in making those donations. I suspect it's not the welfare of workers or our public services, or tackling climate change, or reindustrialising the country.

‌



"I don't think it's a surprise or a shock that both of them are crypto billionaires and the one set of policies Reform does seem to have fully worked out is about de-regulating crypto." He added: "The public will say what does he want for his £36million? Is he doing just because he's a nice fella?"

Unite General Secretary Sharon Graham told the Mirror: "The idea that two crypto billionaires woke up one morning and said ‘I must make the world a better place. I must give tens of millions to Farage…” is fanciful. What this is clearly about is Reform’s politics on crypto among others. We need this issue dealt with decisively and quickly."

She added: "The government now needs to act quickly to cap individual donations in a clear message that British democracy is not for sale."

‌



Reform has announced a number of crypto-friendly policies, including a pledge to slash taxes on crypto assets and set up a “Bitcoin reserve”. Mr Farage told crypto enthusiasts last year that he was so opposed to plans by the Bank of England for a digital currency that he was “prepared to go to prison” to stop it, according to footage of the Zebu Live event in London.

TUC Assistant General Secretary Kate Bell said: “This is proof that Nigel Farage and Reform are already doing the bidding of their billionaire crypto backers. Their priority isn’t helping working people - it’s serving corporate interests.”

On Sunday, Mr Jenrick denied his party was “very pro-cryptocurrency”, saying he wanted to see “proper regulation”. He told the BBC: “At the moment, it’s a wild west in many respects. What we want to see is good regulation here in the UK through the FCA (Financial Conduct Authority) so we can protect people.”

Article continues below

But shadow foreign secretary Tom Tugendhat issued a warning about the murky world of crypto. He told Sky News: “The crypto industry has got many supporters, I know, including in Iran where they use it to buy weapons from Venezuela; including in Russia where they use it to launder money in order to pay agents around Europe.”

Cryptocurrency is a digital form of money that operates on a peer-to-peer basis, without the need for banks or other third parties. Transactions are recorded in a massive database, known as a blockchain, which is distributed through a network of computers to keep it secure.

Famous examples include bitcoin and dogecoin.

News.title: 'I walked into Specsavers for simple tests and found out I had a brain tumour'
News.content:
'I walked into Specsavers for simple tests and found out I had a brain tumour'

EXCLUSIVE: After Lynne Jones, 51, needed her laptop's brightness turned down at work, she decided to get her eyes checked — and a trip to Specsavers in Reading, Berkshire, flipped her world

10 things you should know about brain tumours

A woman who had blurred vision and thought she simply needed some stronger lens was diagnosed with a brain tumour.

‌



Lynne Jones popped into her local Specsavers when she needed her laptop's brightness turned down at work and, due to sudden blurred vision, couldn't make out someone driving a car. The 51-year-old woman assumed it'd be a routine appointment but puzzled staff worked for hours to come up with some answers after she struggled to make out colours.

‌



After a telltale sign was discovered following even more tests, Lynne said she knew trouble was ahead when the optometrist's face suddenly dropped. She was eventually sent to hospital with a letter, and was stunned to discovered the reason for her sight issues were down to a brain tumour, which has actually wrapped around her optic nerves.

‌



Within days, the estate agent, who is from Reading, Berkshire, went under the knife for a craniotomy - a challenging surgical procedure where a neurosurgeon removes a piece of the skull.

Weight loss jab clinics aim to help dieters keep the pounds off in nationwide trial READ MORE :

7 View 7 Images Lynne and husband Lewis' world was turned upside down after she was told to go to hospital right away (Image: Lynne Jones) 7 View 7 Images She soon went under the knife after being told she needed a craniotomy (Image: Lynne Jones)

‌



Speaking to the Mirror, Lynne said: "I started to work from home [weeks prior] as our office was having a re-fit, but when we went back I was struggling with the lights. I asked my colleagues, and they didn't have any complaints.

"I even had to ask my husband to turn the brightness on my laptop down but when I was dropping a parcel off, and I was unable to see people in a car clearly so I did the right thing and booked an appointment.

"I thought I just needed a new prescription so I went to Specsavers, did the checks and went upstairs to do the long-distance vision test. They did my right eye, and it seems all OK. Then it came to the left, and something just wasn't right. We actually spent an hour trying different things, he kept checking. It was weird, not concerning."

‌



View 7 Images She said she owes her life to the staff at the Reading branch (Image: Lynne Jones)

Lynne continued: "He then went and got someone higher up, and she wanted me to get my peripheral vision checked downstairs again, so off I went. She looked at the results, I had missed 50 per cent of colour in both eyes, and I could see the concern on her face.

"They both had a chat, left us in the room, and came back and she said she didn't know what's going on. She said she had never seen it in both eyes."

‌



View 7 Images A number of Specsavers experts couldn't get to the bottom of Lynne Jones' sight problem (Image: Lynne Jones)

Little did the estate agent know that it was just the start of a serious health battle that had her fearing for her life.

"She said she needed me to take a letter to the hospital. It was getting more concerning. I said to my husband that I didn't have the mental capacity to go that day, I said we'll go in the morning," Lynne added.

‌



"We went to the Royal Berkshire hospital and had to sit there all day. I did similar tests. They kept asking me about headaches. I didn't have any so he said he needed to speak to neurology. At this point I'm getting really worried.

View 7 Images The estate agent thought she probably just needed new frames (Image: Lynne Jones)

"I was referred to them a week later and there were lots of balance and coordination tests. They thought I had MS [Multiple Sclerosis]. They then wanted me to go for an MRI scan. At this point it felt like my world was falling apart, I didn't know what was going on and my vision was getting worse."

‌



Recalling the moment Lynne was told she had a brain tumour in October last year, she said she was devastated. She added: "I got the call, it came after 6pm on the Friday," she recalled. "As soon as I saw the time I knew it was really bad. He told me he has a duty of care to inform me I had a brain tumour.

"He said he wanted me to come in and see him on Monday. It was a very long weekend. I was devastated. My husband Lewis collapsed and broke down. I was in such shock, but it allowed us to get some questions ready.

View 7 Images Her scan result revealed some very bad news (Image: Lynne Jones)

‌



"I was then referred to the John Radcliffe Hospital. They then called a day or so later and asked me to come in the next morning. I remember thinking 'god, it really is that serious'. The next day, I had a brain surgeon."

Following 11 hours of surgery to remove the tumour, she woke up with her sight restored. Praising the surgeon, Lynne said: "I'd rather not have needed to know him, but he is an incredible person. He knew how to treat me. He was honest with us, and said the tumour was in a very difficult spot. It was a serious surgery, because it was pressing on my optic nerves. It has wrapped itself around.

"The good news was I found out from the MRI scan that the tumour was benign, so it appeared we weren't dealing with cancer. But it's only after they remove it that they could confirm. I didn't think I would get my sight back, I thought it was gone. The surgeon told me not to give up and I didn't."

‌



View 7 Images Lynne couldn't see colour - and knew she had a problem (Image: Lynne Jones)

She recently has a full-circle moment where she walked into the branch nine months after that fateful day.

"I've had an eye-test since with the same people who saw me in October," she said. "I can't thank Specsavers enough. Even a few days after they gave me the letter to take to the hospital, they called me asking if I had any news. They really cared.

‌



"I think they genuinely knew something serious was wrong. I don't know what would have happened next if they didn't care as much as they did. I can't express well enough how great they were."

"I honestly feel it's really important that people have eye-tests. Sometimes it's not a prescription. Sometimes it doesn't show up in headaches or fevers. Mine was actually me colour and also my left vision. What you think could just be new glasses could be something very different."

Ravi Bhardwaj, store director at the locally owned and run Specsavers Reading store, says: "We are so pleased that Lynne received the care she needed and that her sight has returned following surgery.

Article continues below

"This is a powerful reminder of why regular eye tests are so important. An eye test does not just check whether you need glasses, it can also detect signs of serious underlying health conditions.

"We are incredibly proud of the team for taking the time to investigate Lynne's results thoroughly and making sure she was referred urgently."

News.title: Boris Johnson evacuated after train drone strike in Ukraine
News.content:
Boris Johnson evacuated after train drone strike in Ukraine

Former UK prime minister Boris Johnson had to be evacuated from a train close to the Ukraine-Poland border following a drone strike which hit the tracks

View Image Boris Johnson in a recent visit to Ukraine (Image: ©5 Broadcasting Limited / Two Rivers Media / Soho Studios Entertainment Press Enquiries: press@channel5.com NOTE: Paramount images are for the use of Press outlets only. Any blogs requesting access to these images are required to seek approval from Paramount directly. Contact press@channel5.com While we will continue to send out the weekly PI booklet every Friday, we have now launched the ViacomCBS Media Hub. This is an all-encompassing press centre where you can find the latest PI, press releases and other relevant information.)

A train carrying Boris Johnson was evacuated after a drone attack which hit tracks in Ukraine.

‌



The former UK prime minister was heading back from a security conference in Kyiv on a "special train" in the early hours of this morning when there was a warning of drone strikes by the Polish border.

‌



Passengers on the train including Johnson were awoken at around 5am and temporarily evacuated due to the imminent danger before being allowed to carry on.

‌



Former Swedish premier and foreign minister Carl Bildt, who was on the same train as Johnson, said the train immediately after theirs was hit by the drone.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

UK weather maps reveal 3C cold snap with 108 counties plunging below 10C READ MORE :

Trump responds to backlash over support for united Ireland and 'loves' what he said READ MORE :

He told how they were told to evacuate before managing to escape across the border to NATO territory in Poland.

‌



“This wasn’t our train [that was hit], but the one just minutes after us by the [Polish] border crossing,” said Bildt. “It was evacuated as the [Russian] drone approached and no one was hurt. Very good safety system.

"Our train just had an evacuation warning but could proceed to Dorohusk. The [Russian] attacks against [Ukraine] are intensifying.”

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Dorohusk is on the Polish side of the border at Yahodyn which Russia was attacking.

There were understood to have been 206 passengers on board the train but no one was injured confirmed the Ukrainian railway authorities. Among those travelling on the special train was Günter Sautter, foreign and security policy adviser to German Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

Images show huge flames coming from a drone strike nearby on a road where where a vehicle was on fire and other photos show a damaged train.

Article continues below

A Russian drone hit a petrol station in Yahodyn, just a few hundred metres from the Poland border, said Ukrainian authorities said with such attacks becoming more common to disrupt the infrastructure of the country and supply of fuel. It has led to mesh cages being installed around some of the facilities in Kyiv.

It was described by Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha as "barbaric" who added that it showed how Vladimir Putin's "terror" was "knocking" on the door of the EU and NATO.

He wrote on X: “Russia’s barbaric strikes at the Ukraine-Poland border crossing point in Yahodyn are not just a continuation of its attacks on our state borders. This is Putin’s terror ‘knocking’ directly on the doors of the EU and NATO."

News.title: Restaurant owners team up to get revenge on the 'Bonnie and Clyde of dine and dash'
News.content:
Restaurant owners team up to get revenge on the 'Bonnie and Clyde of dine and dash'

One half of a pair, who left six restaurants without paying in one month, has now been caught after business owners worked together to try and bring the duo to justice

View 3 Images A couple who dined and dashed at six venues have been caugth in Spain (stock) (Image: Getty)

One half of a couple dubbed the ‘Bonnie and Clyde’ of dine and dash was caught after the duo fled six venues in one part of Spain without paying their bill.

‌



The man, 40, who was arrested on September 4, was one half of a duo who skipped out on bills at restaurants and cafes in the Alt Emporda region of the European country, near the country’s border with France.

‌



The string of dine and dash incidents reportedly happened over a month and the affected parties were reportedly in contact with each other during this time, before it all ended at Pizzeria Il Nonno.

‌



It was at this venue that the man was confronted, then chased, by the manager before being arrested by the Castello d’Empuries Local police.

L'independant reports that the couple had also attempted to pull the same stunt at places along the Costa Brava in Catalonia, five of which were in the coastal town of Empuriabrava.

View 3 Images Most of the incidents happened around Empuriabrava (stock) (Image: Getty)

‌



The first of these alleged incidents was reported on August 17 where, having requested to have their coffee outside, the couple exited leaving the Vilabertran venue €95.40 (£81.89) out of pocket.

Later, they would visit the L’Empuria Beach café where the woman left, followed by the man, who claimed to a waitress that he was leaving for cigarettes. They venue was left with a €75 (£64.38) unpaid bill.

Other venues affected, reports El Gerio Digital, were The Loft, Internet Café, and Restaurant Dlux alongside the restaurant in Vilabertran.

‌



However, it all came to a head at the aforementioned Pizzeria Il Nonno over a bill of €55.10 (£47.30).

View 3 Images The man was later caught by local police (stock) (Image: Getty)

Following the events of the couple’s near month-long spree of fleeing, the six restaurants are now working together to assemble a detailed picture of what happened and how much money was lost, along with evidence from security footage.

‌



It is not yet known what has happened to the arrested individual’s alleged accomplice and whether or not she, in turn, has been caught.

As well as being held by the authorities over the dine and dash incidents, the man was also arrested on a separate offence.

The man, who has not been named, was arrested over allegedly breaching an active restraining order in relation to his former partner and currently has a police record. The precise details of this alleged offence are not known.
