News.title: Woman says she's 'tired' trying to prove she's alive after being declared dead by government
News.content:
Woman says she's 'tired' trying to prove she's alive after being declared dead by government

The elderly Florida widow says the mistake has repeatedly caused problems with her finances and official records, despite being told the error had already been corrected

View 2 Images The 84-year-old was told her Social Security number belonged to someone who had died (Image: WFLA News Channel 8/Youtube)

An 84-year-old woman has spent more than two years trying to prove to government agencies that she is still alive after being mistakenly declared dead.

‌



Priscilla Slack says the bizarre mix-up began after her husband died two years ago, when she was somehow also listed as deceased. The mistake seemed like a small administrative error which would quickly be resolved but two years on it has affected vital parts of her life.

‌



Her bank account was first to be affected. Priscilla said : “First they cancelled my bank account, and they cancelled my credit card. When I went to vote, I was still cancelled."

‌



View 2 Images Priscilla has been passed between government agencies for years (Image: WFLA News Channel 8/Youtube)

She initially tried to see the funny side, assuming the mistake would be quickly put right. She told NBC affiliate WFLA: “I kept my sense of humour about it early on, because we can all make mistakes and push the wrong button”

But the mix-up was not resolved as the problems continued to grow. Priscilla said the original error came from the Social Security Administration, and although she believed it had been corrected, other agencies continued to act as though she was dead.

‌



Each time she thought the issue had finally been resolved, another problem appeared. She has since faced many difficulties including holding bank accounts, paying taxes and voting, with agencies periodically requiring her to prove again that she is alive.

Most recently, Priscilla received a letter from the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) claiming she had filed a tax return using the Social Security number of someone who was deceased forcing her to prove that the number belonged to her.

Priscilla said attempts to resolve the problem have involved being repeatedly passed between the IRS and the Social Security Administration. She said: “How am I supposed to deal with these agencies who can’t deal with each other?”

Article continues below

Priscilla believes the agencies involved should now be responsible for correcting the records rather than leaving her to keep challenging the mistake.

The problems have continued for more than two years since her husband’s death, despite Priscilla previously being told the Social Security error had been corrected. She says other agencies have continued to flag her records and freeze accounts when the incorrect information resurfaces.

A spokesperson for the IRS said the matter was being escalated to an advocacy department in an effort to resolve it, according to WFLA.

News.title: Major EES update for 9 UK tourist hotspots including Portugal
News.content:
Major EES update for 9 UK tourist hotspots including Portugal

The European Union entry-exit system (EES) has caused repeated delays for Brits at major EU airports this year

View 3 Images (Image: Anadolu, Anadolu via Getty Images)

British holidaymakers heading abroad may finally be able to breathe a sigh of relief over the widely-criticised EES system. The scheme forces non-EU residents to queue at special machines in airports before gaining entry to 29 nations within the so-called Schengen area – essentially the majority of the European Union.

‌



However, there have been persistent reports of lengthy delays – some stretching to as long as four hours. A new report in the Sunday Times now reveals that the European Union has shelved the controversial entry-exit system (EES) across at least nine countries.

‌



Portugal, Italy, France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany, Malta, Greece and Switzerland are all understood to have been granted permission to postpone full implementation of EES. The newspaper reports that there appears to be no deadline by which these countries must adopt the scheme, which has already sparked widespread reports of enormous queues at European airports this summer in destinations such as Mallorca, Faro, the Canary Islands and Milan.

‌



The scheme has faced fierce criticism from Ryanair and others. The European Union describes the Entry/Exit System (EES) as an automated IT system designed to register non-EU nationals travelling on short stays each time they cross the external borders of participating European countries.

Following years of postponements, the system was rolled out from October 2025, with full implementation originally anticipated by the following April. However, faced with the prospect of significant border queues due to software failures, officials granted countries a 150-day grace period during which they could drop the checks to avoid travel chaos.

That rule ended on September 6. The EU previously insisted there would be no extension.

‌



View 3 Images (Image: Anadolu, Anadolu via Getty Images)

Yet the Sunday Times reports that at least nine Schengen countries are understood to have told the European Commission, which is responsible for overseeing the EES, that they would not enforce the new controls in full until the technology and systems were working correctly.

They have informally been allowed to do so with no time limits apparently in place to adopt the system, it is being reported. One of the main purposes of the system is to track whether non-EU citizens have spent more than their permitted 90 days in the bloc in a rolling 180-day period.

‌



Social media has been awash with debate about the scheme. One post on Reddit saw a traveller say: "They made a mess of it. Seems many basic things like it is hit and miss on the document scanning but also things like people walk up with hats and headphones and the machine doesn't tell them to remove them, and organisational things like if the machine errors the traveller has to back out and has no where to go.

"The right way to do this would have been progressive: start by getting some people eg 5% going through the machine lane, everyone else through normal.

"The vendor observes problems, fixes them, once machine working well, increase to 10%, then 20% and so on." Another person said: "The general lack of functionality of so many IT systems across the EU is kind of astonishing."

‌



A third added: "It's worse than that. There isn't even consistent protocol/IT support within a single EU airport."

Another put it more simply, saying: "I just miss having stamps."

'People are missing their flights'

Nadia, from Greater Manchester, told the Guardian in August she had made two trips to Schengen areas this summer. A trip to Tenerife in June was "quite straightforward", but her experience in July at Frankfurt airport where she was picking up a connecting flight home, was much less so.

‌



"The queue there was ridiculously long, and there was very limited information," she says. "People were wandering around trying to work out where they needed to go.

View 3 Images The new entry and exit system (EES) has led to huge delays for passengers, with some missing flights (Image: Getty)

"I'm very well travelled and pretty confident, but even I was slightly unsure and was thinking, is there some other queue I should be joining? There was no one nearby to check with without losing your place."

Article continues below

Eventually, her passport was checked. "He didn't actually take fingerprints then," says Nadia, who is a solicitor. "I think the queue was so long they decided to dispense with that.

"It's the efficiency of the system I question and the fact that individual member states' systems do not talk to one another. They shouldn't need to get information again if you have already gone through. It's pretty shambolic, and I think people missing their flights because of it is just not acceptable, especially when there's no recourse; it's not your fault."

Ryanair chief executive Michael O'Leary has repeatedly complained about EES. Speaking earlier this year, he said: "There's a bit of Brexit in this too. Here, you voted for Brexit - f***ing join the queue."

News.title: Will record donations to Reform go down as a moment of political change?
News.content:
When news of Reform UK's two record-breaking Â£36m donations emerged this weekend, it felt as if Nigel Farage's inner circle was attempting a fightback.

The last few months have proved difficult for the party, with a dip in the polls, a spike in infighting and a series of questions about money that simply won't go away.

In contrast, the mood within the ranks of Labour and the Conservatives has been fairly chipper.

Most Labour MPs feel Andy Burnham has got off to an impressive start as prime minister, while many Conservatives are feeling confident about Kemi Badenoch's recent reshuffle of her top team.

But Reform has been quietly - and as of this weekend rather loudly - building a formidable war chest.

Even before these two mega donations, Reform had raised Â£30.5m since the start of the year, more than double their nearest rivals.

This extra Â£72m takes them into uncharted financial territory, which the party says will be used to hire the brightest policy minds, as well as up to 400 campaign managers in every target seat around the country.

In a world of fractured politics, when seats can be won on increasingly smaller percentages of the vote, having a ground campaign that is effective at getting out the core voter base could become increasingly important.

Some in Westminster have been less than convinced by Burnham's insistence that he won't call an early general election.

It might be tempting for the prime minister to go to the polls before Farage has had time to splash the cash on a shiny new party machine.

Some Labour MPs think that could factor into his thinking, but one Number 10 source insisted Reform's extra cash does not make an early election any more likely.

Burnham is now likely to come under increasing pressure to further change the rules on party donations.

Labour is already planning to introduce a cap on the amount of money a British citizen living overseas can donate.

There has been much talk about whether that could impact the donations to Reform by cryptocurrency billionaires Christopher Harborne and Ben Delo, but when interviewed by the BBC, Angela Rayner refused to say whether the two would be caught up in the rule changes.

The Liberal Democrats and Greens have also called for a cap for people based in Britain too, to prevent future mega donations.

Burnham has indicated that he's open to having that conversation, but chose not to support an effort by some Labour MPs earlier this month to tighten the rules.

Rayner confirmed this morning that it was still something being considered by ministers.

The Electoral Commission is looking at what more should be done in this area and the calls from within Labour for further change will now grow stronger.

Government sources insist this weekend's donations are not being viewed inside Downing Street as a game-changing moment in this debate.

But people across the political spectrum are now asking whether this massive injection of money will be remembered as a key moment when politics in this country changed.

News.title: Andy Burnham among Great North Run finishers
News.content:
The Great North Run (GNR) returned to Tyneside this weekend, with 63,000 runners taking part in the world's biggest half marathon - including Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

England star and Newcastle captain Dan Burn rang the starter's bell, with famous faces including football personality Chris Kamara and fitness coach Joe Wicks taking on the challenge.

The 13.1-mile (21km) event saw runners and wheelchair users race from Newcastle through Gateshead and South Tyneside, before finishing in South Shields.

Britons David Weir and Melanie Woods won the men's and women's elite wheelchair races respectively. Brigid Kosgei won the elite women's contest and Zouhair Talbi won the men's race.

The half marathon is in its 45th year and raises about Â£25m for charity each time.

News.title: Meghan shares glimpse of family life after Sussexes return to UK
News.content:
The Duchess of Sussex has shared a glimpse of family life in footage posted to Instagram following their return to the UK.

The 34-second clip, which features Wham!'s Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go, begins with Meghan, along with her husband Prince Harry, walking along a country path as she turns and says "come on, you".

UK flag and heart emojis are shown throughout the video, which also shows their son Archie running towards deer as their daughter Lilibet rides her bike.

Another clip sees Harry fishing with the children as their dog walks alongside the water.

It's the first time the Duchess has posted her family on her Instagram grid since the Sussexes returned from from the US after living in California.

It is unclear when, or where, the footage posted on Sunday afternoon was taken, external, but one clip shows a pair of wellington boots walking on the spot in a puddle and the children also appear to be in waterproof boots as they head toward the deer.

The UK has had a wet start to September after experiencing its hottest summer on record.

The post offers a rare glimpse into the lives of seven-year-old Archie and five-year-old Lilibet.

Whereas Meghan does occasionally show the couple's children on social media, their faces are often obscured as they are photgraphed from behind or their faces are hidden by their parents.

Alongside all the outside footage, there is also a moment showing a child's feet in front of an open fire.

News.title: 'Slim chance' government will hit 1.5m new homes target, Rayner tells BBC
News.content:
There is only a "slim chance" the government will meet its target of building 1.5 million homes in England by the next election, Housing Secretary Angela Rayner has told the BBC.

"Headwinds" including the Iran war and rising construction costs are making it harder to meet the key Labour manifesto pledge, Rayner told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg.

"But I'm definitely not giving it up," she said, and stressed that the government was "making a difference" through investing billions in social and affordable homes.

Data up to June this year suggested the government was behind on the rate of construction needed to meet the goal, which housebuilders have previously warned was too optimistic.

Labour promised to hit the target through building both private and social housing by the end of the current parliament, meaning summer 2029 at the latest.

This implied an average of 300,000 new properties would be needed each year - a rate of construction not seen in decades.

Rayner told the BBC on Sunday: "It's a slim chance, but I'm definitely not giving it up."

She said it was important to keep the goal - which she said had always been a "stretch target" - in place, but that she was "being honest with the public" that it would be difficult to achieve.

News.title: Police searching for six men over anti-migrant protest in Portsmouth
News.content:
The government condemned "intimidating and thuggish behaviour" at the demonstration, while stressing the right to peaceful protest.

On Friday, a 42-year-old man from Paulsgrove was charged with violent disorder and assaulting a police officer in connection with the incident. He has been remanded into custody.

A 16-year-old boy was arrested on Saturday in connection with the disorder. He has been released on bail pending further enquiries.

Rowlinson said: "The reality of public order policing is that arrests at the time are not always possible, especially where evidence may need to be reviewed to clearly identify who is responsible for offences."

The force had reviewed "hundreds of hours' worth" of footage, he said, adding: "The actions we have been taking as part of our investigation send a clear warning to anyone intent on causing disruption and disorder at any future events."

Around 500 anti-migrant protesters took to the streets of Portsmouth on Saturday and were met by hundreds of counter-protesters from Stand up to Racism.

Migrants intercepted in the Channel are typically brought to Dover for initial processing.

However, the dinghy that arrived at Eastney Marina had set off from near Cherbourg in the Bay of the Seine, about 170 miles (274km) west of Calais and significantly further west than the usual departure points.

News.title: US embassy child abuse images suspect flown from UK before police interview
News.content:
A US embassy staffer accused of possessing indecent images of children, was detained at his south London flat and flown out of the UK in August, without being first questioned by British police.

The US Embassy confirmed to the BBC that authorities are investigating the allegations and they have reassigned the staff member to the US while inquiries continue.

"The United States government expects all personnel to adhere to the highest standards of conduct, and we take these allegations seriously," embassy officials said in a statement.

They added that they "quickly informed UK law enforcement and took swift action."

It is understood the individual worked at the US embassy in Vauxhall, south west London, and though not a diplomat, he enjoyed the umbrella of diplomatic protection.

He was flown back to the United States on a commercial flight, but their investigations are ongoing in conjunction with UK authorities.

It is also understood Home Office ministers and the Metropolitan Police are in close contact with the US embassy on this matter as investigations continue.

A UK government spokesperson said: "We expect all foreign diplomats in the UK to abide by our laws, in the same way we expect all UK diplomats to do so when posted overseas."

News.title: Was Haaland's winner a VAR error? Man Utd fury at 'injustice'
News.content:
Dale Johnson, BBC Sport football issues correspondent

The curiosity about this incident is that the goal was initially disallowed for the wrong reason. Haaland was flagged offside when he shouldn't have been.

But as it turned out, the goal should have been ruled out because Fernandez was offside.

There is one key part of the offside law which applies to Fernandez here. A player is offside if they are:

"Clearly attempting to play a ball which is close when this action impacts on an opponent."

Both parts of that clause must be met. It is possible for a player in an offside position to attempt to play a ball and not commit an offence â there must be impact on an opponent too.

As the ball came in, Fernandez threw himself to try to head it, with Martinez directly behind him.

Video assistant referee Matt Donohue should ask himself if Fernandez's action would have influenced Martinez.

In other words: If Fernandez had not jumped for the attempted header, would Martinez have made a different decision over playing the ball?

If the ball had been out of reach for Fernandez, or for Martinez, then there is an argument to give the goal.

And also: There would have been no offside had Fernandez made no attempt to play the ball.

But he did. And as it went just a yard in front of Martinez too, it is very difficult to argue Fernandez did not commit an offside offence.

There is also an argument that the actions of Fernandez influence the positioning of goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

However, the goal was originally ruled out for offside against Haaland - which was incorrect. So that decision had to be overturned.

And then, the VAR should have sent referee Michael Oliver to the monitor for the subjective offence by Fernandez.

It would have created the odd situation where a disallowed goal was reviewed to remain ruled out - but this is what should have happened.

It was a clear offside offence by Fernandez and will go down as a VAR mistake.

News.title: Best friends for decades - until a DNA test revealed they were sisters
News.content:
Theirs is a story straight out of a Bollywood film.

Two Indian-born women in their 40s, adopted as babies by different families and raised near each other in the Netherlands, have now discovered they are biological sisters.

Meena Geltink and Minal Tijssen, born in the early 1980s, were adopted from two different orphanages in the western Indian city of Mumbai within months of their birth.

When they first met in their early teens at an event hosted by the adoption agency their parents had used, they were struck by the uncanny similarities in their appearance and mannerisms.

Meena, now 43, remembers the day clearly.

"All the adopted children were brought together to hang out and bond and have dinner."

Both Meena and Minal were with friends who noticed how similar they looked.

"They said, 'Look at yourselves in the mirror'.

"And I was like, 'Oh my God, she has my nose! We have the same laugh'.

"At dinner, I kept looking at her the whole time," Meena told the BBC from her home in the Netherlands.

The following day, the girls exchanged telephone numbers and addresses and promised to keep in touch.

Even though there was no indication they were related by blood, their connection was instant, and for years they wrote each other letters, often addressing each other as "Sis" because "we felt that way".

They wrote about school, friends, boys, going out and dancing. They told each other about the sports they played and discussed music, discovering they both loved Backstreet Boys.

Then 15 years ago, they lost contact. Minal had moved to France. And Meena had recently had her first child and got busy.

News.title: Reform confident it won't need to repay any of £72m under proposed new donor rules
News.content:
Reform UK believes the Â£72m in donations it has received from two cryptocurrency billionaires were "entirely in line with the law", the party's economic spokesman has said.

Robert Jenrick told the BBC he did not expect that the party will have to return any of the money from Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne, who are both British and have spent time living overseas.

The government is seeking to change the law on donations to UK political parties from British expats, including a Â£100,000 cap backdated to 25 March.

"These two donations are entirely in line with the law as it is and, as far as we know, the law as it's going to be in the future," Jenrick said.

As well as limiting how much British citizens can donate to political parties from overseas, the government has proposed a minimum residency period in which the Â£100,000 cap would still apply for those who move back to the UK.

This would be in place for the remainder of the calendar year and the following calendar year after the person returns.

Housing Secretary Angela Rayner told the BBC's Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that the rule changes would apply retrospectively and anyone not complying with them would have "to return that money".

Rayner added she was not commenting specifically on Delo and Harborne as she does not "understand" their "circumstances".

Answering questions about the donations following Rayner's remarks, Jenrick said: "It might be that Angela Rayner or the government keep trying to change the law to make it even harder for people to donate to Reform, nothing would surprise me.

"But, as it stands, we believe these are entirely in line with the law."

BBC News has been told that both Delo and Harborne have returned to the UK. Delo is understood to have been back in the country since last year.

Jenrick said Delo had returned to the UK "in part so that he can comply with the changes to the law".

In a statement after the programme, a Reform UK spokesman said: "We are 100% confident both [donations] are legal and won't ever have to be handed back."

One person familiar with the government's proposed changes said the issue of whether Delo and Harborne are affected would likely come down to how ministers choose to define UK residency.

They said one way would be to adopt the same definition used in tax laws, but stressed how complex the rules around residency are.

News.title: Residents 'did not hear alarms' during fatal tower fire
News.content:
Some residents in an east London tower block have said they did not hear any alarms during a fire in which a man died on the 17th floor.

They told BBC London they had been alerted by neighbours banging on their doors and telling them to leave the building during the early hours of Saturday.

The man died in the flat fire at Neutron Tower in Poplar. Two adults and a child were rescued by firefighters wearing breathing apparatus, the London Fire Brigade (LFB) said.

FirstPort, the building's management company, said "it would not be appropriate for us to speculate on specific matters" while the fire was under investigation.

The LFB said: "There are a range of factors that are being investigated regarding the cause of the fire by the Brigade's Fire Investigation Team."

News.title: Veterans who died by suicide honoured at memorial
News.content:
Hundreds of people have gathered at the National Memorial Arboretum for the dedication of a permanent tribute to veterans and armed forces personnel who have died by suicide.

The Elysium Memorial, at the site in Alrewas, Staffordshire, is the first permanent memorial of its kind to be built in the UK.

More than 1,300 military veterans and personnel have taken their lives in the last 30 years, with the memorial aiming to provide a place for contemplation for those affected by the loss of a friend or loved one.

Edward Mackenzie, co-founder of the Elysium Memorial Foundation, which is behind the project, said he was "blown away" by the number of people that had turned up.

More than 300 motorcyclist rode to the arboretum from Burton-on-Trent on Sunday, with a convoy organised by community organisation Wheels for Wishes.

Mackenzie, who served in the army for more than 30 years and has lost over to 20 friends to suicide, including his best friend, said seeing those veterans' being recognised "means everything".

"This is why I did it, I did for for the friends, the families, the comrades, those that we've lost to suicide," he told the BBC.

"There's a lot of families here today that have been thanking me for achieving this memorial so I'm incredibly grateful."

News.title: New Welsh constituency names could be changed - again
News.content:
New constituency names in Wales - used for the first time in this May's Senedd election - are going to be reviewed and possibly changed.

It means the 16 constituencies could see changes to Welsh-only names that proved unpopular, with any amendments set to be in place by the 2030 election.

Democracy and Boundary Commission Cymru chief executive Shereen Williams said the review would ensure constituencies reflected the communities they serve, including cultural heritage and Welsh language use.

The 2025 review paired UK parliamentary constituencies - for MPs - and former Welsh Senedd areas to create 16 new constituencies for May's Senedd expansion, with six Members of the Senedd representing each.

This saw the number of MSs increase from 60 to 96, with 40 constituencies and five regions changed to 16 areas.

Williams told BBC Radio Wales' Sunday Supplement that the new Welsh-only consistency names could also be revised following public consultation as they did not prove popular with everyone.

She added that legislation required the use of single names where possible, but said: "If we are unable to find a name that reflects the identity of the area, or that's completely unrecognisable, it has nothing to do with the area, then we would then consider bilingual names.

"These set of boundaries that were used for the recent set of elections were always meant to be temporary. We're not we're not starting from a blank slate.

"Some people thought we would be wiping off all the boundaries and rebuilding them.

"No, we are going to start from the boundaries that were used in the recent Senedd elections and go from there."

News.title: Baby death suspects released on bail
News.content:
Two people arrested in connection with the death of a one-year-old girl in Warwickshire have been released on bail, police say.

It comes after emergency services were called to a house on Long Street, Atherstone, at about 11:50 BST on Friday to reports of a child in cardiac arrest. She was pronounced dead at the scene a short while later, police said.

A 19-year-old woman and a man aged 21 were then both arrested at the scene on suspicion of child neglect.

Later the pair were further arrested on suspicion of causing or allowing the death of a child, said Warwickshire Police.

Det Ch Insp Martyn Kendall said: "This tragic death has understandably caused a great deal of shock and concern in the local community.

"The two suspects arrested have now been bailed with strict conditions."

The force said officers were waiting for a post-mortem examination to be carried out to help shed more light on the circumstances leading up to her death.

Anyone with information has been urged to contact the force.

News.title: Police probe use of firearm after man found dead in Armadale
News.content:
Police are investigating the use of a firearm after a man was found dead in West Lothian.

Emergency services were called to reports of an injured person in a property on Harestanes Road, Armadale, at about 11:50 on Saturday. A 35-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene.

Police Scotland said inquiries were at an early stage and a post-mortem examination would take place, but one line of inquiry is that a firearm may have been used.

The force is also looking at whether a car fire in the nearby Netherhouses area is linked to the incident.

News.title: Zoo advertises tickets for 'child predator tour'
News.content:
A zoo has blamed a computer error after it advertised a "child predator tour" online to see its tigers and lions.

Bosses at Chester Zoo quickly changed the 90-minute bus tour's name after it was branded "sinister" by visitors.

A zoo spokeswoman said the error was "due to our default naming convention in our system", but it was "quickly changed".

The name blunder earlier this week was part of the Cheshire zoo's ticket promotion to allow visitors to go on a tour showcasing its Sumatran tigers, lions, rhinos and Komodo dragons.

The mistake was mocked by the zoo's customers and visitors online.

One remarked: "I hope this has been cleared by Cheshire Police - seems a bit dangerous."

Another said: "Staggering - how did that get approved?"

The private bus tour cost Â£25 for children. 'Adult predator' tickets were also advertised by mistake for Â£30.

The zoo's website said: "Discover the predators of the animal kingdom, and their prey in our brand new guided tour.

"You'll be the first visitors in the zoo as you board our electric tour bus and enjoy 90 minutes of the zoo all to yourself.

"Come face to face with some of the zoo's most iconic animals, away from the crowds, including our family of Sumatran tigers.

"Your expert tour guides will be on hand to share fascinating facts about some of nature's most effective hunters."

News.title: Prince William launches £250K fund for village
News.content:
The Prince of Wales is launching a new regeneration fund to support Princetown, the isolated Dartmoor community facing an uncertain future following the closure of Dartmoor Prison.

The Princetown Community Fund will make at least Â£250,000 available to locally led social, economic and environmental projects.

Grants of between Â£500 and Â£40,000 will be distributed through Devon Communities Together, which will also provide support to groups applying for funding.

The fund follows William's decision to stop personally benefiting from the Â£1.5m annual rent generated by Dartmoor Prison, with the funding redirected into the local community.

News.title: US Open final LIVE: Zverev crushes Shelton in tiebreak to move set away from title
News.content:
'I'm the most confident I've ever been in my game' - Shelton ahead of Zverev final

Home hope Ben Shelton bids to make US Open history as the American faces Alexander Zverev in the New York final.

The 23-year-old Shelton is aiming to end the 23-year wait for an American man to triumph at the US Open, since Andy Roddick lifted the title in 2003. Shelton is also aiming to became the first Black man to win the US Open since Arthur Ashe since 1968, and will do so in the stadium that is named after the iconic Ashe.

Standing in Shelton’s way is the top seed Zverev, who is bidding to become a two-time grand slam champion in the season where the German made his breakthrough at the age of 29 at the French Open. Zverev, who was also beaten by Jannik Sinner in the Wimbledon final in July, has won all five of his previous matches with Shelton.

The American will have the home support this time, however, after an inspired late-night victory over defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in the quarter-finals. After returning to beat his good friend Frances Tiafoe in the semi-finals on Friday, Shelton is now just one win away from writing his name in the record books.

A Brazilian Supreme Court justice on Sunday unsealed an investigation into the production of a film about former President Jair Bolsonaro, pointing in his decision to suspicions the movie’s financing had ties to a criminal network.

The suspicions laid out in Justice Flávio Dino’s decision may complicate matters further for Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, only weeks before October’s national elections in which he will challenge President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

Sen. Bolsonaro, the ex-leader's eldest son, is under investigation for corruption, money laundering and tax evasion for receiving millions of dollars from a disgraced banker to finance the biopic about his father, titled “Dark Horse.”

Dino, a Lula appointee who oversees one of the investigations into the film, said the hypothesis that there existed a sophisticated scheme for the allocation and diversion of public funds involving federal congressional budget amendments and the Sao Paulo city government had strengthened.

On Thursday, Brazil’s federal police targeted federal lawmaker and Bolsonaro ally Mário Frias in an operation.

Police seized documents from the film’s production company and from Frias, who sent about 2 million reais ($400,000) to a nonprofit linked to the film. They suspect a criminal organization channeled funds to companies that were irregularly subcontracted, without evidence that the contracted services were provided.

The judge said Sunday that there were strong indications that Frias, who held a cabinet position during Bolsonaro’s term, played a central role within the alleged criminal network.

The network may also have links to the criminal organization the First Command of the Capital, or PCC, Dino said. U.S. President Donald Trump declared the group a foreign terrorist organization earlier this year.

Frias denies wrongdoing. “I never allocated any congressional budget funds to finance or benefice the production of the film in any way,” Frias said Sunday in a post. He had previously described Thursday’s operation as a “smoke screen.”

Brazil’s Supreme Court has been embroiled in turmoil these past few weeks, with suspicions of graft, political bias and police interference looming over several of its members.

Dino recently clashed with Justice André Mendonca, who was appointed by Bolsonaro. On Tuesday, Mendonca removed federal police Director-General Andrei Rodrigues and the force’s intelligence director, Leandro Almada, for allegedly leading illegal investigations against Mendonca.

Then on Wednesday, Dino overruled his colleague and restored the two senior police officials to their posts. Chief-Justice Edson Fachin later suspended their opposing decisions.

The chaos gripping the court stems from the collapse of Banco Master, a mid-sized bank worth up to $16 billion in assets, which was shut down last November after a sprawling investigation into a fraud scheme involving billions of reais.

Banco Master’s former CEO Daniel Vorcaro was arrested earlier this year. It has since emerged that he had links with many high-ranking politicians – including Sen. Bolsonaro – but also several Supreme Court justices, including Alexandre de Moraes who oversaw the case in which Jair Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years in prison for attempting a coup.

News.title: Man United v Man City LIVE: United anticipate apology for Erling Haaland’s controversial derby winner
News.content:
United vs City - Maresca faces first Manchester derby

Manchester City won a controversy-laden derby against Manchester United at Old Trafford thanks to Erling Haaland’s goal being allowed to stand amid questions of offside following a length VAR check, while Phil Foden was also sent off for kicking Bruno Fernandes in the stomach.

With 23 minutes on the clock, Foden and Man United skipper Fernandes tangled to leave the former on the floor, on top of the ball. The Portuguese then appeared to try and kick the ball but caught the England international in the back instead, prompting a moment of fury from Foden as he kicked out with both feet and contacted Fernandes in the stomach, causing referee Michael Oliver to dish out a straight red card.

Just after the hour mark, Haaland expertly finished Josko Gvardiol’s deflected cross at the back post, with the goal initially ruled out for offside. But, after a long VAR check, the goal was awarded, with Haaland narrowly onside thanks to Patrick Dorgu’s outstretched foot and the offside Enzo Fernandez not having touched the ball with his attempted diving header – and somehow being deemed not to be impacting play with his effort. City then held on for victory despite a late United onslaught

That was the in-game drama at Old Trafford but, before kick-off, United fans protested against the club’s ownership in response to the season ticketing “fiasco” that resulted in 685 ticket bans. Fans gathered near the Bishops Blaize pub near Old Trafford to protest both the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe, with chants directed at both parties.

Alexander Zverev faced jeers from the partisan US Open crowd due to the slow pace of his service play as he faced home favourite Ben Shelton in the men’s singles final.

Chair umpire Marijana Veljovic had to remind the crowd to not make noise between the first and second serves after there were groans when Zverev aborted a ball toss on 3-3, 40-40 in the second set.

German world No 2 Zverev’s incessant bouncing of the ball before his serve was a talking point before the final after his semi-final opponent Karen Khachanov complained about the time he would take during serves.

“The way he bounces the ball, look, it annoys not only me, of course, a lot of players, because it takes so much time,” Khachanov said after Zverev was given a time violation during the match.

“At the end of the day, if it’s within the rules with the time between points, I cannot say anything against that,” Khachanov added. “If he extends the time, then he gets a time violation, so it’s as simple as that.”

Shelton, playing in his first grand slam final, appeared to be getting irritated by the pace of Zverev’s play after the French Open champion and Wimbledon runner-up took the first set on Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Zverev had spent 19 hours and 38 minutes on court during his run to a second US Open final. According to Sky Sports, if Zverev then spent 10 seconds bouncing the ball before each serve, he would have spent two hours and 30 minutes of the tournament bouncing the ball.

Speaking after his semi-final, Zverev insisted it is not a deliberate ploy. He said: “I have no idea why. I’m not doing it on purpose. I saw a stat, like, I’d bounced it 12,000 times or something like that. That’s quite funny.”

Practical Magic 2 has claimed the top spot at the North American box office, almost three decades after its predecessor grew from a modest theatrical release into an enduring cult favourite.

The Warner Bros sequel, starring Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman, grossed an estimated $30 million across 4,146 cinemas, according to figures released on Sunday by Rentrak. Its arrival ended a six-week reign at the summit for Spider-Man: Brand New Day.

The opening weekend landed at the lower end of Warner Bros’ projected $30 million to $35 million range. Directed by Susanne Bier, the feature carried a reported $75 million production budget.

Practical Magic 2 reunites Bullock and Kidman as sisters Sally and Gillian Owens, members of a witch family haunted by a curse on their romantic lives. The sequel sees them attempting to break the curse permanently while introducing a younger generation played by Joey King and Maisie Williams. Lee Pace also joins the cast.

open image in gallery Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock mine nostalgia in 'Practical Magic 2' ( Warner Bros. Pictures )

Adapted from author Alice Hoffman’s work, the film arrives 28 years after the original 1998 release. That initial entry took $46 million domestically before gradually building a devoted following via home video, streaming platforms and social media.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day fell to second place with $8.4 million, representing a 54 per cent drop on the previous weekend. The Sony and Marvel blockbuster starring Tom Holland has now grossed roughly $935.2 million domestically.

That total leaves the film within about $1.4 million of the $936.6 million domestic record set by 2015’s Star Wars: Episode VII — The Force Awakens for the top spot on the all-time chart.

Christopher Nolan’s mythic epic The Odyssey took third place with $7 million in its ninth weekend. The Universal Pictures release, starring Matt Damon as Odysseus, has now crossed $600 million in North America.

The film has also overtaken 2015’s Jurassic World to become Universal’s highest-grossing global release in studio history.

open image in gallery Matt Damon and Zendaya in 'The Odyssey' ( Universal Pictures )

Angel Studios' action-comedy Runner opened fourth with $6.7 million. Directed by Scott Waugh across more than 2,500 locations, it stars Alan Ritchson as an ex-soldier pairing up with an unexpected partner, played by Owen Wilson, to transport a human organ while being pursued by a ruthless cartel.

Ketchup Entertainment’s Coyote vs. Acme finished fifth, taking $6.2 million in its third weekend to reach a domestic total of roughly $47.8 million.

Buddy finished sixth with $3.5 million for a $21.3 million total, while Sony’s Insidious: Out of the Further took seventh with $3.4 million, reaching roughly $60.5 million after four weeks.

South Korean sci-fi thriller Hope opened eighth with $3.3 million from 1,560 locations. Directed by Na Hong-jin and starring Hwang Jung-min, Zo In-sung and Hoyeon, it focuses on a remote village thrown into chaos by a mysterious creature.

Historical action drama The Uprising, directed by Paul Greengrass and starring Andrew Garfield, opened ninth with $3.25 million, depicting a commoners' revolt against King Richard II in medieval England. By Any Means rounded out the top 10 with $2.5 million in its second weekend.

open image in gallery Thomasin McKenzie, left, Jamie Bell and Andrew Garfield, right, in a scene from "The Uprising" ( AP )

With final domestic figures being released Monday, this list factors in the estimated ticket sales for Friday through Sunday at U.S. and Canadian theaters, according to Rentrak:

1. “Practical Magic 2,” $30 million.

2. “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” $8.4 million.

3. “The Odyssey,” $7 million.

4. “Runner,” $6.7 million.

5. “Coyote vs. Acme,” $6.2 million.

6. “Buddy,” $3.5 million.

7. “Insidious: Out of the Further,” $3.4 million.

8. “Hope,” $3.3 million.

9. “The Uprising,” $3.25 million.

10. “By Any Means,” $2.5 million.

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca believes Bruno Fernandes should have been sent off alongside Phil Foden in the first half of his side’s 1-0 win in the Manchester derby.

Foden was given a straight red card for lashing out at Fernandes with a wild kick in the 23rd minute after the Manchester United captain had fouled him.

Fernandes also appeared to aim another kick at Foden’s back after the initial foul, sparking the reaction from the City man that eventually got him sent off.

open image in gallery Bruno Fernandes went down theatrically as Phil Foden kicked out ( Reuters )

However, Fernandes received no punishment for the foul or the second kick, and VAR backed up the original decision made by referee Michael Oliver, with official Matt Donohue confirming: “That looks like a clear red card to me. Looks to be a secondary movement.”

Speaking on Sky Sports, commentator Gary Neville said that he was “surprised that Fernandes has got away without a booking”, while former United midfielder Roy Keane said that the Portuguese “is the one who is violent here”.

And City boss Maresca was also clearly confused by the decision, suggesting that Fernandes should also have seen red if Foden did.

“It can be a red card [for Phil Foden], but I think in the same action it can be a red card for Bruno [Fernandes], in the same action,” explained the City manager. “So, anyway... It is what it is. Red card for us. We won,” he added.

The sending off did not impact the result negatively for City in the end as the 10 men earned a memorable victory on the road, though Erling Haaland’s winning goal was another contentious decision on a dramatic afternoon at Old Trafford.

The result leaves City second in the Premier League after four games, with themselves and Arsenal the only two teams to hold a 100 percent winning record so far.

Maresca’s side host Norwich City in the League Cup in their next game on Thursday, before facing Sunderland at the Etihad on Sunday, 20 September in the final game before the international break.

A Republican congressman from Wisconsin said he had to swim to safety after a plane he was traveling in made an emergency landing in a lake late Saturday.

U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany says he was returning from the La Crosse County Lincoln Day Dinner when the light aircraft lost power as it approached Wausau Downtown Airport. The pilot made an emergency landing in Lake Wausau. They both ended up in the water and swam to safety.

"After landing, we called 911. As the plane began to submerge, we exited the aircraft and swam to a shallow area, where we waited until emergency responders reached us by boat," he wrote on X.

The Marathon County Sheriff's Office said in a statement that the emergency landing happened just before 9 p.m. Saturday. Tiffany and the pilot, Leonard Boltz, got out of the plane and called 911. They were rescued by emergency responders in a fire department airboat just after 9 p.m.

Both men were taken to a nearby hospital, where they were treated for minor injuries and released. Tiffany suffered a cut above his right eye that required stitches, his campaign said in an emailed statement.

A no-wake buoy was placed near the plane, which remained in the lake, and boaters were being asked to avoid the area until the plane can be removed, the sheriff's office said. A Federal Aviation Administration spokesperson said the agency would investigate the incident. A National Transportation Safety Board spokesperson said that agency is waiting for the FAA to assess the plane as to whether the damage was substantial enough for it to get involved.

Tiffany is running for governor on the Republican ticket in Wisconsin and has been endorsed by President Donald Trump.

David Crowley, the Democratic candidate, wished Tiffany a “quick recovery” in a post on X and lauded the “heroism of the pilot.”

The plane Tiffany was traveling in was a single-engine, four-seat Beechcraft Bonanza aircraft.

As the fans disappeared from Old Trafford, so did plenty of optimism for the upcoming season. With just four points from the opening four games, it’s beginning to look like the same old story once again for Manchester United.

The nature of a derby game means that sometimes a team can’t learn many lessons, whatever the result. Unfortunately for Michael Carrick, that was not the case today as his side delivered a dismal performance to lose 1-0 to 10-man Manchester City.

United were on the end of a controversial VAR decision as Erling Haaland gave his side a memorable win at Old Trafford, but while the refereeing will dominate the headlines in the immediate aftermath, it was a poor outing from the hosts.

Much has been made of the defensive frailties in Michael Carrick’s side, and that was evident again as Haaland snuck in to steer his side into the lead on the hour mark. It was a poor goal to concede, but it threatens to mask the other glaring issue in this United side – an incoherent and under-performing attack.

open image in gallery Man United’s attackers struggled as 10-man City controlled the game after going ahead ( Reuters )

For all the talk of leaking goals far too easily, it is also true that United struggle to create chances. They are far too reliant on counter-attacking, often looking out of ideas when asked to control possession and pile pressure on teams. For all the encouraging play in midfield, there is a lack of invention and cutting edge in attack, especially if Bruno Fernandes has an off day.

It’a been a theme of the season even after just four games. Parts of the win over Ipswich were encouraging, though even then the quality of the opposition has to be considered, with a penalty and a lucky deflection helping to turn the tide of the game. There were no goals against the back five at Hull, while Bryan Mbeumo took matters into his own hands for the opener against Everton.

Barring Marcus Rashford, this is not an attack that looks to take on a man and beat him. Even when it’s worked into crossing positions there is rarely anyone to aim at, with a lack of a striker telling this afternoon before Benjamin Sesko came on. Matheus Cunha has offered little so far this term, and the false nine experiment is verging on bewildering now that Sesko is seemingly fully fit. Even set-pieces, so often a reliable weapon last season, rarely produce any real threat.

United might have thought they were blessed as Phil Foden was sent off in the first half after lashing out at Bruno Fernandes, but it felt at times like the one-man advantage worked against them. City might have offered counter-attacking opportunities if both teams had had 11 men – instead, the advantage only served to expose more shortcomings.

open image in gallery The result leaves United in 13th in the Premier League, with four points from four games ( Reuters )

The sending off left City needing to climb a mountain of sorts, though United’s defensive frailties showed once again, even with a one-man advantage. Patrick Dorgu’s poor header kicked off the move, with City working it wide before Josko Gvardiol’s deflected cross arrived at the feet of Haaland, who fired in at the back post.

United toiled in attack as they tried to find an equaliser, with their attacking play frenetic and uninspired.

The inspiration can often be provided by a moment of magic from Fernandes, or individuals such as Mbeumo’s last week. It was almost the case again as Marcus Rashford hit the post from a free-kick and Kobbie Mainoo’s long-range effort also rattled the woodwork, but there was no sustained pressure from the hosts.

United too often look toothless in attack without moments of individual quality carrying them through, and that was the case again as City eased to their first win at Old Trafford in three years.

The visitors can thank Gianluigi Donnarumma for a superb stop to deny Mbeumo in the 95th minute, but it would have been a goal that the hosts did not deserve. After 95 minutes of abject attacking, their first clear-cut chance of the game came seconds before the final whistle.

In the end, a contentious refereeing decision and a great City performance will steal the headlines, but they won’t be enough for United to hide behind this time; it won’t take many more displays like that before questions start to be asked of Michael Carrick.

News.title: Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under big pressure
News.content:
Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

It was telling that so little did City’s new head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their new head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a big team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

News.title: Redemption Sunday for Hull and Woad as Europe reclaim Solheim Cup
News.content:
The quiet but steely 22-year-old, who everyone seemed to have forgotten was a rookie, punched her fist when she held the decisive two-footer, before the customary hug with opponent Auston Kim and then being mobbed by her team.

“This was really important,” Woad said. “I mean, I was pretty disappointed and felt like I was kind of letting everyone down. Then the captain kind of spoke to me and said that I was third on [the most] birdies [made]. So I just had to trust that and that’s golf sometimes. And it ended up I got the winning putt.”

Some will claim that Woad was only the match-winner on a technicality. Carlota Ciganda in the penultimate game had not finished off her win against Jennifer Kupcho, but when Woad tapped in, the Spaniard was three up with three to go and was guaranteed a half. So the acclaim Woad received was granted. Not that anyone in the Europe camp cared.

The previous evening they had returned to their team room feeling slightly down that they did not hold the advantage, Kupcho holing a 91-footer on the 17th and a 30-footer on the 18th to deny Ciganda and Céline Boutier. And their mood was not helped when videos appeared on social media of the Americans taking crates of beer on to the bus back to their hotel. Yet that foolish scenario only offered extra incentive. “At least we’ll be the ones taking crates of beer on to our bus this evening,” Mel Reid, the assistant captain, said quite pointedly.

News.title: Lando Norris fumes at virtual safety car rules for costing him Spanish GP win
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix, the first time the race has been held at the all-new, purpose-built street circuit, the Madring. The track has developed a reputation in its short life for being a bit of a tricky one. Some have gone so far as to call it a “car killer”? Is it living up to that reputation? Probably, especially if you look at some of the lower formulae that have run on it.

It has also increasingly become the case for the Formula One cars, too. The first couple of practice sessions on Friday revealed little to worry about. As the drivers began to push, though, from final practice and qualifying, the mistakes and crashes happened. The biggest so far was Oliver Bearman but also a smaller one for Lewis Hamilton.

There will almost certainly be some kind of incident in the race, but whether we see red flags, safety cars and so on remains to be seen. A bigger and perhaps more significant question will be how much overtaking will take place on this track. The drivers are not optimistic. The theory goes that if tyre degradation is high then there will be, because you will have significant pace offsets between worn and fresh tyres. The problem is that the leaders tend not to differ to greatly from one another on strategy these days...

Perhaps George Russell, who qualified down in sixth and has little to lose, will be brave and put on a set of hard tyres to start with. Russell has work to do yet again. He was not miles off Antonelli in qualifying when it came to pace, but given how close it was in the top six, finds four cars between himself and the championship leader, who just missed out on pole to McLaren’s Lando Norris.

Norris said it was the best lap of his life and seemed to come from nowhere. He improved more than a second from Q2 to Q3 and continues his fine form in 2026. He will start alongside Antonelli with Max Verstappen in third, Lewis Hamilton in fourth and Charles Leclerc in fifth, before Russell.

News.title: Tora Bora’s last midwife struggles under Taliban rule as aid runs dry
News.content:
The small clinic, crowded with pregnant women, sits in the shadow of Tora Bora in eastern Afghanistan. Twenty-five years ago, those mountains commanded the attention of the world’s most powerful military. Roughly 15 miles from the clinic, in the Tora Bora cave complex, Osama bin Laden was believed to be hiding as American bombs rained down in the hunt for the architect of 9/11.

Today, another consequence of the West’s long entanglement with Afghanistan is playing out beneath those same mountains – in the struggle to keep mothers and babies alive.

In the baking courtyard of Gandab Kharoti health centre, dozens of women enveloped in sapphire blue burqas sit shoulder to shoulder beneath trees waiting to see Shila Ibrahimi, a 27-year-old midwife.

The women rest against walls, dusty, barefoot children play, and mothers cradle sick babies beneath folds of cloth. Some have walked for hours through the mountains to reach her.

Among them is Fawzia, 30, seven-and-a-half months pregnant with her seventh child. Suffering from headaches, she has walked for miles through the heat.

Her husband works far from the village, so she makes the journey with her children and mother-in-law, hoping the Taliban do not stop her for the “crime” of travelling without a male escort.

Under the Taliban’s morality rules, women face restrictions on travelling alone, while UN monitors have documented the regime’s morality inspectors ordering some health facilities not to treat unaccompanied women.

But enforcement varies and Fawzia says nobody challenged her on her journey here. Asked where she would give birth if the clinic closed she says: “We have nowhere else to go. We cannot afford that. We are poor.”

News.title: Springboks look like World Cup champions elect… again
News.content:
In doing so, Erasmus while still relying on his veteran performers, managed to expose some of the next generation to invaluable white heat pressure, including Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, Morne van den Berg and Cameron Hanekom, who all look to the manor born.

And the substance of the series victory is heightened by the fact it came against a regenerated and rejuvenated All Blacks side, who rediscovered their high-octane and relentless attacking identity under new coach Dave Rennie. At times the handling and precision of the All Blacks were so sumptuous that it felt like they might be in a position to level the series in Baltimore.

But the narrative of the previous two Tests continued. At key moments they were let down by their discipline and turnovers in attack to gift the Springboks’ transition ball, and their directness, backed by their power both in collisions and set piece enabled them to pick up points much more easily than their opponents.

At the end, the scoreboard ran away from the All Blacks, which was harsh on them. But one had wondered if they would be able to maintain their intensity at the end of the first half, when it took 32 phases for Will Jordan to score a try to cut the deficit to three points.

News.title: Sabalenka smashes racket and swears at cameraman after Rybakina clinches US Open
News.content:
Sabalenka and Rybankina have now played four slam finals, with the spoils evenly shared after this 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 grapple in the Apple – as a boxing promoter might have referred to it.

There is certainly something pugilistic about the way these two go toe-to-toe. The emphasis is on landing the first blow, so the rallies tend not to be particularly long: only four points out of 193 went beyond nine shots. But the precision of the ball-striking was breathtaking. At one point in the first set, Rybakina had hit eight winners to just a single unforced error – the sort of ratio to send coaches starry-eyed.

Sabalanka arrived on court in her showy jewellery – which is worth more than £300,000 for the full set, according to the manufacturers – and an orange Nike dress that put one in mind of the Dutch national football team. “Total tennis” may have been the goal, but sometimes your opponent doesn’t allow you to play. This was the case in the early stages as Rybakina – whose own yellow-and-black outfit evoked the natural warning signs of a wasp or hornet – seemed to flush every ball right out of the centre of her racket.

Sabalenka actually did a sterling job of digging herself out of trouble in her service games, saving four of five break points in the first set. But this still wasn’t enough, given that Rybakina was defending her own serve with the same serenity that characterises everything she does.

News.title: Former Geordie Guimaraes taunts Sunderland fans as Arsenal show mark of champions
News.content:
Hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

There’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

“I love those challenges,” said Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”

Arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

Kick off 8pm.

News.title: £329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on new players really does take some doing.

“Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

For Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he said. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”

Sports.title: VAR got Erling Haaland goal wrong and should not have got involved in Manchester derby controversy, says ex-ref Halsey
Sports.content:
THE “subjective” nature of VAR once again dominated a big game in the Premier League in the Manchester derby, and former Premier League referee Mark Halsey has weighed in on the debate.

Erling Haaland‘s strike on the hour was the difference between the teams, but there were a couple of grey areas surrounding the goal.



The Norwegian initially thought he was denied by the offside flag, but replays with the lines drawn from the technology actually showed Patrick Dorgu‘s foot played him on.

However, Enzo Fernandez launched himself at Josko Gvardiol‘s cross trying a diving header.



The Argentine was clearly offside, hence the flga. But he was not adjudged to have been interfering with play as he didn’t touch the ball – which was the view from VAR.

In the end, the goal stood and City held on for all three points to ensure they, alongside Arsenal, started the season with maximum points and four wins from four.

Halsey said: “We saw more controversy in the Manchester derby. Haaland has put Manchester City 1-0 up only for the assistant referee to rule the goal out as offside.

“Now when we look at it, Haaland is not offside but Fernandez is offside. When the ball comes across, he’s in an offside position.

“Being in an offside position is not an offence in itself. It only becomes an offside offence if the player involved becomes involved in active play by interfering with an opponent or making a deliberate play to play the ball.

“In my opinion, Fernandez does that. And I believe that the assistant referee was correct in flagging Fernandez as offside.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“Obviously all goals are checked. VAR have looked at it, and they have decided that the goal is onside.

“In my opinion, it’s subjective to whether you feel Fernandez is making a deliberate play for the ball, or becoming involved in an active play and interfering with defenders.

“If that’s the case, the subjectivity – VAR – should not have got involved. They should have stuck with the on-field decision of offside, which I believe was the correct call.”



It would have been hard to envisage City winning in the 23rd minute when Phil Foden was sent off for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes – something Halsey believes Michael Oliver got right.

Halsey said: “Phil Foden can have no complaints whatsoever about the red card shown to him by Michael Oliver for violent conduct. You can clearly see that while he’s on the ground, he clearly kicks Bruno Fernandes in the stomach – clear red card for violent conduct.

“Now, Bruno Fernandes was reacting to a little tap by Bruno Fernandes on his backside. It was a little tap – petulance not violence – and Bruno was lucky not to receive a yellow card.”

Sports.title: Three things we learned from Man Utd defeat to Man City as transfer issue becomes clear and Fernandes theatrics fail
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED played 70 minutes against ten men in their derby clash with Man City and still left with nothing.

A Phil Foden red card isn’t even the main talking point after the Manchester derby – it’s should Erling Haaland‘s winning goal have stood?



Even so, United played better while they were battling 11 men than they did subsequently against ten.

So what did we learn about Michael Carrick‘s troops following the derby defeat? With four points from their first four games, the landscape is changing fast at Old Trafford.



Wrong on the right

After starting all 38 last season, it took three Premier League games for left back Luke Shaw to drop like a fly this season. That cost United, with left back liability Patrick Dorgu responsible for turning attack into defence for City’s goal.



United have issues on the other side, too. Diogo Dalot was unconvincing at both ends, failing to get on the end of a perceptive pass from Bruno Fernandes and then twice playing his side into trouble with daft attempted lay-offs.

Dalot was also lazily flagged offside. Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha immediately gave him a ticking off.

This was Dalot’s 250th appearance for United and he is into his ninth season at the club. United have not had a right back who has come close to elite since Gary Neville before his crippling ankle injury in March 2007. That is almost 20 years.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Noussair Mazraoui has not convinced in either of his starts against Hull City and Sabah and Dalot wears the number two for a reason. This was additional evidence that United have to be in the market for a high-class right back, as well as a left back, next summer.



Carrick reactive, not proactive

United supporters sang Benjamin Sesko’s name to the old Andy Cole song as the Slovenian striker warmed up in the second half. Michael Carrick ignored them.

Sesko did not emerge for another 19 minutes. By that time, Erling Haaland had put City ahead and United were now chasing an equaliser, rather than an opener.



It was clear in the first half United again lacked a focal point. Carrick had 22 minutes to assess them against ten men before the interval and decided to continue with a strikerless side.

There was an argument to introduce Sesko at the interval. By abiding by the ‘give it 15 minutes’ cliche, Carrick left it too late. Haaland prodded in on the hour.

Fernandes’ theatrics fail to work in his favour

Officials almost always give Bruno Fernandes short shrift when he is on the deck but it was impossible to ignore Phil Foden’s reaction.

Fernandes was snide to boot Foden a couple of times while he was prone, provoking a rash flick and milking it.



However much Foden hurt Fernandes, it was a red card offence from Foden. Yet it did not galvanise Fernandes, whose ball-striking was sloppy and his influence not as profound as in the corresponding fixture last season.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

If anything, Fernandes seemed slightly fazed by the stick City fans gave him as he prepared to take a corner in front of them. He hit the first man.

Fernandes eventually snapped in the 78th minute when he barracked the dozy Dorgu for an errant pass.

Sports.title: Furious Michael Carrick blasts ‘staggering’ explanation given as to why Haaland winner vs Man Utd wasn’t chalked off
Sports.content:
LIVID Michael Carrick fumed at the controversial call to overturn Manchester City’s offside decision.

City talisman Erling Haaland notched his fourth Premier League goal this season after his effort rippled into the back of the net.



While the linesman drew it as offside, VAR reviewed the footage and decided to hand City the lead.

Speaking to Sky Sports in his post-match interview, Carrick blasted: “I’m confused.



“We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision.

“It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now.



“If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a STAGGERING explanation.”

The Prem was quick to release a statement explaining the decision.

They explained that VAR checked the call and determined that the Norwegian was in fact onside.

And they added that Enzo Fernandez’s offside position was irrelevant given he did not play the ball.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Carrick said: “The decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game.

“That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that.

“We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but big moments in games like that have a big impact.

“We did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game.



“We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

“We could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have.”

The Red Devils have had a rocky start to the season after a humiliating defeat by Hull in their opener.



Since then, they’ve scored seven goals, but let in five, as they slip 13th in the table.

He added: “That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to winning ways.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

United will host Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, before travelling to 18th place Fulham in a bid to climb the table.

Sports.title: Man Utd ratings: Diogo Dalot and Patrick Dorgu prove costly at the back as Kobbie Mainoo impressive in the middle
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED were handed a controversial 1-0 home defeat by ten-man Manchester City after Erling Haaland’s goal was bizarrely awarded.

Haaland looked well offside when he tapped home from Josko Gvardiol‘s crossed but it was deemed Patrick Dorgu‘s boot played him on.



Enzo Fernandez was also deemed not to have intefered despite being offside in the middle of the box, in front of Lisandro Martinez.

City had it all to do after Phil Foden was sent off for lashing out at Bruno Fernandes in the first half but held on to secure an unlikely three points.



United could and should have got a point after Bryan Mbeumo‘s poor miss in the closing stages.

Sun Sport’s Samuel Luckhurst has given his verdict on the United players at Old Trafford.

Senne Lammens – 6

Barely muddied his gloves in the first half.

Could do little about Erling Haaland’s far post finish and unconvincingly shovelled an Enzo Fernandez effort on to the post.

Diogo Dalot – 4

Could have got on the end of an early diagonal pass, a run he has made several times before without scoring.

Played himself into trouble in his own third twice and was lazily flagged offside.



Ironically, Patrick Dorgu on the other side turned attack into defence to help City score.

Harry Maguire – 5

Left one on Reyan Cherki early on and had a much different afternoon than expected after Phil Foden was dismissed.

Careless with the ball at times and did not exert his authority enough all afternoon.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Lisandro Martinez – 6

Has a better record against Erling Haaland than many think and he was on song against the Norwegian in the first half.

But Haaland broke the deadlock with Martinez not helped by Dorgu going rogue.

Patrick Dorgu – 4

Cost United with a clumsy pass that Haaland punished to put City 1-0 up.

Dorgu is dubious enough in defence and was not an asset in attack, despite extra freedom.

Like Dalot, he was casually caught offside when in a threatening position.



Youri Tielemans – 5

The early signs suggested he could struggle but City lacked a creator to grab the game by the lapels and Tielemans had more time to survey his surroundings.

Did nothing to influence the game, though.

Kobbie Mainoo – 6

Not as totemic against a much more testing midfield in the first half but grabbed the game by the lapels in the second.



Smacked the post at 0-0 and seemed set to exert his control even more but then Haaland changed the scoreboard.

Bryan Mbeumo – 5

After being on easy street against right backs in recent weeks, Mbeumo had a formidable foe in Josko Gvardiol and his wild attempt from distance just before the hour signalled how tough going he was finding it.

His weakest performance of the season.

Bruno Fernandes – 5

Snide to boot Phil Foden a couple of times but the reaction was a red card offence.

The incident did not galvanise Fernandes, who hit some poor passes and did not dominate the game as profoundly as he did in January.



Marcus Rashford – 6

Back in the starting XI and had an engrossing duel with Matheus Nunes, who marshalled the United winger impressively.



Struck the post with a precisely-hit free kick but came second best in his battle with Nunes.

Matheus Cunha – 5

Fluid on and off the ball as he knitted attacks together but United lacked a focal point, especially after Foden headed down the tunnel.

Also attempted a couple of potshots from distance and fortunate not to make way late on.
