Subs

Benjamin Sesko – 5

Came on too late when he should have come on at the interval.

Joshua Zirkzee – 5

Desperate choice of attempted game-changer.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney ‘gearing up’ for public war after ex-teammate Andy Carroll releases bombshell autobiography
Sports.content:
WAYNE ROONEY appears to be facing his own version of the Wagatha Christie saga.

But while the former footie ace’s wife Coleen faced off with fellow Wag Rebekah Vardy, Wayne appears to be gearing up for a rather public war of words with his old England teammate Andy Carroll.



In his new autobiography, Owning It, Andy alleged Wayne would invite fellow players into his room while they were on Three Lions duties around 2010 and 2011 for a beer and a cigarette.

He wrote of Wayne: “He’d be surrounded by cartons of fags, crates of lager and ­bottles of wine (which he got the hotel manager to deliver to his room), and soon his room would be full of players. No one got smashed, it was just Wazza’s way of breaking the monotony with a couple of drinks.”



But Wayne was not impressed and issued a pretty punchy statement last night, saying: “I don’t normally comment on falsehoods written about me — but I will address this one.

“Andy knows that he and I never really socialised. I bumped into him once, coincidentally, while on a holiday — but that’s about it.



“As for this ‘tale’ about me drinking on England duty, it’s a fabrication. I don’t know where the story comes from. It’s disappointing.”

But now Andy has hit back and has told pals he is puzzled that Wayne has claimed the story is made up.



A friend told me: “Andy is beyond baffled by the suggestion that he invented a story.

“He has no reason to make something like this up and stands by every word of his account.

“This is how Andy remembers the night and he won’t be bullied into changing his version simply because someone else now disputes it.

“It is his honest recollection of the events as he experienced them. He is so proud of this book.”



They added: “The manuscript was carefully assessed ahead of publishing, with the appropriate checks undertaken in line with standard publishing practice.

“The book went through all the usual editorial and legal checks before being printed.”

I can smell Wagatha 2.0 brewing.

In the immortal words of Harry Hill . . . FIGHT!



Misteeq red-hot reunion

IT was a nostalgia overload as Mis-Teeq smashed their anniversary reunion show at the on Saturday night.

In matching red outfits Alesha Dixon, Su-Elise Nash and Sabrina Washington smashed through their string of hits at Ovo Arena Wembley.

And they surprised hardcore fans by bringing their old bandmate Zena McNally to perform Why during the sold-out show.



Alesha and Co’s brilliant set was like a walk down memory lane, with the trio kicking off the performance with 2001 hit One Night Stand before singing Dance Your Cares Away, That Type Of Girl and Can’t Get It Back.

It was the encore that brought the house down, though, with 2003’s Scandalous starting a crowd singalong which made me long for a full-blown return for the group.

Please ladies, make it happen.

Sneak peak at Tim



NEXT time you pop into Mountain Warehouse, keep your eyes peeled for Timothee Chalamet.

The Hollywood actor has outed himself as a secret hiking fan after revealing he’s spent the past couple of weeks walking through the mountains in north-eastern Italy.

Timmie left his girlfriend Kylie Jenner at home and took his journalist dad Marc on the jaunt.

It’s a wise move. I can’t imagine the reality star’s trademark six-inch heels are cut out for the steep inclines.

ADELE TO PARTY WITH TRAITORS



SHE’S on the countdown to her 40th birthday and I am told Adele is going all out for the bash, which is a Traitors-themed do at a Scottish castle.

Insiders told me party-planners were currently scouting out locations across the Highlands in a bid to secure it well in advance of the big celebration in May 2028.

A source said: “Adele absolutely loves to throw a good party and she is going big for her 40th.

“The dream would be to have the party at Ardross Castle where the Traitors is filmed, but it depends whether the BBC will be booking it out for two more years, as it’s already shut off this year and next. Obviously her best friend Alan Carr owns his own castle in the Highlands now too, so that’s on the list of locations.

“The party planning is in the very early stages and at the moment, the locations are just being pulled together for Adele to make a decision.”



Adele will be getting the celebrations started early, as she’s preparing to make her acting debut later this year in Tom Ford’s new movie Cry To Heaven.

The film is set to be released in autumn and we exclusively revealed she had been working on new music for it too.

I’d love to be a fly on the wall at her birthday bash . . .

Carly’s brought to book

CARLY RAE JEPSEN has revealed she was kicked out of her book club – for telling inappropriate jokes.



The pop star, whose eighth album Day And Night is out on Friday, confessed she repeatedly mocked the romance novel she was reading with the group, which led to her fellow members getting annoyed and removing her.

Carly told the Las Culturistas podcast: “I got kicked out of a book club

“You know the type of book where it’s kind of a romance, fantasy, fairy – romantasy?

“All this anticipation is coming, she’s finally gonna get with the guy, and then he has wings, or scales or claws.

“I wanted to get it, I didn’t get it. I made some insensitive jokes.



“So my jokes don’t land. I really got kicked out.”

SIENNA SPIRO’s Great Expectation has been knocked off the top spot since Friday.

The US singer has dropped to No2, after being overtaken by summer hit Movin’ To The Sun by Hugel, Imael Angel and Ultra Nate.

Sienna can still look on the bright side as her song Die On This Hill has broken into the top ten and is at No9.

TATT’S ENOUGH FOR KELLY



KELLY OSBOURNE is learning the perils of modern dating following her split from Slipknot rocker fiancé Sid Wilson.

I spotted her getting cosy with tattoo artist Ugly North at Bon Jovi’s concert earlier this month.

But Kelly has now blocked him on Instagram after several women warned her off him.

She said: “I want to thank all the girlie girls who had my back and cared enough to bring the truth to my attention. I feel more than a little foolish . . . apparently I should’ve done my homework. I also have to look inward and ask myself why I keep leaving the door unlocked for vampires disguised as charm.”

I’d stock up on garlic and get off dating apps for a while, Kelly.



Duet? Yes we Khan

CHAKA KHAN brought some girl power to the stage at Radio 2 In The Park as she belted out her 1978 hit I’m Every Woman with Alexandra Burke.

X Factor winner Alex is currently playing the soul legend in a West End musical about her life and the duet invitation was a thumbs-up from Chaka.

A source said: “Chaka loves what Alexandra has done with the musical and wanted her up on stage with her.



“It was one of the best performances of the weekend and the crowd absolutely loved it.”

Meanwhile, Sharleen Spiteri gave Texas fans a real treat at the BBC’s three-day outdoor music festival in Stirling.

Their six-song set kicked off with Black Eyed Boy and ended with the brilliant Inner Smile, with Sharleen whipping up the crowd.

Say What You Want . . . but the Scottish group sure know how to put on a show.

Sports.title: Gary Neville trolls Noel Gallagher live on Sky Sports in Manchester derby… but made to eat his words within minutes
Sports.content:
GARY NEVILLE couldn’t resist a trolling pun when Noel Gallagher was forced to cut his celebration short for Erling Haaland’s goal against Man United.

Initially, the back-post effort was ruled offside, meaning the Oasis member had to stop his wild celebrations in his tracks.



Neville remarked: “Don’t look back in anger,” referencing Oasis’ hit song that turned 30 years old this year.

However, after a lengthy VAR review, Haaland’s goal then stood and actually proved to be the winner.



Once the decision was announced, Gallagher resumed his celebrations – with even more vigour.



Humble Neville then chimed in: “He’s not looking back in anger anymore.”

City pulled off the massive win in boss Enzo Maresca‘s first-ever Manchester derby – and they did it with ten men.

Phil Foden saw red after a clash with Bruno Fernandes after just 23 minutes.

United legend Roy Keane, working as a pundit, felt the red card was harsh on Foden as Fernandes, in his view, acted as the instigator.



But Haaland’s goal has caused the most point of confusion and debate.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Enzo Fernandez clearly goes for the ball in an offside position, but the laws of the game are more focused on whether he impacts or influences anyone defending the eventual goal.

It appears as though Senne Lammens stutters going across his goal as the Argentine dives for the ball.

Lisandro Martinez said he was drawn into marking Fernandez too and was waiting to hear an explanation from officials of why the goal stood.

Both Keane and former Manchester City star Micah Richards both agreed the goal shouldn’t have stood with Neville insisting on commentary he didn’t believe it was a goal, either.

Sports.title: Man Utd 0 Man City 1: Erling Haaland’s hugely controversial winner the difference after Foden sent off for lashing out
Sports.content:
THERE are games that define a season and a team.

Matches that bring a sense of belief and conviction, results that are bigger than the points they earn.



Famously, Arsenal’s “Invincibles” looked back with their 10-man goalless draw at Old Trafford at the start of that remarkable campaign.

And if Enzo Maresca and City go on to lift the crown in May, this against the odds win with 10 men for more than an hour will go down in Etihad folklore.



When Phil Foden responded to a boot in the backside from Bruno Fernandes by lashing out with his leg, catching the United skipper amidships, City’s hopes looked to be following him down the tunnel.

But inspired by Elliot Anderson and half-time substitute Iliman Ndiaye, twice rescued by the uprights which denied Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo, and with Enzo Fernandez’s tricks and wiles making him an instant City hero, the men in light blue resisted and resisted.

And then, as so often, they struck, through the man who does exactly that, time and again.

Erling Haaland’s back-post finish, his fourth in as many Prem games was initially ruled out before being chalked ON by the Stockley Park video crew.

While it was a smash and grab win, the City players lining up to salute their fans after Gigi Donnarumma’s vital last-gasp save from Bryan Mbeumo, it was a remarkable against the odds triumph.

One that deserved the celebrations from the travelling supporters that will continue for months, joyfully reminding the swiftly emptying stadium of their team’s numerical disadvantage.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

For Michael Carrick, reality bites, hard.

Nine months after the derby win that kickstarted his reign, just four games into the season, United are eight points adrift of their neighbours.

It will hurt, all the more as when Foden was sent off mid-way through the opening period, the stars could not have been more aligned in United’s favour.

Two early meaty crunches by Anderson, the first on Marcus Rashford and the next to dump Mbeumo, suggested Maresca had told his side there could be no repeat of the callow display on their last visit, under Pep Guardiola.



In the event, Foden took the message too literally.

Not that there was too much for either set of fans to talk about in the initial stages – all hustle and bustle but precious little football.

All of which then got overtaken as Foden’s nightmare in front of England boss Thomas Tuchel unfolded.

Foden every right to be furious when he was caught in position out wide on the touchline, fouled to go to ground before receiving a sly kick from the United skipper.



But there was no justification for the flailing boot which caught Bruno flush in his groin.

Michael Oliver could not produce the red card quickly enough but he was right – although City will doubtless, and with some cause, argue both sides should have been down to 10.

The VAR, unable to recommend a yellow for the United man, merely confirmed Oliver’s immediate assessment.

Fernandes was public enemy No1 as far as the City fans were concerned – and United smelled opportunity.



Creating chances, though, remained at a premium.

Donnarumma was smartly off his line to grab the ball from Rashford’s toes but Anderson was a man possessed, plugging every gap.

United, though, were so close in the final minute of the half, after Enzo’s wild challenge sent Youri Tielemans spinning through the air.

Rashford took responsibility, arcing over the wall and towards the corner, Donnarumma nowhere near the ball as it cannoned back off his right-hand upright.



Maresca, booked for protesting after Enzo went down in the United box on the break, made the first change, Ndiaye replacing Rayan Cherki.

It was to prove an inspired call, with Ndiaye terrific – although after the woodwork, again, foiled the home side soon after the restart.

Diogo Dalot’s ball inside was touched on by Bruno for Mainoo to measure a 25-yarder that curved away from Donnarumma’s grasp but once again came back into play off the upright.



When Mainoo’s determined run ended with Rashford’s low strike deflected into the side-netting, City looked ragged and on the rack.

United kept coming, Mateus Cunha spinning into space before flashing narrowly wide from the edge of the box.

Then, from nowhere – after what seemed a pointless VAR check when the flag went up as the ball hit the net – Haaland stole in to score.

It started with a casual error from Patrick Dorgu, with City, through Ndiaye and Antoine Semenyo, combining to find Gvardiol on the left.

Enzo was clearly offside as he went for the ball and Haaland also appeared to be in front of the last defender.



But the semi-automated technology showed the Norwegian was onside because of Dorgu’s foot, that Fernandez had both made no contact and was not interfering with Lisandro Martinez and – at least two minutes after everything had stopped – the goal should count.

Even City seemed surprised and now they really had something to hold onto.

Indeed, had Lammens not got just enough of a touch to flick Enzo’s strike against his left-hand post and away, United, now with Benjamin Sesko on, might have folded.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Instead, they came again. Donnarumma saved from Bruno, Mbeumo flicked a header wide, although Haaland was a whisker away from guiding Enzo’s free-kick inside rather than outside the frame of the goal.

Tempers fraying, Maguire booked for his furious reaction to Enzo’s yellow carded dive inside the box, before it ended with Donnarumma diverting Mbeumo’s effort behind. Astonishing stuff.

Sports.title: Premier League release statement on Erling Haaland goal with fans convinced offside rule not applied correctly
Sports.content:
THE Premier League was forced to make a statement to explain how Erling Haaland’s controversial goal was ruled onside in the Manchester derby.

The City striker bundled the ball into the back of the net on the hour mark, before it was quickly ruled offside.



Soon after, VAR reviewed the footage and overturned the offside call – leaving viewers and Gary Neville on Sky Sports comms stunned.

Haaland initially appeared to be well offside, while Enzo Fernandez was also offside in the middle of the box and appeared to be obstructing United defender Lisandro Martinez.



But the Prem statement read: “VAR checked the referee’s call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded.

“The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn’t play the ball.”

However, there was confusion as the Premier League rules stipulate that a player will be penalised if they prevent an opponent from playing or being able to play the ball by clearly obstructing the opponent’s line of vision.

They will also be punished for challenging an opponent for the ball or blatantly trying to play a ball which is close when this action impedes on an opponent – which it appeared Fernandez clearly did.

Former Man United skipper Neville told Sky Sports that he thinks Pro Ref will be making an apology.

He said: “When they look back on this, they will recognise they got this wrong. The question is does Fernandez, who is offside, stop Martinez getting the ball? He does.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Fans were equally shocked. One wrote on X: “Man United are getting robbed in broad daylight because how is Enzo and Haaland not offside?”

Another said: “Clearest offside I’ve seen… embarrassingly bad.”

It came after Neville had trolled Noel Gallagher live on TV for celebrating the goal – before he was forced to backtrack.

But it was not the only controversy of the game after Phil Foden was shown a red card after 23 minutes.



Roy Keane came out in defence of the City star and said he thought it wasn’t violent conduct.

Haaland’s strike was the only goal of the game and handed Enzo Maresca’s side the three points to go level with Arsenal after four wins in four games.

Michael Carrick, meanwhile, has only picked up four points this season, with United lying in 13th.

The Red Devils will host Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday before travelling to Fulham at the weekend.



City will greet Norwich at the Etihad on Thursday as they look to defend their Carabao success.

They will stay put for their Prem meeting versus Sunderland.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca makes Bruno Fernandes claim as Manchester derby descends into war of words
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca makes Bruno Fernandes claim as Manchester derby descends into war of words

Manchester City came out on top in Sunday's derby courtesy of an Erling Haaland goal but the main talking points after the game revolved around VAR and Phil Foden's red card

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca saw his side win an action-packed Manchester derby (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

City boss Enzo Maresca claimed Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes should have been sent off along with Phil Foden during a brutal encounter at Old Trafford, as the derby descended into a war of words.

‌



It was a heroic victory for City who had Foden sent off after just 23 minutes as he lashed out at Fernandez who had kicked him but United could not find a way back even against ten men.

‌



Maresca praised his players before admitting referee Michael Oliver was right to send off Foden - but said Fernandes should have gone as well.

‌



The Italian said: “The decision can be a red card for Foden, but in the same action, it can be a red card for Bruno because he also kicks Phil.

“The goal was right to stand. I spoke to the fourth official and he told me it was onside. But it was a fantastic win. It’s great for spirit and togetherness.”

Lisandro Martinez insisted Manchester City ’s win was an “injustice”, with the United defender incensed because City midfielder Enzo Fernandez was not flagged offside before the ball reached Erling Haaland, who scored the winning goal

.Martinez said: “He was offside. I went to [Enzo Fernandez] because he was there in front of me, and that’s why Haaland was free [to score].

‌



“I want to be calm, I want to control myself but it’s so hard. Every season they come to our club, they explain the rules for an hour and a half, and they look so confident.

“And then you have five or six people making this mistake. It’s unacceptable because this is the best league in the world. And now we have to go home with this injustice.”

View 2 Images Phil Foden was shown a red card for lashing out at Bruno Fernandes

United boss Michael Carrick was incensed by the goal being allowed to stand. Fernandez was clearly in an offside position with the accusation that he stopped Martinez from clearing the ball before it reached Haaland.

Carrick said: “I'm confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It's more worrying if that's the interpretation of football now.

“If that's the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that's really worrying for me. It's a staggering explanation.”

Carrick also said he understood the pre-match protests from fans outside Old Trafford as they are angry at club decisions on season tickets and the way it is being run generally. He added: “I definitely appreciate the supporters. We want to make them happy - they are everything for this football club. I feel for them today.”

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes' lamentable behaviour in Phil Foden incident not befitting of Man Utd captain
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes' lamentable behaviour in Phil Foden incident not befitting of Man Utd captain

Bruno Fernandes' behaviour made sure Phil Foden was shown the red card in the Manchester derby and the United captain then went missing against City's 10 men

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes got Phil Foden sent off (Image: Shaun Brooks/Getty Images)

First things first, you will be glad to know Bruno Fernandes is okay. Bet you were worried for him after that vicious attack from well-known hard man Phil Foden.

‌



“More of a flick or a gesture,” said Wayne Rooney. And he was absolutely spot-on. It was an angry gesture, for sure. But that was about it.

‌



Fernandes writhed around as though he had been kung fu-kicked in the solar plexus, and Michael Oliver bought it in the same way that Foden had bought it. Both fell for Fernandes's dark arts.

‌



“He’s helped his team-mates there,” remarked Gary Neville, unsurprisingly. Fernandes might have helped his team-mates but it was still a pretty lousy cameo. Yes, he is probably in a majority when it comes to trying to get opponents sent off, but it is still lousy.

This is the Professional Footballers Association Player of the Year, don’t forget. Is it too idealistic to think a player might NOT try to get a fellow pro dismissed and banned? Yes, of course it is. Enzo Fernandez was at it later, trying to get Kobbie Mainoo and Harry Maguire in trouble. It is lamentable. But it is not going to change.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Anyway, the harsh dismissal of Foden was the sole responsibility of Oliver, who, incidentally, had more touches of the ball than Haaland. Matthew Donohue, the VAR, was never going to tell the country’s top-billed referee that he might have got it wrong.

But he was happy to award a goal to Erling Haaland after lengthy deliberation. There will be many out there who still don’t understand how Haaland’s effort - well-taken, to be fair - was allowed to stand.

Surely Enzo Fernandez, clearly offside, was having an impact on proceedings. So, although they will be losing Foden for three games, City cannot really complain about the officiating.

‌



View 3 Images Phil Foden was shocked by the red card (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images)

And as it happened, the red card ended up having a negligible effect on proceedings. If anything, it might have somehow made United a touch complacent - although considering their current status, that would be hard to believe.

This was a real setback for Michael Carrick. He was unable to galvanise his team, unable to elicit any sort of reaction after Haaland’s controversial goal.

‌



Yes, Bryan Mbeumo might have rescued a point in added time but the lack of imagination in United ranks was startling.

Perhaps Fernandes felt guilty for getting Foden sent off. It was a brutal result for Carrick and United, who are already eight points behind City and Arsenal.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick's honeymoon is over (Image: Shaun Brooks - CameraSport via Getty Images)

‌



At the final whistle, Carrick turned to shake Enzo Maresca’s hand, only to find the City manager was already in front of the visiting fans, punching the air. And the Italian did not seem to seek out Carrick after he had gone around each of his City players, giving them a hug.

It left the United boss to walk from the field on his own, head down, no doubt considering the possible injustice of the winner but, more than likely, considering the size of the challenge ahead.

That golden interim period seems a long, long time ago.

Sports.title: Man Utd sent painful reminder in Manchester derby defeat as Enzo Maresca gets huge boost
Sports.content:
Man Utd sent painful reminder in Manchester derby defeat as Enzo Maresca gets huge boost

MANCHESTER UNITED 0-1 MANCHESTER CITY: Erling Haaland scored the goal to settle a derby which will be remembered for its controversies rather than the action on the pitch between two great rivals

View 3 Images Erling Haaland gave 10-man Manchester City victory in the derby (Image: Getty Images)

The chant from the away end was pretty damning. “We’ve only got 10 men.”

‌



Manchester City had one player less than United for more than an hour and still beat their great rivals on their own patch. That only serves to highlight the gap between the two Manchester giants. It was no wonder that, at the final whistle, loud boos rang around Old Trafford because the United faithful were so fed-up.

‌



The game was shrouded in controversy from the moment Phil Foden was sent off after just 23 minutes after lashing out at United captain Bruno Fernandes. Even City’s goal did not feel right. Erling Haaland smashed the ball in the net but this was all about whether Enzo Fernandez was interfering with play and stopped Lisandro Martinez playing the ball.

‌



Fernandez was miles offside but was deemed not to be interfering with play. The whole of the football world felt as if the officials, referee Michael Oliver and the VAR team, got it wrong. But only their decision counts.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



And yet, let’s be clear, even with a big slice of fortune, you still cannot lose at home to your neighbours when they only had ten men. United hit the woodwork twice, Bryan Mbeumo was denied by Gianluigi Donnarumma in the 95th minute.

But United were simply not good enough. Just lumping the ball into the box in desperation. They could not find a way through because they lacked quality and guile.

This was the fixture last season which proved to be Michael Carrick’s starting point. Carrick was brought in as a caretaker, he beat City in his opening game and the momentum carried them into the Champions League places. But passion and legendary status gets you so far. They have made a dodgy start to the campaign, the Carrick feel good factor has ebbed away and now it feels they are back to square one.

‌



Meanwhile, City are on the up. Elliot Anderson, City’s £116m summer signing who chose the Etihad over Old Trafford, was comfortably the best player on the pitch.

View 3 Images Man United had a numerical advantage for more than an hour after Phil Foden was sent off (Image: Catherine Ivill/AMA)

Anderson was incredible in front of England boss Thomas Tuchel in the stands. Then, at the final whistle, Enzo Maresca went over to the away end - including celebrity fan Liam Gallagher - and punched the air and celebrated in style.

‌



Maresca rarely showed such passion while in charge at Chelsea but is quickly finding his feet in the impossible job taking over from Pep Guardiola. Four wins out of four. What a start. It did not look like that would be possible when Foden got his marching orders. Foden snapped and kicked out at Fernandes, who kicked him first. Why on earth Fernandes got away scot free is anyone’s guess.

But referee Oliver had no hesitation and sent off Foden who now has more red cards (one) than goals in 2026. There is no way he gets back into the England squad anytime soon.

Marcus Rashford and Robbie Mainoo both hit the woodwork either side of half time. City sent on Iliman Ndiaye for Rayan Cherki for his work rate. Ndiaye just typified City’s determination.

‌



View 3 Images Enzo Maresca has hit the ground running at City (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

The goal came after an hour. Josko Gvradiol’s cross was deflected by Patrick Dorgu who played Haaland onside. But Fernandez was yards ahead and clearly impacted on Martinez’s ability to clear the danger before the ball reached Haaland.

The officials have had a stinker. Haaland thumped into the net, celebrated and then got a second chance to celebrate when VAR allowed it to stand.

‌



United piled forward but with little imagination. Mbeumo should have scored at the death. But his wayward finishing - and a brilliant save - just typified United’s sloppiness.

This was a crash landing for United and Carrick. But it feels like lift-off for Maresca’s City.

Sports.title: Fuming Lisandro Martinez hits out at 'injustice' after controversial Man Utd decision
Sports.content:
Fuming Lisandro Martinez hits out at 'injustice' after controversial Man Utd decision

The Manchester United defender made his feelings clear when addressing Erling Haaland's winning goal, which was allowed to stand after initially being flagged for offside

View Image Lisandro Martinez was visibly fuming after the game

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez hit out at what he called an 'injustice' after Erling Haaland's opener was initially ruled offside during the Manchester derby. Martinez was positioned between Enzo Fernandez and Haaland, but the Argentine launched himself toward the ball in an attempt to meet it with a diving header.

‌



Following a lengthy VAR review, it was determined that the Manchester City striker was onside and that Fernandez, despite standing in an offside position, had not played the ball, with Martinez defending behind him. Josko Gvardiol's shot deflected off Patrick Dorgu towards the back post, where the Norwegian finished smartly.

‌



A tweet from the Premier League Match Centre said: "#MUNMCI – 59’ VAR OVERTURN. VAR checked the referee’s call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded. The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn’t play the ball."

‌



Wayne Rooney slams Manchester derby VAR call as Man Utd left furious READ MORE :

The rules state that an opponent will be penalised for interfering with play if they clearly attempt to play a nearby ball in a way that impacts an opponent, or if they make an obvious action that affects an opponent's ability to play the ball.

However, Martinez did not agree with the decision to overturn the offside call.

"I think he was offside," the Argentine told Sky Sports post match. "What I can't understand is the rules, you know? He was there, I went to him because he was in front of me that's why Haaland was free but I want to be calm now, I want to control myself.

‌



"So hard because you lost the derby, three points at home. Every time they come to our club, they explain one hour, hour and a half with the rules then after five or six people doing this kind of mistake in the PL is unacceptable. You have the best players, best teams in the world and now we have to go home with this injustice.

"For sure, it's difficult. I have two players there and I was 50/50, had to take the first guy in front. Simple as that (if Enzo isn't there goes to Haaland), let's see what they have to say, let's see, I want to hear what their decision is. Based off what? I want to hear it."

‌



United head coach Michael Carrick also slammed the decision that cost them a 1-0 defeat to City. He said: "Confused, not even confused, we've put things in place to help referees' decisions, screens, referees in an office somewhere. It's more worrying about if that's the interpretation about football.

"If we've got people in place that are meant to understand a game of football or not interfering with play or impacting an attack, throwing your body at it with a defender next to him, it's really worrying for me. It's a staggering decision. I can't understand it once I seen it then the explanation makes it worse.

"The explanation that he's not interfering with play. Incredible. It's not going to change a season, it's a major impact on the game and it's a massive game. It's a long season ahead, we've got to get back to winning football matches, that's on us, that (decision) wasn't on us today."

‌



On Sky Sports commentary, Gary Neville was baffled as the still images suggested Haaland was behind the last defender. "I'm going to need the offside law explaining to me, it's lost me," he said.

"The question is does Enzo Fernandez put off Lisandro Martinez? I think he does because he sort of hesitates. They say Haaland's onside from Dorgu's foot, from where we were didn't look the case but Dorgu's foot is deeper."

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney slams Manchester derby VAR call as Man Utd left furious
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney slams Manchester derby VAR call as Man Utd left furious

Manchester City's winning goal in the Manchester derby was given by VAR - but the decision has sparked a huge backlash among fans and pundits alike following the game

View 2 Images VAR decided Erling Haaland was onside for the only goal of the Manchester City

Wayne Rooney led the inquest into the controversial decision to allow Erling Haaland's winning goal in Sunday's Manchester derby.

‌



The Manchester City striker plundered the only goal of the game to clinch a memorable victory for Enzo Maresca's side, who played with 10 men for more than an hour after Phil Foden was shown a straight red card for aiming a kick into the midriff of Bruno Fernandes midway through the first half.

‌



Just as the debate over Foden's dismissal was dying down, VAR intervened to allow Haaland's goal on the hour mark to stand after it was originally ruled out for offside.

‌



Replays eventually showed that the striker was played onside by a touch from Patrick Dorgu - but the presence of Enzo Fernandez, who was clearly offside, attempting to reach Josko Gvardiol's cross sparked fury.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Rooney was among those who felt that Lisandro Martinez's position was influenced by Fernandez's presence, telling Match of the Day: “Surely it's offside. Martinez is impacted by Enzo's movement, and he is offside.”

Gary Neville was also less than convinced that the right outcome had been reached on commentary. The Sky Sports pundit said: “We're going to have one more look at this goal, does Fernandez put off Martinez? I do think when they look back at this they'll realise they've got it wrong.”

Neville went one further later in the game, suggesting that Manchester United were likely to receive an apology from RefPro after the on-field decision of no goal was overruled. “They're the words [a played not needing to touch the ball to be offside] that I think – emphatically – means we will see an apology from Pro Ref.

‌



View 2 Images Gary Neville was among those confused by the decision to allow Haaland's goal (Image: Sky Sports)

“There is no doubt that Enzo is attempting to play the ball and putting Lisandro Martinez off It’s a really strange one. They’ll recognise they got that wrong.”

Though Rooney and Neville are among those who felt Fernandez's movement should have been deemed as the midfielder interfering with play, the Premier League Match Centre account confirmed that VAR officials were satisfied him not playing the ball was enough to intervene.

They posted on X: “VAR checked the referee’s call of no goal for offside – and determined that Haaland was in an onside position and recommended that the goal was awarded. The VAR also deemed that while in an offside position, Fernandez didn’t play the ball.”

Sports.title: Roy Keane points finger at Bruno Fernandes over Phil Foden red card - 'I have to call it out'
Sports.content:
Roy Keane points finger at Bruno Fernandes over Phil Foden red card - 'I have to call it out'

Phil Foden was sent off in the Manchester derby following a clash with Bruno Fernandes but the Manchester United captain's antics were later questioned by Roy Keane

View 2 Images Roy Keane felt Phil Foden's red card was not warranted (Image: Sky Sports)

Roy Keane claimed Bruno Fernandes was the 'violent one' in the clash which saw Phil Foden sent off for kicking out at his rival in Sunday's Manchester derbu.

‌



The game exploded into life following a coming together between the midfielders midway through the first half with Foden being shown a straight red card by referee Michael Oliver. Foden, who had been left on the ground following a tackle, appeared to be kicked in the back by the Manchester United captain, sparking an angry response from the England star who retaliated by swinging both his feet into Fernandes' stomach.

‌



Foden was stunned at the decision before eventually leaving the field after the call was checked and verified by VAR.

‌



But the incident split opinion online given Fernandes' actions. And Keane, analysing the game for Sky Sports, suggested that Fernandes was fortunate to escape punishment after speaking out in Foden's defence.

He said: “Foden gets up and reacts obviously so he's now sent off. The strange thing is, if you look at it, so Bruno catches him, gives the foul away and gives him a little kick. Foden is sent off and I'm guessing it's classed as violent conduct.

“To me, Bruno is the one who's violent here. I have to call it out. I called Kyle Walker out a few years ago when he went down with a headbutt. Listen, we see violence, I suppose, in a different way. But I don't think that's a red card for Foden.”

Keane's former team-mate, Gary Neville, was less sympathetic to Foden on commentary, though he did go to suggest that Fernandes should have been given a yellow card.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho has his say on Michael Carrick's Man United job with 10-word verdict
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho has his say on Michael Carrick's Man United job with 10-word verdict

Jose Mourinho was recently asked about Michael Carrick and how he has been faring at the Special One's former club Manchester United

View 3 Images Jose Mourinho was ambushed by Martin Brundle during the Spanish GP grid walk (Image: Sky Sports)

Jose Mourinho heralded Michael Carrick for "doing well" as manager of Manchester United. The Special One offered his opinion while at the Spanish GP, not long after his Real Madrid side overcame Rayo Vallecano 4-1.

‌



Carrick is now the United manager, nearly eight years after the Reds sacked Mourinho. While United have endured an inconsistent start to the new campaign, Carrick's excellent impact last season saw him be handed the role full-time.

‌



Mourinho was asked to offer his thoughts on the Englishman, just before the Manchester derby between United and Manchester City kicked off. The former Chelsea boss had nothing but praise for the Englishman.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

He said: "He's doing well Michael, doing well. I'm happy with that."

The Portuguese oversaw 144 fixtures as United's boss from May 2016 to December 2018. In that period, he steered the Reds to a Community Shield, Europa League and League Cup triumph.

‌



However, following a disappointing third season at Old Trafford, he was shown the door in favour of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. Mourinho has since made his return to Real Madrid and earlier this year opened up about his spell in Manchester.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has experienced a mixed start to his first season as permanent Manchester United manager (Image: Michael Regan, Getty Images)

The 63-year-old said: "My career at Manchester United, I know it well. I also know the reason why I ended up leaving.

‌



"But as I always do, or try to do, when I leave a club I close the door and then I do not make comments. I do not analyse externally what happened.

"A door closes and another one will open. That is what happened when I left. The history stayed there, the numbers stayed there, the three medals came home and that is it."

View 3 Images Jose Mourinho has started promisingly at Real Madrid (Image: Soccrates Images, Getty Images)

‌



For Carrick, United's opening to the 2026/27 season has proved testing. It began disastrously with a shock 2-0 away loss to Hull City, but they bounced back with a 5-2 home win over Ipswich Town.

They were seconds away from overcoming Everton at Hill Dickinson, but Ainsley Maitland-Niles' 96th minute thunderbolt secured a draw for David Moyes' side.

United got back to winning ways in the Champions League by beating Azerbaijani side 4-0 at Old Trafford. Meanwhile, Mourinho's side are second in La Liga, having won four and lost one of their opening five matches.

Sports.title: Nordqvist hits back at USA ‘dig’ over Solheim course set-up
Sports.content:
Team Europe captain Anna Nordqvist was quick to shut down suggestions the Bernardus Golf course set-up had been tailored to suit the home team at the Solheim Cup.

Nordqvist's side completed a 15-13 victory over Team USA after prevailing in Sunday's singles in the Netherlands.

The scores were tied at 8-8 following the opening two days, but USA captain Angela Stanford felt her side had been at a disadvantage throughout the tournament due to the slowness of the greens.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Sunday singles from the Solheim Cup

Stanford said at her post-tournament press conference: "Europe played well. I don't think we played bad. I think we just didn't make enough putts.

"And if you listen to everything I've ever said, Europeans always putt better. I don't know why. I still don't know why. I mean, I have a good idea, but I'm not going to say it right now.

"Apparently I didn't get to know the superintendent [grounds manager] as well as I should have."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Team Europe started dancing and celebrating after their Solheim Cup win

When pressed further about whether she was referring to the green speeds being different to what she had been expecting, Stanford added: "Even when we showed up in July here, they were faster.

"And I don't think it had anything to do with the rain either. Now, saying that, it's my responsibility to get the team ready.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Team USA's Nelly Korda appeared to tell a fan to 'have some class' after playing a shot on the 16th hole at Bernardus Golf

"This is the one thing I am kicking myself is that I just didn't keep pushing, you know, we got to figure out how to hit our putts a little bit harder, which is really difficult, to change the way you putt.

"So I'm a little frustrated with myself that I didn't drive that point home."

'We're in Europe in September'

Nordqvist was a little surprised by the apparent dig at the greens when it was put to her at her own press conference.

"We're in Europe and in September. We know how the weather can be," she said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Team Europe captain Anna Nordqvist reacts to winning the Solheim Cup

"I'm not sure I believe a lot in setting up a way to fit Europe because these girls play the same golf courses week-in and week-out competing.

"We came here in July, it was a very hot and dry summer, so the course played a little bit different then.

"So if anything it was just really trying to manage firmness. But then it's obviously been raining a lot in the past couple weeks and then this week we saw a lot of rain.

"So if anything they were probably just playing a little bit softer than we all thought coming here. But that's obviously the weather, we can't control that."

Image: Anna Nordqvist proudly holds the trophy

Stanford: You don't want to take away those moments

The Americans were pictured celebrating on Saturday evening after Jennifer Kupcho had sunk two brilliant putts to snatch a late victory for the visitors and level the match at 8-8 rather than going into the final day trailing 9-7.

Sports.title: Norris calls for rule changes after 'unfair' Madrid defeat
Sports.content:
Lando Norris has called for a change to Formula 1's Virtual Safety Car rules after he lost out on victory to Kimi Antonelli at the Spanish Grand Prix.

Norris was six seconds ahead of Antonelli when a VSC (Virtual Safety Car) for Lance Stroll's stricken Aston Martin was called on Lap 15, which was a trigger point for everyone to make a pit stop as you lose less time by pitting under a VSC or Safety Car compared to normal green flag conditions.

However, Norris just passed the pit entry when the VSC came out, whereas his rivals behind could pit as they had not reached that part of the track.

The VSC only lasted two minutes, so Norris was unable to pit on the next lap as the VSC period ended just before he reached the pit entry. He pitted under green flag conditions and dropped to fifth on the track, before recovering to third by the end of the race.

"I was just unlucky. I was the only one on the whole grid to not get a pit stop and lost 20 seconds. This was out of there [the team's] control, my control. It's a rule that shouldn't define a race," Norris told Sky Sports F1.

"A race should be won by the guy who can put in the best performance. Maybe you take a risk by running long in a stint and maybe you get a Safety Car and things can help because you know that's one of the big factors.

"But for everyone to get a VSC pit stop and for me to not, it's just.. unfair. But it's happened in the past. Others have won from it, I've probably won from it in the past. I just don't think many people have lost a race win over it. It's frustrating. I don't feel that's the way you should lose."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix

Race-winner Antonelli stated he "felt bad" for Norris and the McLaren driver feels everyone should have the opportunity to pit, should a VSC be called.

"We have spoke about it in the past in drivers' briefings saying they [race control] should leave it out for at least a lap, so it's equal for everyone," he continued.

"I was the only one that lost out and I lost out on about 20 seconds of race time and that's not how it should be."

Former F1 strategist Bernie Collins on the VSC rules Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins



“I don’t think the rule needs to change. The rule is there for safety.



“There’s always a question mark on people changing tyres under a red flag but the VSC and Safety Car is there for the safety of a driver who crashed or gone off track and the marshals on track.



“Kimi Antonelli has been one of the most unlucky people with VSCs and Safety Cars. Monaco he missed two Safety Cars, Austria as well.



“It’s come around. It hurt Norris this week and will benefit him at another point.”

McLaren chief executive Zak Brown told Sky Sports F1: "They [the VSCs] were cruel today twice!

"Lando was gone, the team did a great job and the VSC came out a couple of seconds after we went by and went away a couple of seconds before we could pit.

"Nothing we could have done. Great to hear Lando's radio message to 'shrug it off'. That was our race by 20 or 25 seconds. He was dominant, he was gone. Managing, great tyre wear - a league of his own."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli admitted it wasn't the way he wanted to win and that Lando Norris deserved the Spanish GP victory

Why did Norris not stay out and pit later?

McLaren had the option to not pit Norris straight away so he could potentially build a gap to his rivals, particularly as Charles Leclerc stayed out and was holding up Antonelli.

However, McLaren team principal Andrea Stella says Norris' medium tyres were too worn and he would not have enough pace to pull away.

"We considered staying out but you have to accept the fact that now you're on relatively used medium tyres and the people behind you will be on new hards, so you're never going to open a gap on people on new hards," said Stella.

"Therefore, we kind of needed to accept that was what we should have done. And the fact that it was incredibly unfortunate. Sometimes we talk about being unlucky. I think at times that being unlucky is used for too many applications, but in this case, it's almost a mathematical definition of being unlucky."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris lost the race lead after an unlucky sequence of events which saw a missed a pitstop opportunity under a VSC, followed by a very slow stop by McLaren

Change the rules or part of racing?

Virtual Safety Cars were introduced to Formula 1 in 2015 following Jules Bianchi's tragic accident at the 2014 Japanese Grand Prix.

An indirect consequence of them is drivers drive to a delta which sees them go 30 to 40 per cent slower compared to green flag conditions.

The same rules initially apply when there's a full Safety Car, before the field gets bunched up, but it means a sporting advantage can be gained by pitting.

"It is racing and it's happened, so I can't really complain about it. I can be upset about it, but I can't really complain about it," said Norris.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli admitted he felt bad for Lando Norris on team radio as he wins the first F1 race at the Madring

"I think there are things, because we have spoken about it in the past several times, about how it can be at least covered for one lap or everyone has the opportunity to do the pit stops, or you just block the pit entry and no one can box apart from if you have a puncture or something.

"So, I think there are a few things you could do to make it more simple and more fair for everyone, but that's a bigger discussion. This is not something I can just ask for."

Norris' maiden win at the 2024 Miami Grand Prix came with the help of a Safety Car which enabled him to have a cheaper pit stop against Max Verstappen.

But he pointed out that a rule change would require all drivers to come together to agree on new regulations.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player An emotional Lando Norris slams the ending of the Virtual Safety Car, which led to him losing the Spanish Grand Prix

"I think we would all want, but there's a lot more to it. Depending on if it's raining and there's a VSC and you're on slicks, does it mean you can box or not? So it's a complicated subject," he said.

"But I think as a collection of drivers, if we all talk about it, I think everyone wants the same thing, and that's just fairness for everyone. Of course I'm complaining about it today, [but] I could benefit from it next week, next time out, and I could win because of it.

"I have to take it on the chin, but I just hope it doesn't happen to anyone again because it's just not how you should lose a race."

Sports.title: 'There's no stopping Antonelli' - Hamilton says 2026 F1 title bid is over
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton appeared to give up hope of claiming a record eighth Formula 1 title this year as he said that "there's no stopping" Kimi Antonelli following the championship leader's latest victory at the Spanish Grand Prix.

Antonelli benefitted from some good fortune at the new all-new Madring circuit to claim his eighth victory of the season, while Hamilton retired early in the race after suffering a brake-pedal issue on his Ferrari.

The victory saw Antonelli extend his lead at the top of the standings over his Mercedes team-mate George Russell to 81 points, while Hamilton fell 101 points back in third, with Norris five points further adrift in fourth.

"I think there's no stopping him and Mercedes this year," Hamilton said of his former team during a post-race interview with Sky Sports F1.

"They've done a phenomenal job and they deserve it."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Spanish Grand Prix.

While Antonelli was fortunate on Sunday as the timing of a virtual safety car enabled him to leapfrog McLaren's Lando Norris, who had appeared on course for a comfortable victory, the 20-year-old Italian has driven with supreme consistency in just his second F1 campaign.

Even with the huge lead he has built, Antonelli is insisting that he is refusing to think about a maiden title and instead focusing on maintaining a race-by-race approach.

Antonelli said: "I want to keep pushing race by race, keep delivering and keep enjoying it all the way and try to do my best every race and we will see where we end up at the end of the year."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli admitted it wasn't the way he wanted to win and that Lando Norris deserved the Spanish GP victory.

What happened to Hamilton?

Hamilton got a brilliant start to immediately jump Max Verstappen for third and then attempted an audacious dive up the inside of Norris and Antonelli.

Falling back into position as he had to back out of the move, he then nearly made contact with Verstappen, who cut the first chicane but returned to the track ahead of Hamilton.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen FUMES over Red Bull team radio after being told to give position back to Lewis Hamilton after running off track in an incident at the first corner.

Verstappen, who then passed Antonelli for second, was advised by his Red Bull team to drop back to fourth to avoid a penalty, as they felt he would be penalised by the stewards if he didn't.

Hamilton was let through into third, but shortly before that had happened, he had begun experiencing an issue with his brake pedal that left him struggling to control his car and contributed to a bump with a barrier.

"I was already basically before that, braking for Turn Five," Hamilton explained.

"I hit the brake, the car started stopping and then the pedal took a step and, all of a sudden, the car didn't decelerate as fast as it would normally.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton was forced to retire early at the Spanish Grand Prix.

"That ended up carrying a lot of speed in, and then just brushed the barrier.

"Then, after that, the pedal came back and it was fine and then I think a few corners later the pedal went long. I don't really know where that's come from."

Sports.title: Haaland scores controversial derby winner for Man City after Foden red
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland's contentious winner earned 10-man Manchester City a derby win over rivals United at Old Trafford - after Phil Foden's controversial first-half red card.

City have now joined Arsenal as Premier League title race pace setters with maximum points from four games - but their winning goal against Man Utd was widely branded as not legal. Enzo Fernandez looked to impact play when clearly in an offside position - but the goal was not ruled out.

"When they look back on this, they will recognise they got this wrong," added Neville. "We will see an apology from Pro Ref. There is no doubt that Fernandez is attempting to play the ball and putting Lisandro Martinez off."

City will feel justice was done after their job became much harder when Foden was given his marching orders earlier. A tepid first half of the 199th Manchester derby was dominated by Foden's shock sending-off.

After United captain Bruno Fernandes kicked the ball into his midriff, Foden reacted by kicking out at the Portuguese. "VAR has described it as a kick with both feet into the stomach," said Gary Neville on co-commentary.

Whether there was enough contact from Foden to cross the violent conduct threshold will be debated. Whether Fernandes should have also seen red for kicking out at Foden first will also be talked about.

Despite the man advantage, United struggled to use their dominance to full effect. They did hit the post twice through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo - but when Haaland is on the other team, City always have a chance.

That came true as he tapped home at the back post, yet the offside flag went up. The semi-automated offside technology ruled Haaland onside so the goal was given - but Fernandez being clearly offside and trying to get on the end of the same cross was also approved by VAR.

The Premier League Match Centre claimed the goal was allowed because Fernandez did not touch the ball - when the rules state that is not necessarily relevant, as impacting the play is the crucial line in the rulebook.

Image: Offside law graphic shown during coverage of Manchester United's match against Man City

While the debate over Foden red card and the Haaland winner will go on, City will see themselves as real contenders for the title after a gutsy display with 10 men.

United, who saw Bryan Mbeumo denied a late leveller by a stunning Gianluigi Donnarumma save, will ask themselves why they didn't have the quality to hurt a transitional City with an extra man.

WATCH: The two big calls

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Phil Foden was sent off after a clash with Bruno Fernandes

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player There was VAR confusion after Erling Haaland fired Man City ahead

The key moments from Old Trafford

23: RED CARD! A slow-starting derby explodes into life as Foden is sent off for kicking two feet out at Fernandes.

45+1: OFF THE POST! Man Utd struggle to fashion chances after the sending-off, but Rashford's 28-yard free-kick comes off the foot of the woodwork.

51: OFF THE POST AGAIN! Mainoo's curling effort beats Donnarumma but lands on the foot of the post.

60: GOAL! Haaland taps home at the far post but is flagged offside. After a lengthy check, Haaland is deemed onside by the semi-automated offside technology - but was Fernandez offside in the build-up?

68: OFF THE POST! Fernandez nearly doubles City's lead but his drive is tipped onto the post by Senne Lammens.

86: WIDE! Harry Maguire has United's best chance of a leveller but he nods wide at a corner.

90+5: WHAT A SAVE! Donnarumma denies Mbeumo late equaliser with amazing stop!

Man Utd furious with Haaland winner standing

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Carrick, Lisandro Martinez and Erling Haaland react to Manchester City's controversial winner against Manchester United.

Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez to Sky Sports: "I think [Fernandez] was offside. What I can't understand is the rules. He was there! I went to him because he was in front of me. That's why Haaland was free at the back.

"I want to be calm but it is so hard. Every season the officials come to our club and spend an hour explaining the rules and they look so confident with that.

"Then after, five or six people (officials) doing this kind of mistake in the Premier League is unacceptable. We have to go home with this injustice."

Man Utd head coach Michael Carrick: "The explanation I got was that he wasn't interfering with play. I just don't get it, I really don't get it.

"If that's how the rules are interpreted, that you're not interfering with play because you've thrown yourself at the ball six yards from goal and pretty much nearly touched it, which then Licha [Martinez] has to react from.

"On top of that, the [offside] was a bit dubious - where we drew the line to start with. It's worrying if that's really how the game is seen by those who are officiating it."

Maresca: Fernandes should have been sent off on top of Foden!

Man City head coach Enzo Maresca:

"I think Phil Foden's red card is a red card, but I also think that in the same action it's a red card for Bruno Fernandes.

"I reviewed the action immediately after the red card on the bench. And it's a clear red card for Phil, because it's a reaction.

"But you can also see in the same action Bruno's intention. So for me, yes, it's a red card for Phil, but it's also a red card for Bruno.

On Man City's winner: "I think Erling was onside and Enzo doesn't interfere with the action."

How the pundits reacted to Foden red card

Sports.title: Keane disagrees with Foden red card as pundits criticise Fernandes' role
Sports.content:
Roy Keane believes Phil Foden should not have been sent off in the Manchester derby and criticised Man Utd captain Bruno Fernandes' role in the Man City forward's red card.

Foden was shown a straight first-half red card in Man City's 1-0 win at Old Trafford for kicking out at Fernandes after being fouled by the Man Utd midfielder.

Speaking immediately after the incident, Sky Sports' Gary Neville said he was "surprised" Fernandes avoided any punishment after appearing to kick Foden first.

Sports.title: Trump presents Lowry with Irish Open after record 11-stroke win
Sports.content:
Shane Lowry stormed to a record 11-shot victory at the Amgen Irish Open, the home crowd favourite shooting a seven-under 63 on Sunday to finish a staggering 23 under par.

It's Lowry's seventh career title and his second Irish Open triumph, following his 2009 victory as a 22-year-old amateur, with US President Donald Trump presenting him with the trophy.

Image: President Donald Trump presents the Irish Open trophy to Shane Lowry

It's a welcome return to the winner's circle for Lowry after a series of agonising near-misses earlier this season, including a double-bogey on the final hole that cost him the Dubai Invitational by two strokes and a collapse at the Cognizant Classic, where he surrendered a three-stroke lead with three holes to play by closing with two double-bogeys.

The result was never in doubt at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg, however, as Lowry - holding a four-shot lead heading into Sunday - extended his advantage with a superb final round, while Trump watched on for the second consecutive day.

Crowds cheered Donald Trump and chanted "USA" as he told them he was removing tariffs from Irish whiskey, saying he had discussed the matter with Taoiseach Micheal Martin, minister for sport, who was also on the 18th green for the prizegiving ceremony, along with Charlie McConalogue, minister for state.

Image: Shane Lowry celebrates holing one of his birdie putts from distance during his Irish Open victory on Sunday

Lowry hails 'spectacular week' | 'I can't wait to bring trophy home'

Lowry carded eight birdies for his round and just one bogey, at the ninth, with a pair of stunning 45-foot putts at the par-three seventh and par-four 15th sending the watching crowd into a frenzy. He capped his victory in style with another long-range birdie at the last.

"This year has been quite difficult on the course for me," an emotional Lowry said after his triumph. "I've had a few chances to win, and there's been some really tough times.

"To come here this week and do this, I don't do things by half measures! I can't believe I'm standing here with that leaderboard.

"This has been the most spectacular week. It has been unreal.

"When things are not going well at this level, it's hard at home as well, but my wife's been a huge support, and my kids. I just love them so much and I'm so happy for them. I can't wait to bring a trophy home.

"My daughter is always ask me when you're going to bring a trophy home. So, yes, I'm going to bring one home."

Lowry had taken such a sizeable advantage into Sunday in large part thanks to breaking the course record with a second-round 62 on Friday,

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch highlights from Shane Lowry's record-breaking second round as he shot an eight-under 62 at the Irish Open

Jacob Skov Olesen, Lowry's closest challenger at 12 under and four shots back overnight, slipped down the leaderboard with a three-over 73. Patrick Reed's closing 64 and Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen's 63 were impressive enough to earn them second and third respectively, but Lowry had already surged clear.

Joaquin Niemann took a share of second with Reed on 12 under, with Neergaard-Petersen one back.

England's Alex Fitzpatrick was tied-seventh at nine under, a closing 64 from Sergio Garcia had him six under, on the same score as Robert MacIntyre and Matt Wallace, among others.

Jon Rahm finished four under and reigning champion Rory McIlroy rounded off a disappointing week with his best round of 67 to end his title defence one under.

McIlroy positive despite disappointing defence: 'I don't feel too far away'

McIlroy said his final round has given him some encouragement to take into next week at the BMW Championship at Wentworth, a tournament he won in 2014 and has been runner-up at three times since.

Image: Rory McIlroy finished his Irish Open defence a massive 22 shots off the pace at one under

"I've seen enough good stuff this week to give me encouragement going into next week," McIlroy said. "It's a golf course that I know well and one I've had success on.

"Obviously this wasn't the week that I wanted but, at the same time, I don't feel too far away and I feel good going into Wentworth.

"I thought I hit the ball pretty well for the most part. A couple of bad decisions off the tees yesterday but, overall, my iron play was a lot better, my wedge play was pretty good for the most part and obviously it was a struggle on the greens.

"That was the difficult thing and why I wasn't able to get myself into contention. I need a little bit of time on the putting green the next couple days and to get familiar with the greens at Wentworth again."

What's next?

The DP World Tour heads to Wentworth in Surrey next for the BMW PGA Championship.
