Sports.title: Manchester City recover from Foden red card as Haaland wins derby at United
Sports.content:
“Enzo, Enzo, Enzo, in your head” was how delirious Manchester City fans regaled Enzo Fernández, who after a star role in a memorable victory has instant cult hero status.

This 199th derby was won by Erling Haaland’s ninth strike in the fixture but the visitors’ totem was their new No 17. He was the key nuisance in a goal ruled out initially for offside and which the video assistant referee overturned when ruling that Fernández was not distracting Lisandro Martínez when Josko Gvardiol’s ball came over. The Argentinian, too, was an emblem of the fight Maresca’s team carried to Manchester United after Phil Foden appeared to turn the game the hosts’ way on 22 minutes.

As he and Bruno Fernandes challenged along City’s right the forward kicked United’s captain around the midriff and Michael Oliver showed a red card, VAR backing the referee’s instantaneous decision.

Except, down to 10 men, Enzo Maresca refused to go for the draw, by shutting the back door with a defender for a more attacking player, until late on, after Haaland’s finish – when Nico O’Reilly replaced Fernández to help see it out.

City, surely looking at film of the 2-0 defeat here in January, wanted a quick start and not to be knocked off the ball as they were in Michael Carrick’s first game in charge of United. Antoine Semenyo led the charge, losing a tussle with Diogo Dalot before recovering and dispossessing the right-back.

Toe‑to‑toe was an apt characterisation of the contest, as Carrick had Matheus Cunha switching from his false No 9 berth with Marcus Rashford on the left, and Maresca instructed Fernández to drift away from his midfield partner, Elliot Anderson, out wide.

View image in fullscreen Phil Foden remonstrates with Michael Oliver after being shown a red card. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Having Haaland galloping towards goal is a key City tactic, and when he did a sixth goal in four games beckoned but hesitation cost the striker, as Dalot went close to suffering for the same fault: he was unsure under a high ball and Semenyo, lurking, nearly profited.

Now came Foden’s folly – an act that will have infuriated Maresca and most of a City stripe. Fernandes may have made contact with a boot first, but in no way as forcefully as Foden. Maresca agreed it was a red card but also wanted one for the Portugeuse.

City were in a classic twist or stick predicament. A draw was no disaster but finding a way to take the lead would bring with it a famous – and morale‑rocketing – result. When Haaland swooped forward and bent a pass into Rayan Cherki – moved from the No 10 slot to Foden’s on the right – you saw why Maresca had decided to twist.

The Italian’s ambition was admirable – as long as United were kept out. Carrick’s team knew this, too, so composure was required, not the wildness that had Fernandes overhitting a simple cross that should have found Rashford ready to pull the trigger.

Harry Maguire’s tilt for glory from 25 yards that smacked into a colleague was also amateurish, but as the break neared Rashford’s effort was better. A 20-yard free‑kick beat the wall but not the diving Gianluigi Donnarumma’s right post.

Maresca’s move for the second half was to remove Cherki for Iliman Ndiaye’s greater pace along the right – this reinforcing his front‑foot mode. Carrick’s instructions had to be simple: go for the jugular and a precious three points that would lift them to fifth, five points behind the leaders, Arsenal. Kobbie Mainoo, anonymous so far, went as close as Rashford when letting fly: again Donnarumma was beaten and again his right post saved City, the rebound hitting the keeper.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Erling Haaland scores City’s winner, initially ruled out for offside, from a tight angle. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

United were a red rash all over those in blue. Possession was pinballed about, tackles crashed into, as when Patrick Dorgu upended Ndiaye, yet no breakthrough came.

So City’s smash-and-grab dreams were realised when Haaland found the net. The No 9 celebrated with his sit‑down zen-like posture but only after VAR overruled the initial offside call. Gvardiol’s cross from the left hit Dorgu’s foot and continued on, passing a diving Fernández (who missed contact, the subject of VAR’s scrutiny) and Martínez, and Haaland expertly rippled the net.

A twinkling Maresca riffed on a saying when speaking of the Norwegian’s import. “Happy Erling, happy life. My wife will not be happy,” he said.

Carrick replaced Youri Tielemans with Benjamin Sesko as United, desperate, required a goal. It never came – Mbeumo’s added-time effort was fierce but beaten out by Donnarumma. Haaland said of the City goalkeeper: “This wolf in goal is giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match‑winner as well.”

Fernández decorated his afternoon with an attempt that clipped Senne Lammens’s left post. At the final whistle, Maresca skipped down the touchline, the victory a triumph of his and the players’ courage.

Sports.title: Lewis Dunk’s showstopper helps five-star Brighton to rout 10-man Coventry
Sports.content:
The bare facts are bleak: Coventry City are only the second team in Premier League history to lose their first four games of the season ­without scoring a goal. “And yet …” will be the enduring message from Frank ­Lampard to his players.

And yet they have caused prob­lems for opposition teams. And yet they have already faced three of the top flight’s European contingent. And yet they are not altogether playing that badly – the Brighton goalkeeper Bart ­Verbruggen being named player of the match can attest to that. But Coventry des­perately need a point, or even a goal, to give their ­confidence a much-needed boost. It does not take long for a promoted club’s relegation fears to turn to reality.

Goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Malick Yalcouyé, Lewis Dunk – especially – and Yasin Ayari were all moments of individual brilliance. But there was also a sense of Coventry self-destruction, with no complaints from Lampard over Taiwo Awoniyi’s red card for an elbow into Maxim De Cuyper’s face, nor the penalty conceded by Bobby Thomas for Pascal Gross to score the ­visitors’ third. There are also legitimate questions to be asked of Lampard’s decision to maintain an attacking approach even after the sending off.

“It’s a difficult scoreline and it’s not easy at home,” Lampard said. “The first half was pretty good, we created some chances, better chances and we had them under a lot of pressure. Then a mistake to make it 2-0 and the red card makes it very difficult.

“It feels very difficult to take the result, but a lot of circumstances that you can reflect on and say: ‘If, and if, and if.’ We need to be honest about that – we need to take chances in this league. It’s not a nice feeling.”

The scoreline certainly lent weight to Fabian Hürzeler’s insistence that Brighton have no attacking concerns despite Danny Welbeck’s summer departure. Brighton have scored more goals and created more big chances than any other club in the Premier League this season – indeed, they have never started a top‑flight campaign with more goals.

“It’s not about having one good goalscorer,” Hürzeler said. “It’s about the flexibility of having many goalscorers and a lot of players who have this desire to score. We were very efficient today and quite ruthless at the right moments in front of goal.”

That was certainly true, beginning with a moment of mastery from ­Kostoulas to break the deadlock, when the Greek teenager showed great poise to control an aerial ball with his foot, nod it between two defenders and then fire into the bottom corner.

That Brighton were not already behind by then was thanks to ­Verbruggen, who produced two excellent saves to deny Jack Rudoni, when palming a volley and a header to safety.

Lampard publicly urged his ­players to “have belief” during the half‑time interval, but then followed two ­minutes that instantly extinguished Coventry’s hopes.

View image in fullscreen Frank Lampard endures another glum day in the Premier League with Coventry. Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

First came Brighton’s second goal, when Yalcouyé was played in behind the Coventry defence, and the Ivorian’s pace kept all at bay before calmly slotting past Carl Rushworth.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Moments later, the hosts were reduced to 10 men. At first glance, contact appeared accidental between Awoniyi and De Cuyper. But, to the refe­ree Tony Harrington’s credit, he spotted the Nigerian had led with his elbow, prompting a straight red card. To compound matters, the stadium announcer chose that period to tell fans that train cancellations meant there would be no departures from the stadium for 90 minutes after the final whistle.

Thomas’s challenge to bring down Kostoulas inside his own box was as clear a penalty as will be awarded all season and Gross duly stuck the spotkick into the bottom corner.

By the time Dunk sealed the rout with the finest strike of his career – smashed into the top corner from 35 yards – the mass exodus had already begun. It was an outrageous hit, with Dunk saying: “I shocked myself, but it was lovely.”

That was followed in injury time by another excellent finish, this time from Ayari, curled from range into the ­bottom corner.

The only other team to lose their first four Premier League games without scoring were Crystal Palace in 2017‑18. Palace finished 11th that season, but need to pull the emergency Roy Hodgson cord. ­Coventry will hope he is not required here.

Sports.title: Lauren James revels in free role as Chelsea show ‘respect’ by scoring five past Manchester United
Sports.content:
A swaggering Chelsea cast off any suggestion that they had lost the ability to kill off games, putting five goals past a worryingly lacklustre and lackadaisical Manchester United.

Sonia Bompastor, the Chelsea manager, said: “When you have the opportunity to really hurt a team, the best way to respect them is to score as many goals as you can, to create as many opportunities as you can.

“Of course, it’s never easy to see the other team or the other manager concede five goals because if I was the other team, I would be really sad. For me, showing respect to the opponent is having that desire and mentality to score as many goals as possible. That’s the difference between the great teams and the good teams.”

United’s players and fans may have preferred disrespect if that is the case. Instead, it was another bruising result for the new manager, Eva Olid, and her side after an underwhelming performance in their 2-1 defeat against London City Lionesses in the opening game of the season.

Olid needed a result to give her some breathing room and her team some confidence, having had just three weeks to get used to one another before the start of the season, and this early into a project there has to be some grace.

For their opponents this game had been talked about as something of a must‑win after the Blues were held to a 1-1 draw by Aston Villa on the opening weekend despite dominating that match.

View image in fullscreen Keira Walsh scores Chelsea’s side's second goal from the edge of the box. Photograph: James Gill/Danehouse/Getty Images

To some extent the concern over Chelsea’s profligacy did not need to be too deep. They were at their creative best against Villa and were without the injured centre-forwards Melvine Malard and Mayra Ramírez while Aggie Beever-Jones, who led the line against the Midlands side, had not scored in the Women’s Super League since September 2025. The off-target Beever-Jones was relegated to the bench for the trip to United. Instead, Lauren James and Sjoeke Nüsken worked away interchangeably up front.

The visitors were similarly fluid in other areas too, and that flexibility was super effective. Chelsea were unpredictable and James’s free‑to‑roam role put their star talent at the centre of everything.

Lucy Bronze’s marauding forward yielded the opener when she sent a looping ball over the top and Dominique Janssen should have been first to it, but the United defender misread the fall of the ball and a stalking Wieke Kaptein nipped it away from her. The Dutch midfielder squared to Nüsken who fired in from close range.

The second goal, which eluded them against Villa, arrived just over 10 minutes later. A diving header from the new recruit Andrea Medina cleared a cross whipped in from the left but the hard-working Bronze was there to meet it, clipping it into the path of Keira Walsh, who took a step and powered in from the edge of the box.

The hosts’ heads dropped, which left their manager unhappy. “In football we know anything can happen,” Olid said. “You can be losing 2-0 and can end up winning. I don’t like the heads down. Heads up and we have to continue. Everything is about confidence.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

A very brief brighter spell for United after the break was snuffed out by the visiting team and James finally got on the scoresheet after the hour, latching on to Walsh’s defence‑splitting pass and shrugging off Janssen before sending a low drive into the net.

Chelsea’s fourth goal rubbed salt in for a very wounded United side. Janssen, under no pressure, failed to respond to an ambitious burst from Kaptein and the Chelsea midfielder pickpocketed the centre-back and slipped the ball wide to the onrushing Ellie Carpenter, whose first effort was kept out by Phallon Tullis‑Joyce but her follow-up found the net.

Bronze then added to United’s misery during the final minute of added time, hammering the ball in after Walsh knocked a corner back into the melee in the six-yard box.

It became a training exercise for Chelsea and the hosts failed in their attempts to limit the damage. Things look as if they will get worse for Olid’s side before they get better, with a trip to the Emirates Stadium to play Arsenal coming up next weekend, but Olid said she will not divert from the style of football she wants the team to commit to playing.

“If you start changing, then you are never going to build what you want to build,” she said. “It’s a process. I know it’s so hard, the process, because this beginning is hard. Nobody wants to lose games, but we have to be faithful to what we want to do, because I think that long term will give us the wins.”

Sports.title: WSL roundup: Arsenal rue missed chances after draw with Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
Arsenal were left to rue 30 missed chances after dropping points in a 0-0 draw against Crystal Palace at the Emirates Stadium. The Gunners hit the target nine times and had almost 80% possession but could not convert their superiority into goals. Promoted Palace put on a resilient performance, with goalkeeper Pauline Peyraud-Magnin batting away attempts from Alessia Russo, Chloe Kelly and Mariona Caldentey to earn another clean sheet.



Brighton came from two goals down to snatch a last-minute equaliser at Birmingham City. The promoted hosts took an early lead through Oceane Hurtre, who capitalised on a lapse in concentration from Caitlin Hayes before running into the box and slotting past Chiamaka Nnadozie. Lily Crosthwaite made it two in the second half with a low driven shot across the goalkeeper, but Brighton gathered momentum when Olivia García came off the bench to close the gap in the 77th minute. As Birmingham attempted to hold on for the win, Kiko Seike raced into the box with just a few seconds remaining and made the most of a small gap between Sophie Baggaley and the near post to score.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Crystal Palace goalkeeper Pauline Peyraud-Magnin denies Emily Fox with one of a string of saves at the Emirates. Photograph: John Walton/PA

At Goodison Park, Charlton fell to a 1-0 defeat by Everton following an own goal and two red cards. After a goalless first half, things quickly went downhill for the promoted side when Ashleigh Neville saw red for a high boot which caught Ruby Mace. With 13 minutes of normal time to play, the visitors found themselves behind when Holly McNamara’s cross deflected off the leg of Leighanne Robe and into the net. In the latter stages, Charlton went down to nine players after substitute Hawa Cissoko received two yellow cards in quick succession.



Liverpool came from behind to earn a 1-1 draw against Tottenham thanks to a 60th-minute header from Aurelie Csillag. Spurs took the lead just before half-time when Signe Gaupset’s effort was deflected in off the foot of Liverpool’s Sam Kerr. The hosts levelled things up at the hour-mark after Csillag got in front of Lize Kop to head home Fuka Nagano’s cross.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo calls for lifetime bans in Saudi Pro League after Diogo Jota chants
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo said that fans who appeared to ⁠make chants referencing his former teammate Diogo Jota at Rúben Neves during a Saudi ⁠Pro League ⁠match ​should be banned for life from football stadiums.

The chants occurred on Saturday during ⁠a fixture between Al-Taawoun and Neves’s side, Al-Hilal, in Buraydah, Saudi Arabia.

Jota died last year in a car crash in Zamora, ​north-western Spain, along with ‌his brother André ‌Silva. A close friend of Jota, Neves was a ‌pallbearer at his funeral.

Footage filmed from the stands during the match and circulated on social media appeared to show supporters chanting “Jota”. The shouts attracted the attention of Neves, who pointed to his eye and ‌then up to the sky in response. Passing through the mixed zone after the game, ​Neves said: “I hope they don’t go to pray afterwards.”

In response to an Instagram post showing the footage, Ronaldo commented from his personal account. “The league must take ⁠action and punish this kind of fan behaviour,” he wrote. “This ​is no longer football, ​and there have to be limits. People ​who behave ‌like this should ​never ​be allowed to enter a stadium again.“

The game finished 6-0 to Al-Hilal, with Neves playing 75 minutes before being substituted.

Reuters has contacted Al-Taawoun and Al-Hilal for comment.

Sports.title: Rangers lay down Old Firm marker to send Celtic packing from Scottish League Cup
Sports.content:
Derek McInnes has endured a much‑scrutinised start to life at Ibrox but the Rangers manager got the old ground bouncing here as his side dominated Celtic in front of an all-blue crowd to decide the first Old Firm encounter of the season.

Against a backdrop of bouncing techno from the tannoy, Rangers fans celebrated three memorable goals in a thumping League Cup win. A brace for the captain, Dan Neil, bookended Kevin Kelsy’s second‑half finish to put Martin O’Neill’s side down with relative ease. It also showcased a nascent identity for McInnes’s side, one defined by unbending physical commitment and lots and lots of sprinting. The quality of the football may have been patchy, but the commitment was enough to get the 51,212 home fans at the top of their voices.

With away fans banned from Old Firm fixtures this season after the pitch invasion that followed a Scottish Cup tie in March, the atmosphere was always likely to be partisan, if perhaps less heated than is customary. Before the match there was a brisk trade on both Graeme Souness flags and boiled sweets. Inside the ground the Union Bears ultras unveiled a tifo showcasing the apparently resonant moment when Rangers’ Ian Ferguson grabbed Celtic’s Mike Galloway by the lapels during a clash in 1993. A deep cut of a banner, it did a good job of setting the tone for what was to follow.

McInnes said: “I’m delighted. The performance we gave today was the one required to overcome a team like Celtic. I thought the game demanded the players’ full attention and I’m delighted they’ve managed to deliver that. We’ve seen the strength of the club today and it does the players no harm to understand what this match means to so many people.”

Rangers went about the match with an intensity that Celtic struggled to equal from the off, some of their players looking distinctly overawed by the occasion. The former England goalkeeper Sam Johnstone was among them, flapping at two early openings, but he could do nothing about the opening goal when it arrived in the 22nd minute. After a Celtic counter broke down Rangers immediately turned play around with a long ball to the Celtic area where Cameron Carter‑Vickers failed to properly clear. Kelsy picked up the loose ball, slipped it to Neil and the captain, signed on a free transfer from Sunderland in the summer, placed an excellent shot just inside Johnstone’s left‑hand post.

After seizing the advantage, Rangers went on to dominate the second half and a second goal appeared inevitable. It duly arrived when a free-kick from the impressive James Penrice was flicked on by Ryan Naderi to the back post where Kelsy clipped his effort around the keeper and inside the left-hand post.

View image in fullscreen Kevin Kelsy lashes in Rangers’ second goal around the hour. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

Neil then took matters into his own hands with a quarter of an hour remaining as he controlled a loose ball on the edge of the Celtic area and wrapped a shot into the top corner to unleash delirium in the Copland Stand. “I haven’t scored many goals in my career, so to come away with a brace is immense,” Neil said.

It was perhaps just as well for O’Neill that his supporters had been denied access to this match. Celtic began with a calmness that suggested confidence. Ultimately it was more likely to have reflected timidity. The Bhoys were unable to get a foot on the ball at all in the second half, and the big-money signing Kasper Høgh looked lost at the tip of the Celtic attack before he was substituted on 65 minutes.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“We were well beaten in the end, on the day we were second best,” O’Neill said. “There has to be a realisation how big this game is, it’s still one of the great fixtures in European football if not the world. We’ve got to know that. We have to learn from it. Hopefully it’s a wake‑up call.”

Rangers will play Aberdeen in the semi-finals, but McInnes was still being asked about Rangers’ stuttering start to the season after this match, generating the timeless response: “Why are you pissing on my chips?”

After this result the Rangers manager can at least look forward with optimism and he could be set to unleash the spirit of Ian Ferguson again as early as next weekend when a second Old Firm derby awaits, this time at Celtic Park.

Sports.title: European football: Lamine Yamal keeps Barcelona perfect, Leipzig rout Hamburg
Sports.content:
Barcelona continued their perfect start to the ⁠season with a hard-fought 4-2 La Liga victory over Levante in Valencia ⁠on Sunday.

Levante ⁠found ​themselves two goals down within 19 minutes after swift play from ⁠Barcelona led to goals for Xavi Espart and Lamine Yamal. The home side ⁠then rallied, finishing the half with six ​shots to Barcelona’s ‌three.

Just 42 ‌seconds into the second half, Barcelona were awarded ‌a penalty, won and converted by Lamine Yamal. The 19-year-old now has three doubles in his past three La Liga matches.

An errant pass from Espart allowed Levante forward Iván Romero ‌to round goalkeeper Joan García and pass the ball into the net ​with 12 minutes to go. With two minutes remaining, Roger Brugue burst through multiple Barcelona challenges to score a second for Levante.

The ⁠home side’s hopes of a draw were definitively ​ended ​by a mazy run ​and finish from Karim Adeyemi ​in the ‌93rd minute.

Barcelona ​are alone ​at the top of the table with five wins from five, three points ahead of Real Madrid.

RB Leipzig bounced back from their Champions League defeat at Como by thumping strugglers Hamburg 5-0 at home in the Bundesliga on Sunday.

Norway winger Antonio Nusa was the best of the bunch for the hosts, scoring one goal and setting up two more, including one for Christopher Nkunku, the French winger’s first since returning to Leipzig in August.

Tidiam Gomis, Willi Orban and Romulo also got on the scoresheet for Leipzig, who climbed to fourth with the victory.

“It’s easy to look into the past too much. You lost two games. It’s difficult, but you have to look forward,” Nusa said.

“Today we had to perform and we did, so I think we had a good balance of not thinking too much of the past, but trying to attack today and I think we did it.”

Hamburg’s third big defeat in their third league match this campaign leaves the six-time German champions in bottom spot in the table.

Later on Sunday in Spain, Getafe host Deportivo A Coruña before Atlético Madrid visit Real Sociedad.

In the big Bundesliga game, unbeaten Bayern Munich travel to promoted Elversberg, who have won their first two matches. In Italy, Napoli host Bologna, while Juventus are at Sassuolo. Paris Saint-Germain – with just two points from their first three games – will try to kickstart their Ligue 1 campaign at Brest.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta says penalty given to Sunderland ‘unacceptable at this level’
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta’s delight at Arsenal’s latest win was tempered by his fury with the referee John Brooks as the champions triumphed 2-0 at Sunderland on Saturday night.

Before Bruno Guimarães gave Arsenal the lead in a tight match that Régis Le Bris’s team were arguably unlucky to lose, David Raya made a brilliant save to deny Enzo Le Fée from the penalty spot. Arteta, however, did not believe that Ezri Konsa had hauled Dan Ballard to the ground, instead blaming the Sunderland man for pulling down his opponent.

“We had to overcome a really tough opponent in a difficult place,” said Arsenal’s manager. “Sunderland can suffocate you and they decided to be really physical and very direct and we also had to overcome a situation that, in my opinion was unacceptable at this level.

“I’m very worried and sad because this can never be a penalty. It’s a judo roll from the opponent. Ezri does nothing. We have to take responsibility to protect the game. Today the game was unprotected and it could have cost us the win and our momentum. I’m really sad. It should never have happened.”

Arteta, who was booked in the first half for persistently stepping out of his technical area, hailed Guimarães’s goal as “beautiful” after watching Bukayo Saka scored a second goal from the penalty spot in stoppage time, when Sunderland’s Reinildo was sent off for a second bookable offence.

Le Bris was left with mixed feelings. “I’m proud and disappointed, these are the two words that are in my mind at the minute,” said Sunderland’s manager. “I’m proud because I think we showed that we are really close to achieving something big against one of the best teams in Europe right now. After the first half we were a bit reserved with the ball I think, but our second half was excellent.

“We got the momentum, created chances and it was a big save from Raya from the penalty. I think it was very good goalkeeping rather than a poor penalty. Raya was absolutely impressive today.

“We stayed in the game and we created other chances but we didn’t score and that was the difference today.

Sports.title: From the moment stupid Phil Foden was sent off, there was only one team playing smart, cute football... and it wasn't Man United, who fell straight into City's trap, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
Manchester City have inflicted a few embarrassments on their neighbours in modern times and now they have done it again. Another big day out at Old Trafford. Another victory. Another song to sing.

The cast may be different but the story remains the same. City blue looking at United red in the rear-view mirror.

This was a victory that had controversy written right through it.

Phil Foden was sent off for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes in only the 23rd minute. Foden was provoked by a sly Fernandes kick that itself warranted some kind of punishment that never came. But the City player was stupid and reckless. He had to go.

As for the winning goal – poked in at the far post midway through the second half by Erling Haaland – it is hard to work out why it was allowed to stand. Initially ruled out by a linesman, the decision was overturned by VAR.

Enzo Fernandez – chief City pest all day – didn’t make contact with the ball as it passed in front of him on the six-yard line. But he clearly tried to and – given that he was a yard offside – that should have been enough to see the initial decision confirmed.

Man City beat Man United 1-0 at Old Trafford despite being reduced to 10 men in the first half

Erling Haaland scored the winner despite the fact his goal caused significant controversy

He was originally called offside before VAR intervened, but Enzo Fernandez (No 17) was in an offside position and appeared to interfere with play

Why wasn’t it? Suffice to say, we will have to wait until Howard Webb next stands in front of a TV camera to find out.

So United have reason to feel aggrieved and doubtless they will. But the fact remains that from the moment Foden walked in the first half, there was only one team playing smart, cute football and it wasn’t Michael Carrick’s team.

United hit the post twice from distance – Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – while Gianluigi Donnarumma made perhaps the save of the season to deny Bryan Mbeumo in the fourth minute of five added. No wonder his team-mates ran to the big Italian at the end. Donnarumma has had a difficult time of late but this was a reminder of his star quality.

But where City were clever and intelligent and in control as they drew the sting and the energy out of United, their opponents were suckered in to playing a game that didn’t suit them.

In the City midfield, Fernandez was a defining influence and is destined to become a hero in that part of town. Meanwhile, Elliot Anderson schooled United’s Kobbie Mainoo in a way that shows just why he plays for England and his opponent doesn’t.

England manager Thomas Tuchel was here to see this ahead of naming a squad on Friday but you didn’t have to have a trained eye to see the trail of quality Anderson left across this football pitch. United tried to sign him, too. Ouch.

At the end City’s joy was unconfined. New manager Enzo Maresca was off down the touchline like a bunny. It wasn’t quite full Jose Mourinho but it had all the same vibes. With Arsenal setting a furious pace at the top of the league, City cannot afford to lose many. As such, this was a big result for reasons above and beyond those that involve the mood that the people of Manchester take in to work with them the next morning.

From the start, it had felt like a big afternoon for both clubs. But then when isn’t it when the derby rolls around? For all the fakery and false narratives imposed upon us by the Premier League’s corporate machine these days, this is a rivalry that remains very real.

City are only a few games into Maresca’s evolution while United remain a curious mix of optimism and self-harm. The four goals Carrick’s team had scored in the Champions League last Thursday will have helped their self-esteem. But this was different. It was a real opponent.

Maresca rolled his dice in terms of his attacking line up and had clearly instructed his players to get on the front foot. It was an approach that had served them well here before but was one that was tempered once Foden made that long diagonal walk across the Old Trafford turf and off down its famous corner tunnel.

It was a shame to see him go. Not only because Foden’s gradual re-emergence had slowly gathered pace this autumn but also because it changed the feel of the game. The opening quarter of the game had felt like a street fight. Not pretty but intense and adrenaline-charged. The sending off took some of the juice out of that as City dropped in to a shape and invited United to unlock them.

That wasn’t always going to suit the home team, as strange as it sounds. They remain a side most dangerous on the counter attack and had shown signs of that early on here, particularly when Rashford was invited to stretch City down United’s left flank.

With a man over and the scale of City’s ambition changing, United were asked to play in a way that does not altogether suit them.

Phil Foden was sent off after he kicked out at Bruno Fernandes having been fouled by him

This was a huge victory for Enzo Maresca as he made it four wins from four in the league so far

But this was a difficult day for Michael Carrick, whose side did nowhere near enough after Foden's dismissal

Earlier, it had been fractious. Twice in the opening two minutes, United players came crashing in to their opponents. First Diogo Dalot brought down Anderson and then Harry Maguire went through the dangerous Rayan Cherki.

It was not a one-way street for City, though. Over time and before the red card, United took a foothold. Rashford was always the main outlet but Fernandes was creative too. One chipped through pass had United roars in throats only for the recipient found to be Dalot, who could not control.

Haaland was quiet. He often is. Indeed for the first fifteen minutes he didn’t touch the ball. But then a Fernandes mistake invited him to charge through the middle and his pass towards Cherki on the right would have opened up had Lisandro Martinez not made an important interception.

Even before Foden departed, City struggled to control the rhythms and tempo of the game the way they often did here in the Pep Guardiola years. That said much for the way United had lifted their levels after last weekend’s disappointing draw at Everton. They looked at times like a team ready to take a big step forward. Sadly for them, that feel wasn’t to last.

Either side of the half-time break, Carrick’s team struck a post from distance. First Rashford did so from a 25-yard free-kick and then, in the 50th minute, Mainoo did likewise after running on to the ball in a central position just outside the penalty area at the Stretford End.

Rashford then drilled an effort in to the side netting with his left foot before Matheus Cunha drove over from the other side. As the hour mark approached, United were beginning to run hot. Maresca had replaced Cherki with Iliman Ndiaye at half-time but that had done nothing for his team at this juncture.

It felt as if a goal would come and soon it did. Incredibly, it was at the other end. Haaland had done nothing all day but his finish to Josko Gvardiol’s far post cross was superb. Haaland looked offside but wasn’t. Fernandez – diving at the ball as it came across - looked offside and was. Even so, City had an unlikely and rather confusing lead that would have been doubled had United goalkeeper Senne Lammens not touched Fernandez's low shot on to the inside of the post with his fingertips.

For United embarrassment beckoned and the tale of the game was to be found in the statistics. Despite their domination of ball and territory and despite two strikes against woodwork, it took them 50 minutes following Foden’s dismissal to register a shot on target. As we entered the last 15 minutes, they had to find something.

Instead, Haaland almost poked in a low Fernandes free-kick at the far post as the United back four wobbled again.

City, frankly, were proving themselves to be cleverer than their opponents. Now that United had to chase it, City drew fouls and wasted time. As they did so, United’s frustration grew.

Kobbie Mainoo struggled against counterpart Elliot Anderson, who was exceptional for City

Fernandez (No 17) was also a defining influence and managed to wind up United's players

Fernandez seemed to be at the heart of most of it but United should have risen above it and didn’t. They fell right into the City trap.

Bryan Mbeumo and Maguire both drifted headers wide as time wore on. There was no kitchen sink thrown though. There was no onslaught. It all felt a bit forlorn and hopeful.

Mbeumo’s chance at the death came on the back of an isolated moment of football intelligence.

Against any modern City side – old or new – you have to find something a bit better than that.

Sports.title: More gloom and misery for Frank Lampard as Coventry's pointless - and goalless - start to the season leaves them rock bottom as Brighton run out 5-0 winners
Sports.content:
More gloom and misery for Frank Lampard as Coventry's pointless - and goalless - start to the season leaves them rock bottom as Brighton run out 5-0 winners

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

More misery for Frank Lampard. More gloom. More concern.

Coventry's pointless – and goalless – start to the season extended to four Premier League games and left them rock bottom.

This was a stuffing by a free-scoring Brighton side who had five different players on the scoresheet and ran out easy winners.

Lampard's men showed fight and created some decent first-half opportunities and that should not be overlooked.

Yet classy strikes from Charalampos Kostoulas, Malick Yalcouye, Lewis Dunk and Yasin Ayari, and a Pascal Gross penalty, underlined the Seagulls' superiority.

Coventry had Taiwo Awoniyi deservedly sent off early in the second half and Brighton, already 2-0 up, took them to the cleaners.

There was more gloom and misery for Frank Lampard as their pointless - and goalless - start to the season rumbled on

Lampard agony continues

When Lampard guided Coventry to promotion as Championship title winners last term, romance in the game breathed.

Here was one of the greatest players of his generation returning one of English football's traditional old clubs back to the big time after a traumatic 25-year absence.

Lampard rates the success as the finest achievement of a managerial career which has not always reached the heights he hit as a player.

The greater challenge, of course, will be keeping the Midlands outfit in the big time.

The 48-year-old spent £130million in the summer but the effects of that lavish spree have yet to be felt.

On this evidence, Coventry's survival chances are slipping and wealthy owner Doug King watched on from the stands here.

That Hull and Ipswich already have two wins apiece will merely add to his concerns.

But Sky Blues fans sang their hearts out until the death here and Lampard will need that support if he is to turn the situation around.

Coventry cannot score

Brighton, typically, popped the ball around with a swagger early on but Coventry gradually steadied themselves and fashioned some decent opportunities.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS COVENTRY (3-4-2-1): Rushworth 6; Amenda 6, Thomas 5.5, Pinnock 6; van Ewijk 6, Onyeka 6 (Yirenkyi 73, 6), Grimes 6 (Torp 84), Dasilva 6.5; Rudoni 6.5 (Thomas-Asante 73, 6), Mason-Clark 6 (Cherif 60, 6); Awoniyi 5.5 Sent off: Awoniyi 53 Manager: Frank Lampard 5.5 BRIGHTON (4-2-3-1): VERBRUGGEN 8, Kadioglu 6, Vuskovic 6 (Struijk 78), Dunk 7.5, Boscagli 6 (Osman 78); Gross 7, Ayari 7; Gomez 6.5 (Costinha 84), Yalcouye 7 (Chema Andres 65, 6), Du Cuyper 6.5; Kostoulas 7.5 (O'Riley 84) Scorers: Kostoulas 35, Yalcouyé 51, Gross 70 (pen), Dunk 83, Ayari 90 Manager: Fabian Hurzeler 7.5 Referee: Tony Harrington 6.5 Attendance: 31,492

Jay Dasilva was a threat on the left flank and his dangerous cross was met by Jack Rudoni, whose right-foot volley drew the best of Bart Verbruggen's saves.

Brighton's goalkeeper earned the player of the match honours and his side hit Coventry with a vicious sucker-punch in the 39th minute.

Kostoulas showed delightful skill to create the space to drive a low, right-foot shot past Carl Rushworth.

Lampard said: 'We created chances but didn't take them and then we're one-nil down from a moment of quality – welcome to the Premier League.

'Their second goal was the most disappointing because it was a mistake from us and then the red card, at 2-0, makes it very difficult.

'We need to be more clinical to give ourselves a chance in this league and we need to be honest about that. This wasn't a nice feeling.'

Six minutes into the second half, Yalcouye raced behind a leaden-footed defence to coolly slot home the Seagulls' second.

Awoniyi, a £9million summer signing from Nottingham Forest, then saw red for elbowing Maxim De Cuyper and Lampard had no issues with the decision.

The game was already up for his men but Gross added a third from the spot after Bobby Thomas felled Kostoulas.

Remarkably, centre-half and captain Dunk scored with a stupendous 35-yard shot which flew into Rushworth's top corner before Ayari's neat curling effort late on.

Seagulls score again

Lewis Dunk scored the pick of the goals as Brighton became the division's top goalscorers

Having thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 on the opening day, this latest crushing victory maintained Brighton's impressive start to the season.

It remains early days, but Hurzeler's side appear set fair for another year of progress.

It was all too easy in the end but 13 goals from their opening four games makes them the Premier League's current top goalscorers.

Hurzeler said: 'I wouldn't say it was a complete performance, but our goalkeeper was great and we were ruthless in front of goal.

'If you have that desire to score then you can do it from different positions.

'I wasn't surprised by Lewis' goal because he has a great right foot and shows that technique on a daily basis in training.'

Brighton finished eighth last season to qualify for the Europa Conference League and next up is a trip to Manchester United in the Carabao Cup and a home clash with Arsenal.

Hurzeler added: 'We should stay very humble but also have a belief that we can go anywhere and compete.'

Sports.title: Furious Mikel Arteta is beginning to sound a lot like Sir Alex Ferguson after his latest referee outburst - but this is why it could backfire for Arsenal
Sports.content:
Furious Mikel Arteta is beginning to sound a lot like Sir Alex Ferguson after his latest referee outburst - but this is why it could backfire for Arsenal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Three points secured on a gritty night away in Sunderland.

After what happened here last time out for Arsenal in November, Brian Brobbey’s injury-time equaliser halting a five-game winning run, many assumed Mikel Arteta would be chuffed afterwards.

It’s now five wins in a row and, just as crucially, a show of defiance in many ways. Bruno Guimaraes’ stunning strike – including a cupped ear celebration to a club who detest him from his Newcastle days – and David Raya’s world-class save to deny Enzo Le Fee’s spot-kick both typified this.

Yet, Arteta strode into the post-match press conference with steam coming from his ears.

I opened proceedings, asking about John Brooks’ controversial decision to award the Black Cats a penalty on 54 minutes.

Ezri Konsa, who had a tough night at the hands of many wrestling jousts with Brobbey, was embroiled in another such battle – this time with Dan Ballard.

Mikel Arteta was incensed despite Arsenal earning a hard fought 2-0 victory over Sunderland

Arteta claimed the decision to award Sunderland a penalty was 'not acceptable' and compared Dan Ballard's action to a 'judo roll'

David Raya saved the resulting penalty but Arteta hit out at the awarding of the spot-kick post match

Both had hold of each other’s shirts in the area as the ball arrived, Ballard falling to the deck. Brooks’ call for a penalty was very soft, incorrect even, the pair each culpable for the holding.

Le Fee stepped up to take the resulting penalty, which Raya sprang at full stretch to tip onto the right-hand post.

The memory of that save went out of the window initially for Arteta, though, incensed over the decision.

‘(What) we have to go through today in my opinion is not acceptable,’ Arteta fumed.

‘I watched it 20 times, and I cannot find a way to understand how we even think to give a penalty.

'But I'm sad that we have to discuss in such a beautiful game something at this level that has the gravity to change the course of the season, and it can cost you the championship.

'It's a judo roll.’

It was Newcastle away all over again, that night in November 2023 springing to mind. On that occasion, Mikel Arteta described the decision to award Anthony Gordon’s winning goal against Arsenal as ‘disgraceful’ and ‘embarrassing’.

Arteta wants to make sure that the refereeing fraternity are aware that any major decisions which, in his eyes, go incorrectly against Arsenal will be called out

His comments post-match sounded a lot like legendary Man United boss Sir Alex Ferguson

While Arteta was right to be aggrieved over the decision, but needs to be careful as such forthrightness could go against Arsenal if he is seen to be putting undue pressure on referees

Again, walking into the room, the Spaniard was full of anger and you had a sense of the tirade he was about to unfurl.

Rewinding back to Arsenal’s last-gasp escape against West Ham at the end of last season, where the VAR overturned Callum Wilson’s equaliser, Arteta had said he now ‘realised how difficult and how big the referee’s job is’.

He had forgotten about this when it came to Brooks’ judgement. There was an element of Sir Alex Ferguson about his words. Winning wasn’t enough. He wants to make sure that the refereeing fraternity are aware that any major decisions which, in his eyes, go incorrectly against Arsenal will be called out.

A further line channelled his inner Ferguson.

‘I cannot find an explanation, honestly. That's why I'm going to try to find an explanation now,’ he said.

The Spaniard was right to be aggrieved over the decision, but needs to be careful. Such forthrightness could go against Arsenal if he is deemed to be putting undue pressure on referees.

On the other side, it also showed the wider mindset at Arsenal. Having tasted a first league title in 22 years, and experiencing such a tight finish last time round, Arteta and Arsenal are not leaving anything to chance.

They know how tight the margins are and want to get ahead of the curve. Making a point about refereeing decisions now is a psychological marker. That can have an effect in the months to come when a tight, game-changing call arises. Every point counts at this level.

On this decision, Arteta was right, Brooks’s call harsh because of the level of contact Ballard and Konsa had placed on each other.

Arsenal, though, do like to get physical in the area so need to be careful themselves going forward.

It remains to be seen what level of restraint Arteta can keep going forward, for he’s on a tightrope.

Sports.title: Man United 0-1 Man City PLAYER RATINGS: Who was given just 4.5/10 and offered no threat? Now have YOUR say after chaotic derby at Old Trafford
Sports.content:
Man United 0-1 Man City PLAYER RATINGS: Who was given just 4.5/10 and offered no threat? Now have YOUR say after chaotic derby at Old Trafford

The first Manchester derby of the season dramatic and then some, with City toppling arch rivals United 1-0 in a game of controversy.

Phil Foden was sent off in the first-half after kicking out at United captain Bruno Fernandes, despite the Red Devils star seemingly kicking his opponent too.

But the drama wasn't done there. As United struggled against the ten men of City, Erling Haaland put the visitors ahead in the second-half, only for it to be ruled offside on-field.

After a VAR check, Haaland was adjudged to be onside, though the role of Enzo Fernandez, who rushed towards the ball from an offside position, seemingly wasn't taken into consideration.

City saw out the game to earn a vital win, but debate will rage on about the key decisions made in the game.

Daily Mail Sport's CHRIS WHEELER and JACK GAUGHAN were at Old Trafford to rate the players.

Two key decisions dominated the Manchester derby, including the allowing of Erling Haaland's winning goal

Phil Foden was also sent off for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes, though it had appeared that the United captain had kicked Foden too

Manchester United (4-2-3-1)

SENNE LAMMENS - 6

About the first thing he had to do was pick the ball out of his net after an hour. Smart save to turn Fernandez’s shot against the post.

DIOGO DALOT – 6.5

Almost got caught napping by Semenyo when he tried to shepherd the ball out in the first-half, but otherwise handled the City winger well.

HARRY MAGUIRE -6

Had Haaland under his thumb until the goal. Just shows you can’t switch off against City’s goal machine. Booked for a silly shove on Fernandez.

LISANDRO MARTINEZ - 6

Did well to snuff out an isolated Haaland run early on. Inevitably got involved when it all kicked off over Foden.

PATRICK DORGU - 6

Deputised for Luke Shaw and marked Cherki and Ndiaye well, but out of position when he played Haaland onside for the goal.

YOURI TIELEMANS - 6.5

Picked some nice passes but had a lot less time on the ball than he did in Europe on Thursday, and was the first United player replaced.

KOBBIE MAINOO - 7

Another energetic display from him, and almost crowned it with a goal when he rattled the post in the second-half.

BRYAN MBEUMO – 4.5

Scored in United’s last two league games, but offered little threat and missed a glaring chance to equalise in the dying seconds.

BRUNO FERNANDES – 5.5

Main contribution was the red card flashpoint when he was lucky not to be booked – and maybe worse – for a dig at Foden which drew the retaliation.

MARCUS RASHFORD - 7

Tends to come alive for the derby and this was no different. United’s brightest player and hit the post with a free-kick.

MATHEUS CUNHA - 5

Picked as a false nine ahead of Sesko but didn’t offer enough. Dropped too deep too often, and had just one decent effort on goal.

Subs

Benjamin Sesko (for Tielemans 67) – 6

Joshua Zirkzee (for Rashford 82)

Head coach: Michael Carrick - 5

Began his spell as United head coach with a win in this fixture, but failed to capitalise on the red card and City’s ten men were too comfortable.

Bryan Mbeumo missed a golden opportunity to equalise for United right at the death

Manchester City (4-2-3-1)

GIANLUIGI DONNARUMMA – 8

Stunning stoppage time save from Mbeumo preserved the points. Top sweeping up when Fernandes released Rashford too.

MATHEUS NUNES - 8

A first Premier League start of the season and really composed up against Rashford. More reliable than ever.

MARC GUEHI – 8.5

His finest week in a City shirt after performances at Porto and now Old Trafford. Imperious display, calmness personified.

RUBEN DIAS - 7

Organised well. Strong work on the cover a few times. Looked cleaner in possession than in previous weeks.

JOSKO GVARDIOL - 7

Mbeumo barely earned a mention until very late on and for that Gvardiol deserves huge credit.

ELLIOT ANDERSON – 8

Had to man the fort alone quite a lot of the time and did so with his usual energy. Action man was everywhere again.

ENZO FERNANDEZ – 8

Grew into the game, especially after Erling Haaland’s opener. Very good game management and hit the post.

PHIL FODEN – 3

Whether the force warranted a red card or not, Foden’s petulance at kicking Fernandes let his team down.

RAYAN CHERKI – 6

A few nice touches before the sending off but couldn’t get into the game thereafter. Sacrificed at half-time.

Erling Haaland (left) woke up after his goal, while Gianluigi Donnarumma (centre) produced a stunning stoppage time save

ANTOINE SEMENYO – 6.5

Some of his best work was in the wrong direction and put in a shift down the left-hand side. Always a lingering threat too.

Woke up after his goal. Suddenly burst into life. Top finish and then became far more of a focal point.

Sports.title: Furious Man United fans tell club 'the way you treat us is a disgrace': Supporters unveil protest banner ahead of Manchester derby amid huge protests in front of onlooking Sir Jim Ratcliffe at Old Trafford
Sports.content:
Manchester United fans have displayed a solitary banner in the Stretford End at Sunday's Old Trafford derby branding the club a 'disgrace'.

The Red Army opted not to have any other flags or banners at the game against Manchester City in protest over 'the recent behaviour of the club'.

Fans group The 1958 staged a demonstration before the game over United's clampdown on ticket touts, which they claim has targeted innocent supporters.

The TRA, who organise and pay for the flags and banners in the Stretford End, issued a statement on Saturday explaining their actions.

It read: 'On Sunday there will be no flag display on the Stretford End. In its place, a single banner will hang above the players' tunnel with a clear message to the owners, directors and decision-making staff at Manchester United: 'The Way You Treat Us is a Disgrace'.

'This isn't a TRA message, it's a message on behalf of every genuine fan group, match-going supporter, supporters' club and fan representative who has either contacted us directly or been negatively impacted by the recent behaviour of the club.

Manchester United fans have displayed a solitary banner in the Stretford End at Sunday's Old Trafford derby branding the club a 'disgrace'

Sir Jim Ratcliffe was watching on amid huge protests from home supporters

Fans group The 1958 staged a demonstration before the game over United's clampdown on ticket touts, which they claim has targeted innocent supporters

The Red Army opted not to have any other flags or banners at the game against Manchester City in protest over 'the recent behaviour of the club'

'It's an honest, heartfelt cry for recognition from the maligned, vilified, and misrepresented beating heart of our football club – the generational match-going supporters.

'Neither is this solely a Manchester United problem, this is a league-wide crisis that should be addressed at every club, regardless of rivalries and history. Without drastic changes, there will be no rivalries in the future vision for football shared by the decision makers.

'Whilst we still advocate for a change in ownership, we believe that there should be a realistic roadmap for any protest if it is to act as a catalyst for change.

'Unless our generational match-going support is given a real voice that is actually listened to, the little that remains of our fan culture will soon be gone forever.

'TRA aren't a protest group, we're an 'atmosphere' group but we've never shied away from making our position clear when we believe not doing so would be to the detriment of the interests of match-going supporters.

'We hope that you'll understand and support our decision and that those of you who are asking for meaningful change and are able to help will stand up and be counted when called upon in the near future.

'Until then, we'll continue to fully back and support the players and manager throughout, starting with the derby on Sunday.'

United revealed the outcome of their ticket tout investigation on Friday, saying that a total of 685 suspicious accounts have been hit with bans for breaching season-ticket rules.

The club claim to have broken up large-scale organised networks involved in touting and denied that innocent fans have been targeted, adding that some examples of unfair treatment of supporters shared on social media are untrue and don't tell the full story.

Sports.title: Gareth Southgate set to launch new podcast starring his old England favourite, no love lost between EFL and Southampton after Spygate - and toilet roll troubles continue at Man United's Leigh Sports Village: INSIDE SPORT
Sports.content:
In November, Inside Sport noted how reporters covering Manchester United’s women side when they play at the Leigh Sports Village had taken to bringing their own toilet roll to games thanks to a lack of the product at the council-operated facility.

United have long denied claims of a lack of investment in their women’s team but the noise refuses to go away following the departure of head coach Marc Skinner.

On Sunday, it got louder when they made it back-back losses to open the campaign escaping a lop-sided home clash with Chelsea with a 5-0 pasting while, up in the press box, there was again no loo roll.

Spygate tensions rumble on

As they await the Spygate verdict from the FA, there would appear to be no love lost between Southampton and the EFL. Spies inside the boardroom at Birmingham City have told Inside Sport that EFL chief Rick Parry, who was at St Andrews for the Saints' recent Championship clash, did not speak to any of the travelling delegation, preferring instead to spend the duration of his visit with Blues officials.

The apparent snub did not go unnoticed at Southampton, where there remains some upset about how the decision to throw them out of the play-offs unfolded. While the FA’s punishment remains to be seen, any further measures would no doubt add to that feeling, given the Saints have already paid the ultimate penalty.

EFL insiders say that Parry was in a different area of the boardroom and did not spot the Saints party.

EFL chief Rick Parry, who was at St Andrews for the Saints' recent Championship clash, did not speak to any of the travelling delegation, Inside Sport understands

Chakraborty hard to replace for BBC

Federation bosses are closely monitoring the BBC’s next move ahead of the Olympics following the departure of its head of major events and general sport. Ron Chakraborty is departing the broadcaster at the end of the year after more than 28 years.

He leads the Beeb’s Olympics coverage and, as a highly-respected operator, leaves big shoes to fill. ‘Ron is a great guy,’ explained one source, ‘and did a brilliant job on this year’s Winter Games. It will be interesting to see what they do for LA – producing 35 sports is not easy. There’s nothing like it.’

Some have accused the Beeb, under director of sport Alex Kay-Jelski, of showing little regard for television as it searches for a younger audience by pouring resource into digital output.

Insiders say they are confident in their succession plan, believe in the team that delivered both the summer and winter Games, which remains in place, and say additional leadership oversight will be provided. They reject any suggestion that LA coverage will be compromised given the expertise they believe remains at their disposal.

Southgate set to launch new podcast

Gareth Southgate is set to expand his media empire with a new podcast focusing on managers. Insiders say the show is set to be named The Dugout, and is expected to feature broadcaster Mark Chapman and former Everton defender Conor Coady speaking to bosses from across the game.

Southgate, along with long-time business partner Jimmy Worrall have already launched The Football Boardroom, which aims to take listeners inside the corridors of power.

EFL clubs will meet this week in their divisions to discuss key matters. Inside Sport understands that they will be briefed on the latest with regards to financial distribution, as a deal with the Premier League inches closer.

Gareth Southgate is set to expand his media empire with a new podcast focusing on managers

Russini suffers fresh blow after Vrabel scandal

It would appear that Dianna Russini, the reporter at the centre of a huge NFL scandal, has cast her final vote in the sport’s prestigious end of year awards.

Russini, 43, resigned from her role with The Athletic, in the wake of explosive allegations over her relationship with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel. She was one of 50 journalists selected to make picks in the Associated Press’s poll, holding the coveted spot since 2022.

Russini and Vrabel, who are both married with children, denied having an affair after shock pictures emerged of them together at an adults-only resort in Arizona.

However, the images, coupled with further shots which appeared to show the pair kissing in a New York City bar in 2020 led some to call on the AP to release ballots from previous polls amid concerns over integrity. They have declined to do so.

Inside Sport asked AP to clarify whether Russini would be voting this year. They stopped short of directly answering the question however, in a quote, seemed to suggest that would not be the case.

A spokesperson said simply: ‘The makeup of AP’s NFL awards voting panel changes regularly as sports reporters change positions and organizations, and this year is no different.’

Sports.title: Real Madrid take over the Spanish Grand Prix: Jude Bellingham is joined by his brother Jobe and Trent Alexander-Arnold... while Jose Mouriunho interview with Sky Sports' Martin Brundle is awkwardly cut short
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham led a cohort of Real Madrid stars in attending the Spanish Grand Prix in the capital, as he declared his support for Mercedes drivers.

Bellingham was joined by his brother Jobe – whose Borussia Dortmund team won 3-0 on Saturday – as Madrid hosted a Formula One race for the first time since 1981.

The brothers were seen in the McLaren garage ahead of the race, while they also stopped off with their rivals Mercedes.

Bellingham was seen embracing drivers' championship leader Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, with Real Madrid players and drivers exchanging signed shirts.

Fede Valverde, Vinicius Jnr, Rodrygo and Trent Alexander-Arnold were also among the current Real Madrid stars present.

The trip followed Real Madrid earning a 4-1 victory over Rayo Vallecano on Saturday night, with Bellingham among the scorers for Jose Mourinho's side.

Jude Bellingham and his brother Jobe were among the sporting stars present for the Madrid Grand Prix

The Bellingham brothers visited both McLaren and Mercedes garages ahead of the race

Jose Mourinho and Trent Alexander-Arnold were also part of a cohort from Real Madrid to attend the race after they had overcome Rayo Vallecano 4-1 on Saturday

'Good going, a good start to the season for the team, one little slip up but other than that doing pretty good,' Bellingham said when asked by Sky Sports about their start to the season.

On the Grand Prix, Bellingham added: 'I have been with Mercedes and met George and Kimi, they have been telling us about it [F1] and I have to act like I understand.

'To be honest the level those guys are operating at with the strategy and all those things is a different level.

'It is unbelievable, I am used to a PlayStation controller but these guys are whipping out things with 40 buttons.

'Credit to them and with the work they put in, they deserve everything they get.

'The thing I most admire is the poise of them all, it is really impressive.'

In a separate interview, Bellingham revealed that he typically cheers on Mercedes and British drivers during the F1 season.

Real Madrid boss Mourinho was also present having vowed only to be in attendance if his side were victorious on Saturday.

Mourinho was seen in dicussion with Spanish tennis legend Rafael Nadal at the Grand Prix

Real Madrid great Roberto Carlos spoke to Fernando Alonso in the Aston Martin garage

Mourinho's interview with Sky Sports' grid reporter Martin Brundle was abruptly halted in an awkward moment for the broadcaster.

Brundle had seconds left of his customary segment, and had to cut off the interview after just a brief exchange, when the national anthem began playing with the drivers assembled and Mourinho mid-sentence.

Mourinho was earlier collared by another Sky Sports reporter trackside where he was asked about whether Bellingham could one day be considered England's greatest player.

'Very special,' Mourinho replied. 'Not a bit special, very special.'

Mourinho, however, offered no prediction when asked about how his former club Man United and coach Michael Carrick will get on in Sunday's Manchester derby.

'He's doing well Michael, doing well, I'm happy with that,' Mourinho said.

Mourinho was also pictured in conversation with legendary Spanish tennis star Rafael Nadal at the Grand Prix.

Former Real Madrid greats Roberto Carlos and Steve McManaman were also among the sporting icons present.

Sports.title: Why Tottenham can't score a goal after £320m spending spree: Lost Mathys Tel is thinking like a playmaker, gambling on versatile wide men has backfired - and how Omar Marmoush looks the best fit to end barren start
Sports.content:
Almost an hour had passed after the final whistle on Saturday when Tottenham’s manager Roberto De Zerbi arrived to do his press conference. There is a temptation to think his side could have spent that time on the pitch and still wouldn’t have scored against a team of mannequins. He would go on to tell us about ‘blockages’, which might have applied to the Everton backline in a 0-0 draw, but in this instance involved something else – it was a discussion about the mental hurdles his forward players are facing in front of goal. In short, he said they lack confidence. Overthinking has crept in. The weight of recent history is pressing them down and, like a golfer with the yips, they find themselves unable to pull the trigger. The wait for a Tottenham goal in the league now measures in excess of six hours, dating back to the 43rd minute of the final game of last season against Everton. Palhinha could be the answer to a quiz question at this point. That they have drawn blanks in all four Premier League fixtures this season is a club record and sits horrendously against the backdrop of summer spending to the tune of around £320million. One bookmaker’s social media account had a little play with those figures of £320million and six hours and came up with a decent gag: ‘You could make and watch Titanic twice for that.’ De Zerbi and Spurs fans won’t necessarily appreciate their role in yet another punchline. Roberto De Zerbi suggested his Tottenham side had mental hurdles to overcome after a fourth match without scoring What are his options? Therein lies the problem – De Zerbi doesn’t have many, or possibly any of top-half calibre, if that remains an aspiration. During a record-breaking transfer window, Spurs brought in three wingers, a left back, three centre-backs, two midfielders and a back-up goalkeeper. With Richarlison tucked away in exile, that left Dominic Solanke as the only fully-designated senior striker. Solanke, for some context, hasn’t scored in the league since March and was utterly anonymous on Saturday – 19 touches, no shots. Tottenham’s recruitment has instead gambled on the versatility of men better suited to wide positions. One of those is Omar Marmoush, who started on left wing against Everton having played up front against Nottingham Forest, and the other is Mathys Tel. He replaced Solanke after an hour and clearly irritated De Zerbi by turning backwards too often rather than towards goal. Dominic Solanke has not scored in the league since March and was anonymous on Saturday Is Marmoush the solution longer term? That feels like the best fit for the way De Zerbi wants to play, which is currently wedded to positional fluidity and fewer fixed points in the team. The notion is that his striker can wander to deeper spots, sucking in the marker and then attacking the space with a wide man or No10. Those interchanges were a feature of Saturday’s game all over the pitch – Archie Gray and Savio occasionally swapped spots when Gray overlapped on the right, Andy Robertson and Marmoush would do likewise on the left, and Marmoush would often change with Solanke. At its best, it can work and its worst, it is a watery mess – at the weekend and against Nottingham Forest, it was the latter. But Marmoush’s mobility lends itself to this brief. We saw in Germany that he can finish and his chances to replicate the numbers at Manchester City were stymied by the presence of Erling Haaland. Solanke has suffered injuries for the past 18 months, but he has not looked close to the reliable finisher he was at Bournemouth in the 2023-24 campaign. More pertinently, Solanke also looks less comfortable than Marmoush when he is asked to drop into deeper positions to satisfy De Zerbi’s grand vision. With so many other left wingers in the squad, including Savio, who played off the right on Saturday, there would be no direct consequence to moving Marmoush forward. Omar Marmoush looks better suited to De Zerbi's plans and can operate in deeper positions The deeper problem… Call it the Tottenham paradox. They have an assortment of attacking options but are creating very little – the issue runs deeper than finishing, because you can only finish what you create. In the past two games, Tottenham have had one meaningful shot on target, and that came close to the end against Everton when Jordan Pickford had to save from Lucas Bergvall. Savio can terrify defences with his acceleration, which he showed early against Vitalii Mykolenko, whom he skinned twice. But his deliveries and decision making with the final ball were poor and far below the expectation of a £75m signing. When Mykolenko found his bearings in that duel, Savio found no way to adapt and lost himself down blind alleys. He became irrelevant to the match. Mateus Fernandes cost £10m more than Savio and has been slow to suggest it was well spent. He is aggressively minded and can be fun to watch at full speed, but his four touches to control a ball when clean through in the first half was a calamitous waste of a good chance. It wasn’t isolated – he needs to be decisive, especially as the most expensive recruit of the bunch, Sandro Tonali, is drifting through games. Does Tonali even want to be there? The Tel episode was interesting, because De Zerbi was right to question his striking instincts. The coach believes he can play up front, on the thin basis that he has played there before (albeit with two goals from his 15 games as a striker last season), but Tel is still thinking like a playmaker. One problem related to Tel is that too many of Tottenham’s attackers do not see it as their responsibility to score the goals. Maybe that is an upshot of De Zerbi’s fluidity vision. But where is the wisdom in publicly berating a 21-year-old, as De Zerbi did on the pitch after the game? Savio can terrify defences with his acceleration but faded after an impressive start against Everton Mateus Fernandes taking four touches to control the ball when clean through was a calamitous waste of a good chance De Zerbi was right to question Mathys Tel's striking instincts, but there was a lack of wisdom shown by doing it publicly Delusion or deficiency? De Zerbi spoke passionately after the game and, predictably, believes it will all be okay in the long run. Having kept Tottenham up, he deserves some benefit of the doubt but their start to this campaign inspires little confidence. The small pockets of booing from the crowd at the whistle would suggest a crisis is not far away. However, De Zerbi was right to highlight the first 30 minutes of the match, when his side were quick on the ball and occasionally dominant. His argument is that if they could sustain that level beyond an hour, they probably win the game. Maybe, but it’s moot – they couldn’t and didn’t. It was also a thin excuse when he argued that he has had less than a fortnight with the group and legs are tired after the World Cup – these are conditions under which all teams are operating and only Fulham, Aston Villa and Coventry sit beneath Spurs. After they face Liverpool in the League Cup on Tuesday, Tottenham play Villa in the league on Saturday – if they lose there will be an escalating feeling of crisis and even fewer excuses.

Sports.title: BBC news reaction to Saffie Osborne's historic win 'chastening indication of where horseracing sits'
Sports.content:
No-one likes us. We should care. I’m guessing you felt the same way as I did as you watched the final furlong of the Betfred St Leger on Saturday.

The 250th running of the great race served us with something we had never seen before as Saffie Osborne, aboard Highwayman, became the first woman to ride the winner of a British Classic. It seemed like the biggest story in racing since Rachael Blackmore landed the 2021 Grand National aboard Minella Times.

But not everybody thought it was such headline news. Watching the BBC News on Saturday night, Osborne’s history-making triumph didn’t receive a mention - and ITV also ignored it, even though they had the pictures.

Saffie Osborne cries tears of joy as she makes history on Highwayman in 250th St Leger READ MORE :

If you were catching up with sporting events yesterday morning, you would have found it on the BBC Sport app, but it was a lot nearer the bottom than the top - and a long way beneath that absolutely massive story that Ukrainian Kate Koval is leaving Louisiana State University’s basketball team.

‌



It’s true this is less of a deal than was once the case - people have different ways of consuming content and don’t sit down in front of the evening news like they did.

But it’s also a chastening indication of where horseracing sits in the minds of those who set the news agenda - worrying at a time when our sport needs to assert its relevance.

It’s interesting to ponder what the BBC’s response would have been to a negative happening from Town Moor - an injury to a runner, or a whip ban. But I think we all know the answer to that.

View 4 Images John Hunt will be tackling charity walk for his family's foundation (Image: Hunt Family/BBC News)

‌



Support John Hunt Family Fund

On Saturday, John Hunt starts a 125-mile walk from Bushey to Bournemouth, in company with his daughter Amy and her partner Gareth Jones.

The nine-day journey, via Windsor and the New Forest, will raise funds for the Hunt Family Fund, founded to honour the lives and spirits of John’s wife Carol and their daughters Hannah and Louise.

The charity’s aim is to tackle male violence against women and empower women’s lives. If you have a good week on the horses - or even if you don’t - please search ‘justgiving’ and ‘Hunt Family Fund’ online to donate to this most worthy cause.

View 4 Images New Gambling Commission chair has never worked in gambling (Image: Getty Images)

‌



You couldn't make it up

Congratulations to Ruth Evans on her appointment as the new chair of the Gambling Commission.

Evans’ CV? Chair of Stop Scams UK, chair of the Independent Parliamentary Standards Authority, non-executive director of the Serious Fraud Office and a committee member at the General Medical Medical Council.

Has never worked in gambling or, very likely, had a bet. You couldn’t make it up.

View 4 Images Other travel agents are available (Image: jet2holidays)

‌



Poor judgement

Tripadvisor has blocked the sale of tickets to horseracing events on the grounds of animal welfare.

If the Massachusetts-based website’s judgement is that poor, I’ll look for my hotel and restaurant reviews elsewhere.

Sports.content:
Julian Alvarez left 'out' of Atletico Madrid squad as statement released on Arsenal transfer target

Julian Alvarez has been ruled out of Atletico Madrid's La Liga clash with Real Sociedad on Sunday amid links to Arsenal

View Image Julian Alvarez will miss Atletico Madrid's match against Real Sociedad through injury (Image: Getty Images)

Julian Alvarez has been omitted from Atletico Madrid's travelling squad as the La Liga side gear up for Sunday night's clash with Real Sociedad. The club moved quickly to stress that his absence is purely injury‑related, distancing it from any remaining tension after a long, Arsenal‑shadowed summer transfer saga.

‌



When announcing their squad for the 8pm kick‑off at the Reale Arena, Atleti confirmed via social media: "Julian will not travel to San Sebastian due to a muscle overload that led to his withdrawal from yesterday's training session. After conducting the relevant tests, the medical services have ruled out his participation in today's match."

‌



Transfer insider Fabrizio Romano had earlier reported: "Julian Alvarez, out for Atletico Madrid today and not even travelling with the squad."

‌



Diego Simeone makes honest Julian Alvarez admission ahead of Liverpool clash READ MORE :

Julian Alvarez 'suffering' after failed Arsenal transfer as statement made before Liverpool READ MORE :

The news comes amid a turbulent return to La Liga for Alvarez, following a lengthy transfer saga that dragged on for the best part of two months, with both Barcelona and Arsenal circling. The Gunners made no secret of their desire to land the 26-year-old as a marquee signing, as they look to defend the Premier League title they won in May.

Barcelona had also thrown their hat into the ring for the Argentine, but Arsenal received a significant boost in their pursuit when Atleti flatly refused to sell Alvarez to their domestic rivals.

Despite their utmost efforts, Mikel Arteta and the Arsenal board fell short of securing a deal for the striker, with the club opting to begin the campaign with Kai Havertz shouldering the bulk of their attacking responsibilities.

‌



That outcome has ultimately worked in the club's favour, as they have made a flawless start to 2026/27, claiming wins in all four of their opening fixtures.
